abomasum, also known as the maw, [Abomasitis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abomasitis) is a relatively rare, but serious, disease of the abomasum whose causes are currently unknown.

Abscission () is the shedding of various parts of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism), such as a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) dropping a [leaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf), [fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit), [flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower), or [seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed).

acromioclavicular joint, or AC joint, is a [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) at the top of the [shoulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder).

adductor canal (also known as the subsartorial canal or Hunter's canal) is an [aponeurotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aponeurosis) tunnel in the middle third of the [thigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thigh) giving passage to parts of the [femoral artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femoral_artery), [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femoral_vein), and [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femoral_nerve).

adductor hiatus also known as hiatus magnus is a [hiatus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hiatus_(anatomy)) (gap) between the [adductor magnus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adductor_magnus) muscle and the [femur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femur) that allows the passage of the femoral vessels from the anterior thigh to the posterior thigh and then the [popliteal fossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_fossa).

adherens junctions (or zonula adherens, intermediate junction, or ==Models== Adherens junctions were, for many years, thought to share the characteristic of [anchor cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anchor_cell)s through their cytoplasmic [actin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actin) filaments.
adipose eyelid is a transparent [eyelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelid) found in some species of [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish), that covers some or all of the eye.
adnation is the fusion of two or more [whorls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whorl_(botany)) of a [flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower), e.g.

adrenal glands (also known as suprarenal glands) are [endocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_gland)s that produce a variety of hormones including [adrenaline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrenaline) and the steroids [aldosterone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aldosterone) and [cortisol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortisol).

aecium (plural aecia) is a specialised reproductive structure found in some plant pathogenic [rust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(fungus)) fungi that produce [aeciospore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeciospore)s.

aedeagus ( or In some [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s, sperm is not passed to the female as liquid with free-swimming [spermatozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatozoa), but as capsules called [spermatophore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatophore)s in which the actual spermatozoa are enclosed.
Aesthetes are organs in [chiton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiton)s, derived from the [mantle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mantle_(mollusc)) of the organism.

agaric () is a type of [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) [fruiting body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporocarp_(fungi)) characterized by the presence of a [pileus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pileus_(mycology)) (cap) that is clearly differentiated from the [stipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stipe_(mycology)) (stalk), with [lamellae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamellae_(mycology)) (gills) on the underside of the pileus.
Air sacs are spaces within an organism where there is the constant presence of air.

definition: Alpha cells (α-cells) are [endocrine cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_cell)s that are found in the [Islets of Langerhans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islets_of_langerhans) in the [pancreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreas).

Alpha cell hyperplasia is defined as a specific (without similar change in other islet cells), diffuse (not limited to a particular part of pancreas), and overwhelming (many-fold) increase of the number of pancreatic [alpha cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alpha_cells).

alula , or bastard wing, (plural alulae) is a small projection on the [anterior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior) edge of the [wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wing) of modern [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s and a few [non-avian dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-avian_dinosaur)s.
Alveolus ( , ; , ; ) is a general anatomical term for a concave cavity or pit.
amacrine cells are [interneuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interneuron)s in the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina).

Ambulacral is a term typically used in the context of anatomical parts of the phylum [Echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinoderm)ata or class [Asteroidea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_star) and [Edrioasteroidea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edrioasteroidea).
ambulacrum is an elongated area of the shell of an [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinoderm) in which a row of [tube feet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tube_feet) are arranged.

Amphids ([Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language): amphi, around, double) are innervated invaginations of [cuticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuticle) in [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode)s.

ampulla of Vater, hepatopancreatic ampulla or hepatopancreatic duct is the common duct that is usually formed by a union of the [common bile duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_bile_duct) and the [pancreatic duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreatic_duct) within the wall of the [duodenum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duodenum).
Ampullae of Lorenzini (: ampulla) are [electroreceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroreceptor)s, sense organs able to detect electric fields.
AMSilk is an industrial supplier of synthetic silk [biopolymer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopolymer)s.
Amyloplasts are a type of [plastid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastid), double-enveloped organelles in plant cells that are involved in various biological pathways.
Anal cells are rear components of the [insect wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_wing)s, found for example in [Diptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diptera) (flies).
anal glands or anal sacs are small glands near the [anus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anus) in many [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.

anal sulcus, also called the anal sinus or anal canal, in [Gastropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropods) is a notch, a shelly tube at the top of the [aperture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aperture_(mollusc)).
anal triangle is the posterior part of the [perineum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perineum).
spatium or anatomic space is a space (cavity or gap).

definition: anatomical plane is an imaginary flat surface ([plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mathematical_plane)) that is used to transect the body, in order to describe the location of structures or the direction of movements.

Anatomical Science International is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) that covers [gross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_anatomy), [histologic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology), cellular, molecular, biochemical, physiological and behavioral studies of humans and experimental animals.

anatomical snuff box or snuffbox or foveola radialis is a triangular deepening on the [[Anatomical terms of location#Relative directions|radial]], [dorsal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorsum_(biology)) aspect of the [hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand)—at the level of the [carpal bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpal_bones), specifically, the [scaphoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scaphoid_bone) and [trapezium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapezium_(bone)) bones forming the floor.

Anatomical terminology is a specialized system of terms used by [anatomists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomists), [zoologists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoologists), and [health professionals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Health_professionals), such as [doctors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physician), [surgeons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgeons), and [pharmacists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharmacists), to describe the structures and [functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(biology)) of the [body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_(biology)).
anatomical terms descriptive of bone are defined in [anatomical terminology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_terminology), and are often derived from Greek and Latin.
Squamous epithelium has cells that are wider than their height (flat and scale-like).

Anatomical Theatre of the Archiginnasio is a hall once used for [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) lectures and displays held at the medical school in [Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bologna), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy) that used to be located in the [Palace of the Archiginnasio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archiginnasio_of_Bologna), the first unified seat of the [University of Bologna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Bologna).

definition: anatomical variation, anatomical variant, or anatomical variability is a presentation of body structure with [morphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) features different from those that are typically described in the majority of individuals.
Anatomy Charts of the Arabs are a collection of [drawing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Drawing)s described by [Karl Sudhoff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karl_Sudhoff) on 1908.

anatomy murder (sometimes called burking in [British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English)) is a murder committed in order [to use all or part of the cadaver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Murder_for_body_parts) for medical research or teaching.
anatomy of pterosaurs was highly modified from their reptilian ancestors by the adaptation to flight.
anchor cell is a cell in [nematodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematodes) such as [Caenorhabditis elegans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caenorhabditis_elegans).
Ancient Egyptian anatomical studies is an article about the [history of anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_anatomy) within [ancient Egypt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Egypt).

Animal reflectors or animal mirrors are important to the survival of many kinds of [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal), and, in some cases, have been mimicked by engineers developing [photonic crystals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photonic_crystals).
Tooth development or odontogenesis is the process in which [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teeth) develop and grow into the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth).

Ann Arbor staging is the [staging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer_staging) system for [lymphoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymphoma)s, both in [Hodgkin's lymphoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hodgkin's_lymphoma) (formerly designated Hodgkin's disease) and [non-Hodgkin lymphoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-Hodgkin_lymphoma) (abbreviated NHL).

Annular pancreas is a rare condition in which the second part of the [duodenum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Duodenum) is surrounded by a ring of [pancreatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreas) tissue continuous with the [head of the pancreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_the_pancreas).

annulus is the ring-like or collar-like structure sometimes found on the [stipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stipe_(mycology)) of some species of [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom)s.
annulus is an external circular ring.

definition: Anonychia is the failure to form [fingernails or toenail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy))s.

anorectal canal is an embryonic structure in [placental mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placental_mammal)s that develops from the posterior portion of the [cloaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloaca_(embryology)), after it is divided by the [urorectal septum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urorectal_septum) in the 6th week of [embryonic development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryogenesis).

antenna (plural: antennae) is one of a pair of [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s used for [sensing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_system) in [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s.
antennal lobe is the primary (first order) olfactory brain area in [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s.

anterior chamber angle is a part of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) located between the [cornea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornea) and [iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_(anatomy)) which contains the [trabecular meshwork](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trabecular_meshwork).

anterior chamber ([[Optometric Abbreviations#AC|AC]]) is the [aqueous humor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aqueous_humor)-filled space inside the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) between the [iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_(anatomy)) and the [cornea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornea)'s innermost surface, the [endothelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corneal_endothelium).
anterior compartment of the leg is a [fascial compartment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascial_compartments_of_leg) of the lower [leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leg).

anterior intermuscular septum of leg or anterior crural intermuscular septum is a band of [fascia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascia) which separates the [lateral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateral_compartment_of_leg) from the [anterior compartment of leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_compartment_of_leg).
anterior ligament of the [elbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbow-joint) is a broad and thin fibrous layer covering the anterior surface of the joint.
anterior meniscofemoral ligament (ligament of Humphry) is a small fibrous band of the [knee joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee_joint).

anterior pituitary (also called the adenohypophysis or pars anterior) is a major [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) of the [endocrine system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_system).

Anterior vertebral [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vein) is a venous structure located in the cervical region.

antheridium is a [haploid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haploid) structure or organ producing and containing male [gamete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamete)s (called antherozoids or [sperm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sperm)).
Anthropometry (, ) refers to the measurement of the human individual.

Antigen retrieval is a non-enzymatic pretreatment for immunostaining to reduce or eliminate the chemical modifications caused by formalin fixation, through high temperature heating or strong alkaline solution (non-heating).

Antlers are extensions of an animal's [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) found in members of the [Cervidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cervidae) (deer) [family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_(taxonomy)).

definition: Antonio Scarpa (9 May 1752 – 31 October 1832) was an Italian [anatomist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomist) and professor.
antorbital fenestra (plural: fenestrae) is an opening in the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) that is in front of the eye sockets.
antrum is a general term for a cavity or chamber, which may have specific meaning in reference to certain organs or sites in the body.

aortic valve is a [valve in the heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_valve) of humans and most other animals, located between the [left ventricle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventricle_(heart)) and the [aorta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aorta).

Simian hand |image = Ape Hand.jpg |image_size = |alt = |caption = Ape hand deformity |pronounce = |specialty = Ape hand deformity is one aspect of [median nerve palsy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Median_nerve_palsy), which is usually caused by deep injuries to the arm, forearm, and wrist area.

aperture is an opening in certain kinds of [mollusc shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc_shell)s: it is the main opening of the shell, where the head-foot part of the body of the animal emerges for locomotion, feeding, etc.

apex ([adjectival form](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adjectival_form): apical) is part of the [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc_shell) of a [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk).

Apophallation is the biting off of the penis, known to occur in [terrestrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrestrial_animal) [slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug)s, which are [hermaphroditic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermaphroditic) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s.

apoplast is the network of cell walls, intercellular spaces, and xylem vessels in plants that allows the movement of water, ions, and small molecules outside the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane).
appendage (or outgrowth) is an external body part or natural prolongation that protrudes from an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)'s body such as an arm or a leg.

appressorium is a specialized cell typical of many fungal [plant pathogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_pathogen)s that is used to infect [host](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Host_(biology)) plants.
Aptery is the anatomical condition of an animal completely lacking any kind of [wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wing)s.

DNA barcoding is an alternative method to the traditional morphological [taxonomic classification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomic_classification), and has frequently been used to identify species of aquatic [macroinvertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macroinvertebrate)s (generally considered those large enough to be seen without magnification).

aqueous humour is a [transparent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transparency_and_translucency) water-like fluid similar to [blood plasma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_plasma), but containing low protein concentrations.

Archaeocytes (from [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) [[:wikt:ἀρχαῖος|archaios]] ) or amoebocytes are [amoeboid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amoebocyte) cells found in [sponges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_sponge).

archinephros, or holonephros, is a primitive kidney that has been retained by the larvae of [hagfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hagfish) and some [caecilians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caecilians).

arctometatarsalian organism is one in which the [[Anatomical_terms_of_location#Proximal_and_distal|proximal]] part of the middle [metatarsal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metatarsal) is pinched between the surrounding metatarsals.

media.file: T. rex versus A. atrox feet.JPG

definition: arcuate uterus is a form of a [uterine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterine) anomaly or variation where the [uterine cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterine_cavity) displays a concave contour towards the [fundus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundus_(uterus)).

Breast schematic diagram ==Mechanoreceptors== [Breastfeeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breastfeeding) by the baby stimulates slowly and rapidly adapting [mechanoreceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanoreceptor)s that are densely packed around the areolar region.
Areolar glands, also known as glandulae areolares, Montgomery glands, and tubercula areolae, are 10–15 elevations found on the [areola](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Areola).
arista is a simple or variously modified [[Wiktionary:apex|apical]] or subapical bristle, arising from the third [antennal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antenna_(biology)) segment.

arm refers to the [upper limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_limb) in common usage, although academically the term specifically means the upper arm ==See also== * [Axilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axilla) – also known as armpit, underarm or oxter * [Common flexor tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_flexor_tendon) ==References== [[Category:Arm| ]] [[Category:Upper limb anatomy]] foi4i3dv06am6m96atgfjnaycdxt3xq

artery of Percheron (AOP) is a rare [anatomical variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_variation) in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) vascularization in which a single arterial trunk arises from the [posterior cerebral artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_cerebral_artery) (PCA) to supply both sides of the [thalamus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thalamus) and [midbrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midbrain).

Arthroconidia are a type of [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore) typically produced by segmentation of pre-existing fungal [hyphae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphae).

arthropod leg is a form of jointed [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage) of [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s, usually used for [walking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walking).

Arthur Thomson (21 March 1858, [Edinburgh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edinburgh) – 7 February 1935, [Oxford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxford)) was a British [anatomist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) and [anthropologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropology).

articular bone is part of the lower jaw of most [vertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrates), including most [jawed fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawed_fish), [amphibians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibians), [birds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birds) and various kinds of [reptiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptiles), as well as ancestral [mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal).

term: Articular capsule of the knee joint
page: Articular capsule of the knee joint

definition: articulations of the heads of the ribs (or costocentral articulations) constitute a series of gliding or [arthrodial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthrodial) [joints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joints), and are formed by the [articulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Articulation_(anatomy)) of the heads of the typical [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib)s with the [costal facet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costal_facet)s on the contiguous margins of the [bodies of the](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_of_vertebra) [thoracic vertebrae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoracic_vertebrae) and with the [intervertebral disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intervertebral_disc)s between them; the [first](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/First_rib), tenth, [eleventh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eleventh_rib) and [twelfth rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_rib)s each articulate with a single vertebra.

term: Ascending limb of loop of Henle
page: Ascending limb of loop of Henle
definition: ascending limb of the loop of Henle is a segment of the heterogenous [loop of Henle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loop_of_Henle) downstream of the [descending limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Descending_limb_of_loop_of_Henle), after the sharp bend of the loop.
related: Descending limb of loop of Henle

definition: ascocarp, or ascoma (: ascomata), is the fruiting body ([sporocarp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporocarp_(fungi))) of an [ascomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascomycete) phylum fungus.
ascus (; : asci) an example is the illustrated Hypomyces chrysospermus.
association cortex is a part of the [cerebral cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_cortex) that performs complex cognitive functions.
atrioventricular node (AV node, or Aschoff-Tawara node) is part of the [electrical conduction system of the heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrical_conduction_system_of_the_heart).

atrium (; : atria) is one of the two [[Heart#Chambers|upper chambers]] in the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) that receives blood from the [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system).
Atrophy is the partial or complete [wasting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wasting) away of a part of the body.

augmented renal clearance (ARC) is a phenomenon where certain critically ill patients may display increased [clearance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clearance_(pharmacology)) of a medication through the kidneys.

auramine–rhodamine stain (AR), also known as the Truant auramine–rhodamine stain, is a [histological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology) technique used to visualize [acid-fast bacilli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acid-fast) using [[microscopy#Fluorescence|fluorescence microscopy]], notably species in the [Mycobacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycobacterium) [genus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genus).

Automated species identification is a method of making the expertise of [taxonomists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomy_(biology)) available to ecologists, [parataxonomists](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parataxonomy) and others via digital technology and [artificial intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artificial_intelligence).

Automated tissue image analysis or histopathology image analysis (HIMA) is a process by which computer-controlled [automatic test equipment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Automatic_test_equipment) is used to evaluate [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) samples, using computations to derive quantitative measurements from an image to avoid subjective errors.
Autospores are a type of spores that are produced by algae to enable asexual reproduction and spread.
Auxesis (from the Greek word meaning increase; grow) refers to growth from an increase in [cell size](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_size) rather than an increase in the number of cells.

auxiliary cell is a [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore)-like structure that forms within the [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) [family](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Family_(taxonomy)) [Gigasporaceae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigasporaceae) (order [Gigasporales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gigasporales) }} [[File:Spiny to papillate auxiliary cells from a species of Gigaspora.jpg|thumb|A cluster of spiny to papillate auxiliary cells from a species of Gigaspora]] [[File:Auxiliary cells knobby.jpg|thumb|A cluster of knobby auxiliary cel

categories: Jodrell Professors of Zoology and Comparative Anatomy

definition: axial line is the line between two adjacent [dermatomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermatome_(anatomy)) that are not represented by immediately adjacent spinal levels.

axial skeleton is the [core](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core_(anatomy)) part of the [endoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endoskeleton) made of the [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)s of the [head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head) and [trunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunk_(anatomy)) of [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.

axilla (: axillae or axillas; also known as the armpit, underarm or oxter) is the area on the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) directly under the [shoulder joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder_joint).

axillary arch is a [variant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_variation) of the [latissimus dorsi muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latissimus_dorsi_muscle) in [humans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humans).

axillary joints are two [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint)s in the [axillary region](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axilla) of the body, and include the [shoulder joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder_joint) and the [acromioclavicular joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acromioclavicular_joint).
axillary lines are the anterior axillary line, midaxillary line and the posterior axillary line.

axoneme is the [microtubule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtubule)-based [cytoskeletal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoskeletal) structure that forms the core of a [cilium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilium) or [flagellum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellum).
azygoesophageal recess is a right posterior mediastinal recess into which the medial edge of the right lower lobe extends.
azygos lobe is a normal [anatomical variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_variation) of the upper lobe of the right [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_lung).
Azzopardi phenomenon, or Azzopardi effect, is the presence of DNA in [necrotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Necrosis) [venule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venule)s.

back is the area of [horse anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equine_anatomy) where the [saddle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddle) goes, and in popular usage extends to include the loin or lumbar region behind the thoracic vertebrae that also is crucial to a horse's weight-carrying ability.
bacterial capsule is a large structure common to many [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).
bacterial outer membrane is found in [gram-negative bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria).

bacteriome is a specialized organ, found mainly in some [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s, that hosts [endosymbiotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endosymbiotic) [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).
ball-and-chain inactivation is a model to explain the fast inactivation mechanism of [voltage-gated ion channels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Voltage-gated_ion_channels).

ballistospore or ballistoconidia is a [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore) that is discharged into the air from a living being, usually a species of [fungus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus).

band cell (also called band neutrophil, band form or stab cell) is a cell undergoing [granulopoiesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granulopoiesis), derived from a [metamyelocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamyelocyte), and leading to a mature [granulocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granulocyte).

Bandemia refers to an excess or increased levels of [band cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Band_cell)s (immature [white blood cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_blood_cells)) released by the [bone marrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_marrow) into the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood).
barbel is a slender, whisker-like sensory [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) near the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth) (sometimes called whiskers or tendrils).

definition: basal lamina is a layer of [extracellular matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_matrix) secreted by the epithelial cells, on which the [epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium) sits.

basement membrane, also known as the basal lamina, is a specialized form of [extracellular matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_matrix) (ECM) common to all [multicellular animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism)s.

basidiocarp, basidiome, or basidioma () is the [sporocarp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporocarp_(fungi)) of a [basidiomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiomycete), the [multicellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular) structure on which the [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore)-producing [hymenium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymenium) is borne.

Basidiolichens are [lichen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichen)ized members of the [division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Division_(taxonomy)) [Basidiomycota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiomycota) within the subkingdom [Dikarya](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dikarya) of the [kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_(biology)) [Fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus).

basidiospore is a reproductive [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore) produced by [basidiomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiomycete) [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi), a grouping that includes [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom)s, [shelf fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shelf_fungus), [rusts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_fungus), and [smut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smut_(fungus))s.

basidium (: basidia) is a microscopic [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore)-producing structure found on the [hymenophore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymenophore) of [reproductive bodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporocarp_(fungi)) of [basidiomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiomycota) fungi.
basihyal tooth plate is a specialized structure found in certain fish species.

basilic vein is a large [superficial vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superficial_vein) of the [upper limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_limb) that helps drain parts of the [hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand) and [forearm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forearm).
anterior pituitary basophil is a type of cell in the [anterior pituitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_pituitary) which manufactures [hormones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hormones).

Computational anatomy (CA) is a discipline within [medical imaging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_imaging) focusing on the study of anatomical shape and form at the visible or [gross anatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_anatomy) scale of [morphology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)).
beak is part of the [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc_shell) of a [bivalve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalve) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk), i.e.
Beau's lines are deep grooved lines that run from side to side on the [fingernail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy)) or the toenail.
categories: Anatomy named for one who described it

definition: Béclard's triangle is an area whose boundaries are the posterior border of the [hyoglossus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyoglossus), the posterior belly of the [digastric muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digastric_muscle) and the greater horn of the [hyoid bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyoid_bone).

media.file: BCC with squamous cell metaplasia with HE and BerEP4 staining.jpg

definition: Beta cells (β-cells) are specialized [endocrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_system) [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) located within the [pancreatic islets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreatic_islets) of [Langerhans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langerhans_cell) responsible for the production and release of [insulin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insulin) and [amylin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amylin).

bicipital aponeurosis (also known as lacertus fibrosus or Pirogoff's aponeurosis) is a broad [aponeurosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aponeurosis) of the [biceps brachii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biceps_brachii), which is located in the [cubital fossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubital_fossa) of the [elbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbow).

bicipitoradial bursa is a [bursa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bursa_(anatomy)) located between the distal tendon of the [biceps brachii muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biceps_brachii_muscle) and the anterior part of the [tuberosity of the radius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberosity_of_the_radius).

biological screw joint is a naturally occurring form of the [screw joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Screw_joint), a mechanical device that combines rotational movement with single-axis translation.

Biological Stain Commission (BSC) is an organization that provides third-party testing and certification of [dye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dye)s and a few other compounds that are used to enhance contrast in specimens examined in biological and medical laboratories.

biology of depression is the attempt to identify a biochemical origin of [depression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Depression_(mood)), as opposed to theories that emphasize psychological or situational causes.

Biphenotypic acute leukaemia (BAL) is an uncommon type of leukemia which arises in multipotent progenitor cells which have the ability to differentiate into both [myeloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myeloid) and [lymphoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymphoid) lineages.

related: List of terms used in bird topography

definition: Vision is the most important sense for [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s, since good eyesight is a major leverage for safe flight.

media.file: Bald Eagle at The National Zoo.jpg

definition: Bird wings are paired [forelimb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forelimb)s in [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s, which evolved [specialized feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight_feather)s to generate [lift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lift_(force)) and [thrust](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thrust) and allow the birds to [fly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_flight).

bivalve shell is the enveloping [exoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoskeleton) or [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc_shell) of a [bivalve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalve) [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc), composed of two hinged halves or [valves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Valve_(mollusc)).

blastoconidium (plural blastoconidia) is an asexual holoblastic [conidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conidia) formed through the blowing out or [budding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budding) process of a yeast cell, which is a type of [asexual reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asexual_reproduction) that results in a bud arising from a parent cell.

blastospore is an [asexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asexual_reproduction) reproductive [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore) produced by [budding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budding), commonly found in [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) within the division [Glomeromycota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glomeromycota).

blood gill is a [gill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill)-like structure restricted to organs with spacious lumen and poorly developed/absent [trachea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trachea), found in larvae of [aquatic insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_insect)s.
Blood vessels are the tubular structures of a [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system) transporting [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) in animal bodies.

blood–ocular barrier is a barrier created by endothelium of [capillaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillaries) of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) and [iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_(anatomy)), [ciliary epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliary_body) and [retinal pigment epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_pigment_epithelium).

blood–retinal barrier, or the BRB, is part of the [blood–ocular barrier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood–ocular_barrier) that consists of cells that are joined tightly together to prevent certain substances from entering the tissue of the retina.
blue whale penis is the largest in the animal kingdom.

Bodies: The Exhibition is an [exhibition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exhibition) showcasing human bodies that have been preserved through a process called [plastination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastination) and dissected to display bodily systems.
body cavity is any space or compartment, or [potential space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Potential_space), in an animal body.

Body hair or androgenic hair is [terminal hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminal_hair) that develops on the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) during and after [puberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puberty).

body or shaft of the penis is the free portion of the [human penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_penis) that is located outside of the [pelvic cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvic_cavity).
body orifice is any opening in the body of an animal.

body plan, (), or ground plan is a set of [morphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) [features](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic_trait) common to many members of a [phylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylum) of [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s.

Body proportions is the study of artistic [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy), which attempts to explore the relation of the elements of the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) to each other and to the whole.
Body snatching is the illicit removal of [corpse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpse)s from graves, morgues, and other burial sites.

media.file: Body snatchers at work, Old Crown Inn, Penicuik.JPG

definition: bolete is a type of [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom), or [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) [fruiting body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruiting_body).

Bone canaliculi are microscopic canals between the [lacunae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacuna_(histology)) of [ossified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ossified) [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone).
Bone decalcification is the softening of bones due to the removal of calcium ions, and can be performed as a histological technique to study bones and extract DNA.

Bone healing, or fracture healing, is a [proliferative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_growth) [physiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiological) process in which the body facilitates the repair of a [bone fracture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_fracture).

Bone marrow adipose tissue (BMAT), also referred to as marrow adipose tissue (MAT), is a type of [adipose tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adipose_tissue) (fat deposit) found within the [bone marrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_marrow).

bone sarcoma is a [primary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_tumor) [malignant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malignant) [bone tumour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_tumour), a type of [sarcoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcoma) that starts in the [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)s.

Bonwill Triangle is a triangle formed by the contact point of the [mandibular central incisors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_central_incisor) and the right and left [[Mandibular condyles#Condyle|mandibular condyles]].

Borderline lichen is a term used in [lichenology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichenology) for structurally simple, [symbiotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbiosis) associations between a [fungus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) and a [photosynthetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthesis) partner (an [alga](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alga) or [cyanobacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyanobacterium)).

Bothria (from Greek bothrion = small pit, diminutive of [bothros](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bothros) = pit, trench) are elongate, dorsal or ventral longitudinal grooves on the [scolex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scolex) of [cestoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cestoda).
Bouin solution, or Bouin's solution, is a compound [fixative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixation_(histology)) used in [histology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology).

Bowman's capsule (or the Bowman capsule, capsula glomeruli, or glomerular capsule) is a cup-like sac at the beginning of the [tubular component](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_tubule) of a [nephron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephron) in the [mammalian kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammalian_kidney) that performs the first step in the [filtration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filtration) of blood to form urine.

Bowman's layer (Bowman's membrane, anterior limiting lamina, anterior elastic lamina) is a smooth, acellular, nonregenerating layer, located between the superficial [epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium) and the [stroma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stroma_of_cornea) in the [cornea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornea) of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye).

brain is an [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(biology)) that serves as the center of the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) in all [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) and most [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate) [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s.

Brain death is the permanent, irreversible, and complete loss of [brain function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electroencephalography), which may include cessation of involuntary activity (e.g., [[Control of ventilation#Control of respiratory rhythm|breathing]]) necessary to sustain life.

Brainstem death is a clinical syndrome defined by the absence of reflexes with pathways through the [brainstem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brainstem) and that in terms of its ability to diagnose de facto brainstem death it falls far short.

Brain–body mass ratio, also known as the brain–body weight ratio, is the ratio of brain mass to body mass, which is hypothesized to be a rough estimate of the [intelligence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intelligence_(trait)) of an [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal), although fairly inaccurate in many cases.

bulbus arteriosus is a [pear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pear) shaped chamber that functions as a capacitor, maintaining continuous [blood flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_flow) into the [gill arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill_arch)es.

Bulliform cells or motor cells are large, bubble-shaped [epidermal cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(botany)) that occur in groups on the upper surface of the leaves of many [monocot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monocot)s.
bursa of Fabricius ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin): bursa cloacalis or bursa Fabricii) is the site of [hematopoiesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hematopoiesis).

buttocks (: buttock) are two rounded portions of the exterior anatomy of humans, located on the posterior of the pelvic region.

calf (: calves; [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin): sura) is the back portion of the lower leg in [human anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_anatomy).
callosity is a type of [callus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callus), a piece of [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin) that has become thickened as a result of repeated contact and friction.

calypter is either of two posterior lobes of the posterior margin of the [forewing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_wing) of [flies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fly) between the extreme posterior wing base and the [[insect wing#Fields|alula]], which covers the [haltere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haltere)s.
cambium (: cambiums or cambia), in plants, is a tissue layer that provides partially undifferentiated [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell)s for plant growth.

Campaniform sensilla are a class of [mechanoreceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanoreceptor)s found in [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s, which respond to local stress and strain within the animal's cuticle.
canal (or canalis in [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin)) is a tubular passage or channel which connects different regions of the body.
Canine massage is a branch of [massage therapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Massage_therapy) that promotes health in [dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog)s.
canthus (: canthi, palpebral commissures) is either corner of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) where the upper and lower [eyelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelid)s meet.

Cappella Sansevero (also known as the Cappella Sansevero de' Sangri or Pietatella) is a chapel located on Via Francesco de Sanctis 19, just northeast of the church of [San Domenico Maggiore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Domenico_Maggiore), in the historic center of [Naples](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naples), [Italy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Italy).
capsule of the glenohumeral (shoulder) joint is the [articular capsule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Articular_capsule) of the [shoulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenohumeral_joint).

carapace is a [dorsal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorsum_(biology)) (upper) section of the [exoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoskeleton) or shell in a number of animal groups, including [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s, such as [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s and [arachnid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arachnid)s, as well as vertebrates, such as [turtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turtles) and [tortoises](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tortoises).
Carcinoma is a malignancy that develops from [epithelial cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelial_cells).

definition: Cardiac excitation-contraction coupling (Cardiac EC coupling) describes the series of events, from the production of an [electrical impulse (action potential)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_action_potential) to the [contraction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle_contraction) of [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle)s in the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart).

Cardiac physiology or heart function is the study of healthy, unimpaired function of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart): involving blood flow; [myocardium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle) structure; the [electrical conduction system of the heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_conduction_system); the [cardiac cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_cycle) and cardiac output and how these interact and depend on one another.

cardiac skeleton, also known as the fibrous skeleton of the heart, is a high-density homogeneous structure of [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) that forms and anchors the [valves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_valve) of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart), and influences the forces exerted by and through them.
cardiocentric hypothesis, the heart is the primary location of human emotions, cognition, and awareness.

Cardiomyocyte proliferation refers to the ability of [cardiac muscle cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle_cells) to progress through the [cell cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_cycle) and continue to divide.

Cardiovascular physiology is the study of the [cardiovascular system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiovascular_system), specifically addressing the [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) ( || || over-perfused || Crucial in [thermoregulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermoregulation).
Carnassials are paired upper and lower teeth modified in such a way as to allow enlarged and often self-sharpening edges to pass by each other in a shearing manner.

Carnoy's solution is a [fixative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fixation_(histology)) composed of 60% [ethanol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ethanol), 30% [chloroform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroform) and 10% glacial [acetic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acetic_acid), 1 gram of ferric chloride.
Carpometacarpal bossing (or metacarpal/carpal bossing) is a small, immovable mass of bone on the back of the wrist.

Cavernous tissue refers to [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood)-filled spaces lined by [endothelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endothelium) and surrounded by [smooth muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_muscle).

cavo-tricuspid isthmus is a body of fibrous tissue in the lower [right atrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_atrium) between the [inferior vena cava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inferior_vena_cava), and the [tricuspid valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricuspid_valve).

cavoatrial junction (CAJ) is the point at which the [superior vena cava](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superior_vena_cava) meets and melds into the [[Anatomical terms of location#Superior and inferior|superior]] wall of the [cardiac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) right [atrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atrium_(heart)).
cell is the basic structural and functional unit of all [forms of life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Life) or [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s.
Cell division orientation is the direction along which the new daughter [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s are formed.
Cell junctions Cell adhesion is a vital component of the body.

cell membrane (also known as the plasma membrane or cytoplasmic membrane, and historically referred to as the plasmalemma) is a [semipermeable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semipermeable_membrane) [biological membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_membrane) that separates and protects the [interior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) of a [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) from the [outside environment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_space) (the extracellular space).
cell nucleus (; : nuclei) is a [membrane-bound organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane-bound_organelle) found in [eukaryotic cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic_cell)s.

Cellular extensions also known as cytoplasmic protrusions and cytoplasmic processes are those structures that project from different [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), in the body, or in other organisms.
Cement glands are small organs found in [Acanthocephala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acanthocephala) that are used to temporarily close the posterior end of the female after copulation.

cementoenamel junction (CEJ) is the location where the [enamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_enamel), which covers the anatomical [crown](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crown_(tooth)) of a [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth), and the [cementum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cementum), which covers the anatomical root of a tooth, meet.
cenchrus (plural cenchri) is a specialized anatomical structure in the [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) group known as [sawflies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sawfly).

central spindle is a microtubule based structure, which forms in between segregating [chromosomes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosomes) during [anaphase](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anaphase) where the two sets of [microtubules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtubules), emanating from opposite halves of the [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), overlap, and become arranged into antiparallel bundles by various microtubule associated proteins (MAPs) and [motor proteins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Motor_proteins).

central tendon of the [diaphragm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoracic_diaphragm) is a thin but strong [aponeurosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aponeurosis) situated slightly anterior to [the vault formed by the muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_abdominal_wall), resulting in longer posterior muscle fibers.

centric relation is the [mandibular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_mandible) jaw position in which the [head of the condyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_condyle) is situated as far anterior and superior as it possibly can within the [mandibular fossa/glenoid fossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_fossa).

definition: cephalon is the [head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head) section of an [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod).

cephalothorax is the region including cephalon and thorax, marked in yellow.|upright=1.2]] The cephalothorax, also called prosoma in some groups, is a [tagma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tagma_(biology)) of various [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s, comprising the head and the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax_(arthropod_anatomy)) fused together, as distinct from the [[Abdomen#Arthropoda|abdomen]] behind.

Cerata, singular ceras, are anatomical structures found externally in [nudibranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nudibranch) [sea slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_slug)s, especially in aeolid nudibranchs, [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_animal) [opisthobranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opisthobranch) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s in the [clade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clade) [Aeolidida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aeolidida).

Cerci (: cercus) are paired [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s usually on the rear-most segments of many [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s, including [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s and [symphyla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symphyla)ns.

cerebral arteriovenous malformation (cerebral AVM, CAVM, cAVM, brain AVM, or BAVM) is an abnormal connection between the [arteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artery) and [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vein)s in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain)—specifically, an [arteriovenous malformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arteriovenous_malformation) in the [cerebrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebrum).
Cervical ribs are the [ribs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ribs) of the [neck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neck) in many [tetrapods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapods).

cervicoaxillary canal is the passageway that extends between the [neck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neck) and the upper extremities through which the [long thoracic nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_thoracic_nerve) and other structures pass.

cervix in [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s is a membrane that separates the [head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head) from the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax_(insect_anatomy)) and is composed of structures from both of these.

chaeta or cheta (; ) is a [chitin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitin)ous bristle or [seta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seta) found on [annelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annelid) worms, although the term is also frequently used to describe similar structures in other invertebrates such as [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s.
chalaza (; ; : chalazas or chalazae ) is a structure inside [bird egg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird_egg)s and plant [ovule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovule)s.

Charles Barrett Lockwood (23 September 1856 – 8 November 1914) was a British [surgeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgeon) and [anatomist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomist) who practiced surgery at [[St.
