definition: Charles Collignon [FRS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fellow_of_the_Royal_Society) (30 January 1725 – 1 October 1785) was a British surgeon and Cambridge's professor of anatomy.
Cheek pouches are pockets on both sides of the head of some mammals between the jaw and the cheek.

media.file: Chipmunk with stuffed cheeks in Prospect Park (05980) - cropped.jpg
Syrian hamster filling his cheek pouches with Dandelion leaves.JPG

definition: chelicerae () are the [mouthparts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod_mouthparts) of the subphylum [Chelicerata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelicerata), an [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod) group that includes [arachnid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arachnid)s, [horseshoe crab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horseshoe_crab)s, and [sea spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_spider)s.

chestnut is a keratinized growth found on the inner side of the leg above the knee on the front leg, and if present, below the [hock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hock_(zoology)) on the hind leg in many [equines](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equinae).

chlamydospore is the thick-walled large [resting spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resting_spore) of several kinds of [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi), including [Ascomycota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascomycota) such as [Candida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Candida_(fungus)), page=0123 Allenpress.com] [[Category:Germ cells]] [[Category:Fungal morphology and anatomy]] [[Category:Mycology]] 2o9sfl3s6bs6qxpwzj0nvm8buc26ufa

Chloragogen cells, also called y cells, are star-shaped cells in [annelids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annelids) involved with [excretory functions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excretory_system) and intermediary [metabolism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metabolism).

choanoderm is a type of cell layer composed of [flagellated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellated) collar cells, or [choanocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choanocyte)s, found in [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge)s.

choanosome is an inner region of a [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge), supported on the [choanoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choanoskeleton), the structure that contains the [choanocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choanocyte)s.

chordae tendineae (: chorda tendinea) or tendinous cords, colloquially known as the heart strings, are inelastic cords of [fibrous connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibrous_connective_tissue) that connect the [papillary muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Papillary_muscle)s to the [tricuspid valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tricuspid_valve) and the [mitral valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bicuspid_valve) in the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart).

Chordotonal organs are [stretch receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stretch_receptor) organs found only in [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s and [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s.
choriovitelline placenta is a [placenta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placenta) formed by the [yolk sac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yolk_sac) and [chorion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chorion).
Choristomas, a form of [heterotopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heterotopia_(medicine)), are masses of normal tissues found in abnormal locations.

choroid, also known as the choroidea or choroid coat, is a part of the [uvea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uvea), the [vascular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel) layer of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).
choroidal fissure is a groove that extends along the ventral aspect of the [optic stalk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optic_stalk).

Chromaffin cells, also called pheochromocytes (or phaeochromocytes), are [neuroendocrine cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroendocrine_cell)s found mostly in the [medulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrenal_medulla) of the [adrenal gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrenal_gland)s in [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.

categories: Anatomy named for one who described it

definition: ciliary processes are formed by the inward folding of the various layers of the [choroid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choroid), viz.

cilium (: cilia; ; in Medieval Latin and in anatomy, cilium) is a short hair-like [membrane protrusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_protrusion) from many types of [eukaryotic cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic_cell).

circulating tumor cell (CTC) is a [cancer cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer_cell) from a [primary tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_tumor) that has [shed into](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intravasate) the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) of the [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system), or the [lymph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymph) of the [lymphatic system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymphatic_system).
Circulating tumor DNA (ctDNA) is [tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor)-derived fragmented [DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA) in the bloodstream that is not associated with cells.

circulatory system of [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod)s is [open](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Open_circulatory_system), with the fluid, or [haemolymph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haemolymph), flowing through [sinuses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinus_(anatomy)) and bathing the tissues directly.
circulatory system of the horse consists of the heart, the blood vessels, and the blood.

circumesophageal or circumpharyngeal nerve ring is an arrangement of [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve) [ganglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganglion) around the [foregut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foregut) ([esophagus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esophagus) or [pharynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharynx)) of an animal.

cirrus ( , : cirri, , from the Latin cirrus meaning a curl-like tuft or fringe) is a long, thin structure in an animal similar to a [tentacle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tentacle) but generally lacking the tentacle's strength, flexibility, thickness, and sensitivity.

media.file: Attachment clamps of 'Omanicotyle heterospina' (Monogenea, Microcotylidae) - Median View.jpg

definition: clamp connection is a hook-like structure formed by growing [hypha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypha)l cells of certain [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi).
clasper is a [male](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male) anatomical structure found in some groups of animals, used in [mating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mating).

Clathrin-independent endocytosis refers to the cellular process by which cells internalize extracellular molecules and particles through mechanisms that do not rely on the protein [clathrin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clathrin), playing a crucial role in diverse physiological processes such as nutrient uptake, membrane turnover, and [cellular signaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_signaling).

clavarioid fungi are a group of [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) in the [Basidiomycota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiomycota) typically having erect, simple or branched [basidiocarps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiocarps) (fruit bodies) that are formed on the ground, on decaying vegetation, or on dead wood.
clavicle, collarbone, or keybone is a slender, S-shaped [long bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Long_bone) approximately long which evolved from the clavicles found in coelurosaurian theropods.

clavipectoral fascia (costocoracoid membrane; coracoclavicular fascia) is a strong [fascia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascia) situated under cover of the [clavicular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavicle) portion of the [pectoralis major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoralis_major).

claw is a curved, pointed appendage found at the end of a toe or finger in most [amniote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amniote)s ([mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammals), [reptiles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptiles), [birds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birds)).

media.file: The Splayed Front Paws of a Cat.jpg

definition: cleithrum (: cleithra) is a [membrane bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_bone) which first appears as part of the skeleton in primitive [bony fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteichthyes), where it runs vertically along the [scapula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapula).

Clinical Anatomy is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer-reviewed) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) that covers [human anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_anatomy) in all its aspects—[gross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gross_anatomy), [histologic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology), [developmental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Developmental_anatomy), and [neurologic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurology)—as applied to [medical practice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine).

clitellum is a thickened [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland)ular and non-segmented section of the body wall near the head in [earthworm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthworm)s and [leeches](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leeches) that secretes a [viscid sac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viscid_sac) in which eggs are stored.

cloaca ( ), : cloacae ( or ), or vent, is the rear [orifice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_orifice) that serves as the only opening for the [digestive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gut_(anatomy)) ([rectum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectum)), [reproductive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_system), and [urinary tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urination)s (if present) of many [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) animals.
Clonogens are [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) that can self-renew and form [colonies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_(biology)).
cloven hoof, cleft hoof, divided hoof, or split hoof is a [hoof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoof) split into two toes.
cloven paw is a congenital anomaly (birth defect) that affects some animals such as dogs.

cluster of differentiation (also known as cluster of designation or classification determinant and often abbreviated as CD) is a protocol used for the identification and investigation of [cell surface molecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_surface_molecule)s providing targets for [immunophenotyping](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immunophenotyping) of cells.
Cluster roots, also known as proteoid roots, are [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)s that form clusters of closely spaced short lateral rootlets.
clypeus is one of the [sclerite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclerite)s that make up the face of an [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod).

cnemial crest is a crestlike prominence located at the front side of the head of the [tibiotarsus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibiotarsus) or [tibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibia) in the [leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leg)s of many [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s and [reptile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptile)s (including [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s and other [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur)s).

cnidocyte (also known as a cnidoblast) is a type of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) containing a large secretory [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle) called a cnidocyst, that can deliver a sting to other organisms as a way to subdue prey and defend against predators.

cnidosac is an [anatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical) feature that is found in the group of [sea slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_slug)s known as aeolid [nudibranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nudibranch)s, a clade of [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_(ocean)) [opisthobranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opisthobranch) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s.

coccygeal glomus (coccygeal gland or body; [Luschka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hubert_von_Luschka)’s gland) is a [vestigial structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vestigiality) ==References== [[Category:Human anatomy]] tcayb8ay5pqzjdh8ifcdx1s6yh9mx7y
Coeloconica are a type of sensory organ found in various insects, including mosquitoes, ants, and centipedes.
Coenenchyme is the common tissue that surrounds and links the [polyp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyp_(zoology))s in [octocorals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octocorallia).

coenocyte () is a [multinucleate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multinucleate) [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) which can result from multiple [nuclear divisions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karyokinesis) without their accompanying [cytokinesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytokinesis), in contrast to a [syncytium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syncytium), which results from cellular aggregation followed by dissolution of the [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane)s inside the mass.
coenogamete is a multi-nucleate [gamete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamete) (a gamete with more than one [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleus_(cell))).
coenosarc is the living tissue overlying the stony skeletal material of the coral.

coenosteum is the stony skeletal material secreted by the [coenosarc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coenosarc), the layer of living material lying between the [corallite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corallite)s (the stony cups in which the [polyp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyp_(zoology))s sit).

coffin bone, also known as the pedal bone (U.S.), is the [distal phalanx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phalanx_bones), or Charles | location = Cincinnati, Ohio | year = 2006 | page = 217 | isbn = 0-7153-2307-5 }} [[Category:Horse anatomy]] [[Category:Equine hoof]] 1hwn8g56mw83yq2lkhfuey4uacep0gy

coleoptile is a pointed protective sheath covering the emerging shoot in [monocotyledons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monocotyledons) such as grasses in which few leaf primordia and [shoot apex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoot_apex) of monocot embryo remain enclosed.

coleorhiza or root sheath is a protective layer of tissue that surrounds the [radicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radicle) (the embryonic primary root) in [monocotyledon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monocotyledon) [seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed)s.

collateral eminence is an elongated swelling lying [lateral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateralization_of_brain_function) parallel with the [hippocampus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hippocampus).

Collateral ventilation is a back-up system of [alveolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_alveolus) ventilation that can bypass the normal route of airflow when airways are restricted or obstructed.

collecting duct system of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) consists of a series of tubules and ducts that physically connect [nephron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephron)s to a [minor calyx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Minor_calyx) or directly to the [renal pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_pelvis).

Colloblasts are unique, multicellular structures found in [tentaculate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tentaculata) [ctenophores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ctenophora), a [synapomorphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synapomorphy) of that group.
Collocyte is a term variously applied in [botany](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Botany) == References == [[Category:Histology]] [[Category:Ctenophora]] c37iik5xo7oya9c5g4o3ohbf2xdxkym

collophore is a tube-like structure on the ventral side of the first [abdominal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominal) segment of the body of [springtail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Springtail)s (collembolans).
Columella (in plants) is an axis of sterile tissue which passes through the center of the spore-case of [moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moss)es.
commissure () is the location at which two objects [[wikt:abut#Verb|abut]] or are joined.

common extensor tendon is a [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon) that attaches to the [lateral epicondyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lateral_epicondyle_of_the_humerus) of the [humerus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humerus).
common iliac veins are formed by the [external iliac vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_iliac_vein)s and [internal iliac vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_iliac_vein)s.

media.file: Comparative view of the human and elephant frame, Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins, 1860.jpg

definition: Compensatory growth is a type of regenerative growth that can take place in a number of human organs after the organs are either damaged, removed, or cease to function.

Complementary cells are a mass of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s in plants, formed from the [cork cambium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cork_cambium) at the position of the [lenticel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lenticel)s.

oil bodies of [liverwort](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liverwort)s, occasionally dubbed complex oil bodies for distinction, are unique [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle)s exclusive to the [Marchantiophyta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marchantiophyta).

related: List of organs of the human body

definition: compound eye is a [visual organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) found in [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s such as [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s and [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s.
Computational anatomy is an interdisciplinary field of [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) focused on quantitative investigation and modelling of anatomical shapes variability.

Computer facial animation is primarily an area of [computer graphics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_graphics) that encapsulates methods and techniques for generating and animating images or models of a character face.

Comstock–Needham system is a naming system for insect [wing vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wing_vein)s, devised by [John Comstock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Henry_Comstock) and [George Needham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/James_George_Needham) in 1898.
Conceptacles are specialized cavities of marine and freshwater [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae) that contain the reproductive organs.

condition index in fish is a way to measure the overall health of a [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish) by comparing its weight with the typical weight of other fish of the same kind and of the same length.
condyle of humerus is the distal end of the [humerus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humerus).

Cone cells or cones are [photoreceptor cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photoreceptor_cells) in the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of the vertebrate [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).

Conidial anastomosis tubes (CATs) are cells formed from the [conidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conidia) (a type of fungal asexual spores) of many filamentous [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi).
Conidiomata (singular: Conidioma) are blister-like fruiting structures produced by a specific type of fungus called a [coelomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coelomycete).

media.file: Chain of conidia of an Alternaria sp. fungus PHIL 3963 lores.jpg

definition: Conjugate eye movement refers to motor coordination of the eyes that allows for bilateral fixation on a single object.

conjunctiva (: conjunctivae) is a thin [mucous membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucous_membrane) that lines the inside of the [eyelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelid)s and covers the [sclera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclera) (the white of the eye).

Connation in [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s is the developmental fusion of organs of the same type, for example, [petal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Petal)s to one another to form a tubular [corolla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corolla_(flower)).

connective tissue neoplasm or connective tissue tumor is a [neoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasm) arising from the tissues of the [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue).

corallite is the skeletal cup, formed by an individual [stony coral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scleractinia) polyp, in which the [polyp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyp_(zoology)) sits and into which it can retract.

corium is the thickened, leathery, basal portion of the forewing or [hemelytron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemelytron) of an insect in the order [Hemiptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemiptera), suborder [Heteroptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heteroptera).
Cork cambium (: cambia or cambiums) is a [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_tissue) found in many vascular plants as a part of the [periderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periderm).

cornea is the [transparent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transparency_(optics)) front part of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) which covers the [iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_(anatomy)), [pupil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pupil), and [anterior chamber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_chamber_of_eyeball).
corneal endothelium is a single layer of endothelial cells on the inner surface of the [cornea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornea).

corneal limbus (Latin: corneal border) is a highly vascularized and pigmented zone between the [cornea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornea), [conjunctiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunctiva), and the [sclera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclera) (the white of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye)) that protects and heals the cornea.

Corneocytes are terminally [differentiated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_differentiation) [keratinocytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keratinocytes) and compose most of the [stratum corneum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum_corneum), the outermost layer of the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis).

Corneous is a biological and [medical term](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_term) meaning horny, in other words made out of a substance similar to that of [horn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_(anatomy))s and [hooves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hooves) in some [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.
cornicle (or siphuncule) is one of a pair of small upright backward-pointing tubes found on the dorsal side of the fifth or sixth abdominal segments of [aphids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aphids).

Coronary circulation is the [[Circulatory system#Coronary vessels|circulation of blood]] in the [arteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arteries) and [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vein)s that supply the [heart muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle) (myocardium).

coronary sulcus (also called coronary groove, auriculoventricular groove, atrioventricular groove, AV groove) is a [groove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sulcus_(morphology)) on the surface of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) at the base of right auricle that separates the [atria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atrium_(heart)) from the [ventricles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventricle_(heart)).

corpus allatum (plural: corpora allata) is an [endocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_gland) that generates [juvenile hormone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Juvenile_hormone); as such, it plays a crucial role in [metamorphosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metamorphosis).

corpuscles of Stannius are special [endocrine organs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_system) in the kidney in fish and are responsible for maintaining [calcium balance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium_metabolism).
cortex (: cortices) is the outermost, otherwise known as superficial, layer of an [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)).
cortex of the hair shaft is located between the [hair cuticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_cuticle) and [medulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medulla_(hair)) and is the thickest hair layer.
cortical lobule (or renal lobule) is a part of a [renal lobe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_lobe).

Cosmine is a spongy, bony material that makes up the [dentine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dentine)-like layers in the scales of the [lobe-finned fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobe-finned_fish)es of the [class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_(biology)) [Sarcopterygii](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcopterygii).

costa (plural costae) is one of the vertical plates lying outside the [corallite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corallite) wall, a continuation of a [septum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Septum_(coral)) (plural septa) which lies inside the wall.

Costal cartilage, also known as rib cartilage, are bars of [hyaline cartilage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyaline_cartilage) that serve to prolong the [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib)s forward and contribute to the elasticity of the walls of the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax).

coxal gland is a [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland) found in some [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s, for collecting and excreting [urine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urine).

Crista dividens is a structure in the developing [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) of the human [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo) that divides the [right atrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atrium_(heart)) in a way such that it creates a pan [systolic murmur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Systolic_heart_murmur) in the same way as the [foramen ovale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foramen_ovale_(heart)).

Crista supraventricularis, also supraventricular crest, is a muscular ridge within the [right ventricle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_ventricle) of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart).

crop (also the croup, the craw, the ingluvies, and the sublingual pouch) is a thin-walled, expanded portion of the [alimentary tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gut_(anatomy)), which is used for the storage of food before [digestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digestion).

Crossed dystopia (also unilateral fusion cross fused renal ectopia) is a rare form of [renal ectopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_ectopia) ([kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) displacement) where both kidneys are on the same side of the [spine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebral_column).

crotch is the bottom of the [pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_pelvis) (the region of the [body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) where the [leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_leg)s join the [torso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torso)) and is the part of the body that includes the [groin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groin) and [genitals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex_organ).
crown is the top portion of the [head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head) behind the [vertex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertex_(anatomy)).

crozier is an anatomical feature of many fungi in the phylum [Ascomycota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascomycota) that forms at the base of [asci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascus) and looks like a hook-topped shepherd’s staff or stylized religious [crosier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crosier).

cuboideonavicular joint is a [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) (articulation) in the [foot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foot) formed between the [navicular bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navicular_bone) and [cuboid bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuboid_bone).

cut of meat is part of an animal carcass sold for [meat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meat).

cuticle (), or cuticula, is any of a variety of tough but flexible, non-mineral outer coverings of an organism, or parts of an organism, that provide protection.
hair cuticle is the outermost part of the [hair shaft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_shaft).

definition: cuticulosome is a spherical, iron-rich structure located in the [cuticular plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuticular_plate) of auditory and vestibular [hair cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_cells) in birds.

Cutin is one of two [wax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wax)y polymers that are the main components of the [plant cuticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cuticle), which covers all aerial surfaces of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s, the other being [cutan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cutan_(polymer)).

cystidium (: cystidia) is a relatively large cell found on the [sporocarp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporocarp_(fungi)) of a [basidiomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiomycete) (for example, on the surface of a [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom) gill), often between clusters of [basidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidium).

deep fascia of leg or crural fascia forms a complete investment to the [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle)s, and is fused with the [periosteum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periosteum) over the subcutaneous surfaces of the [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)s.

dermal bone or investing bone or membrane bone is a bony structure derived from [intramembranous ossification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intramembranous_ossification) forming components of the [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) [skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeleton), including much of the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull), [jaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaw)s, [gill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill) covers, shoulder girdle, [fin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fin) rays ([lepidotrichia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lepidotrichia)), and the shells of [turtles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turtle_shell) and [[armadillo#Skin|armadillos]].

dorsal veins of the penis are [blood vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel) that drain the [shaft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_of_penis) ([corpora cavernosa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_cavernosum_penis), [corpus spongiosum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_spongiosum_(penis))), the skin and the [glans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glans_penis) of the [human penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_penis).

Dua's layer, according to a 2013 paper by [Harminder Singh Dua](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harminder_Singh_Dua)'s group at the [University of Nottingham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/University_of_Nottingham), is a layer of the [cornea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornea) that had not been detected previously.

Dufour's gland is an abdominal [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland) of certain [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s, part of the anatomy of the [ovipositor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovipositor) or [sting apparatus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stinger) in female members of [Apocrita](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apocrita).

media.file: Photomicrograph of sting apparatus components journal.pone.0050400.png

definition: Duvernoy's gland is a gland found in some groups of [colubrid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colubridae) [snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake)s.

dyadic space is the name for the volume of [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) between pairs (dyads) of areas where the [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane) and an [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle) such as the [endoplasmic reticulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endoplasmic_reticulum) (or [sarcoplasmic reticulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcoplasmic_reticulum)) come into close contact (within 10-12 nanometers) when extracellular calcium enters the cell through [ion channels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion_channels) in [T-Tubule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/T-Tubule)s, leading to a rapidly increased calcium concentration in the dyadic space, triggering [ryanodine receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ryanodine_receptor)s on the [sarcoplasmic reticulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcoplasmic_reticulum) to release more calcium and trigger [cardiac myocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_myocyte) contraction - the heart beat.

dystenoid nervous system is an arrangement of [ganglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganglion) in the anterior region of some [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s where the cerebral and pleural ganglia are situated closer to each other than they are in those molluscs with the more archaic [hypoathroid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypoathroid) nervous system, but still further apart than those animals with an evolutionarily more recent [epiathroid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epiathroid) nervous system.
Dystrobrevin beta is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) which in humans is encoded by the DTNB [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).
eagle eye is among the sharpest in the animal kingdom, with an eyesight estimated at 4 to 8 times stronger than that of the average human.

eardrum, also called the tympanic membrane or myringa, is a thin, cone-shaped [membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_membrane) that separates the [external ear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_ear) from the [middle ear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_ear).

Ecdysis is the [moulting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moulting) of the [cuticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuticle) in many invertebrates of the clade [Ecdysozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecdysozoa).

Ecomorphology or ecological morphology is the study of the relationship between the [ecological role](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecological) of an individual and its [morphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) adaptations.

Ectasia (), also called ectasis (), is dilation or distention of a hollow or tubular structure, * [Dolichoectasias](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolichoectasias), weakening of arteries, usually caused by [high blood pressure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/High_blood_pressure).

ectomycorrhiza (; abbreviated EcM; or ectomycorrhizas) is a form of [symbiotic relationship](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbiotic_relationship) that occurs between a [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungal) [symbiont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symbiont), or [mycobiont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycobiont), and the [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)s of various plant species.

Ectomycorrhizal extramatrical mycelium (also known as extraradical mycelium) is the collection of filamentous [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungal) [hyphae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphae) emanating from [ectomycorrhizas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ectomycorrhizas).

ectopic kidney is a [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) that is not located in its usual position ([ectopia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ectopia_(medicine))) in the lumbar retroperitoneal space.

Ectoplasm, also called exoplasm, is the clear, gel-like, and agranular outer portion of the [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) in [protist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protist)s, that lies just beneath the [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane).

Ectoplasmic specializations are actin-related [cell–cell junctions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_junction) present in the testicular [seminiferous epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seminiferous_epithelium) and occur during [spermatogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatogenesis).

ectotympanic, or tympanicum, is a bony structure found in all [mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammals), located on the [tympanic part of the temporal bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tympanic_part_of_the_temporal_bone), which holds the [tympanic membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tympanic_membrane) (eardrum) in place.

Edward Alfred Minchin (26 February 1866 – 30 September 1915) was a British [zoologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoologist) who specialised in the study of [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge)s and [Protozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protozoa).
categories: Jodrell Professors of Zoology and Comparative Anatomy

definition: egg tooth is a temporary, sharp projection present on the [bill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beak) or snout of an [oviparous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oviparity) animal at hatching.

media.file: Painted turtle hatchling with egg tooth.jpg

definition: Eimer's organs are [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_organ)s for the sense of touch, shaped like bulbous [[wikt:papilla|papilla]]e, formed from modified [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(skin)).

Eisosomes ('eis' meaning into or portal and 'soma', meaning body) are large, heterodimeric, immobile protein complexes at the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane) which mark the site of [endocytosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocytosis) in some [eukaryote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote)s, and were discovered in the [yeast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yeast) [Saccharomyces cerevisiae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saccharomyces_cerevisiae) in 2006.
ejaculatory ducts (ductus ejaculatorii) are paired structures in the [male reproductive system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male_reproductive_system).

El Anfiteatro Anatómico Español (') was a [Spanish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spanish_Empire) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) dedicated to the fields of [Medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicine), [Surgery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgery), and [Auxiliary Sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auxiliary_Sciences), founded in the 19th century.
elbow is the region between the [upper arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arm) and the [forearm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forearm) that surrounds the elbow joint.

electric organ is an [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(biology)) that an [electric fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_fish) uses to create an [electric field](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electric_field).

Electroantennography or EAG is a technique for measuring the average output of an [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) [antenna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antenna_(biology)) to its [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) for a given [odor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odor).

Electrochemical skin conductance (ESC) is an objective, [non-invasive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-invasive_procedure) and quantitative [electrophysiological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electrophysiology) [measure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Measurement) of skin conductance through the application of a pulsating direct current on the skin.
electron microscope is a [microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope) that uses a beam of [electron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron)s as a source of illumination.

Embalming is the art and science of preserving human remains by treating them with [embalming chemicals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embalming_chemicals) in modern times to forestall [decomposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decomposition).

media.file: Unknown location. Embalming surgeon at work on soldier's body LOC cwpb.01887.jpg

definition: Embalming chemicals are a variety of preservatives, sanitising and disinfectant agents, and additives used in modern [embalming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embalming) to temporarily prevent [decomposition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decomposition) and restore a natural appearance for [viewing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viewing_(funeral)) a body after death in [funeral home](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Funeral_home)s.
embrasures are V-shaped valleys between adjacent [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teeth).

Enameloid, also known as durodentine or vitrodentine, is an [enamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_enamel)-like [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) found in [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish).
endocardium (: endocardia) is the innermost layer of [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) that lines the chambers of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart).
endocast is the internal cast of a hollow object, often referring to the [cranial vault](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranial_vault) in the study of brain development in humans and other organisms.

media.file: Australopithecus africanus - Cast of taung child.jpg

definition: endocochlear potential (EP; also called endolymphatic potential) is the positive voltage of 80-100mV seen in the cochlear endolymphatic spaces.

endocranium in [comparative anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparative_anatomy) is a part of the [skull base](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Base_of_skull) in [vertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrates) and it represents the basal, inner part of the [cranium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranium).
Endocytosis is a [cellular process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_process) in which [substances](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_substance) are brought into the cell.
endolymphatic sac is a structure in the [inner ear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_ear).

Endometrial cups form during pregnancy in [mare](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mare)s and are the source of [equine chorionic gonadotropin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equine_chorionic_gonadotropin) (eCG) and a placenta-associated structure, which is derived from the [fetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetus).
Endoplasm, also known as entoplasm, generally refers to the inner (often granulated), dense part of a cell's [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm).

media.file: Collection Penard MHNG Specimen 40-1-4 Amoeba terricola.tif

definition: endostyle is an [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(biology)) found in [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate) [chordate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chordate) species of [tunicate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunicate)s and [lancelet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lancelet)s, and in the larval stage of [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) [lamprey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamprey)s.

endothoracic fascia is the layer of loose [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) deep to the [intercostal spaces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intercostal_spaces) and [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib)s, separating these structures from the underlying [pleura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_pleurae).
entepicondylar foramen is an opening in the distal (far) end of the [humerus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humerus) (upper arm bone) present in some [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.

enteric nervous system (ENS) is one of the three divisions of the [autonomic nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomic_nervous_system) (ANS), the others being the [sympathetic nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sympathetic_nervous_system) (SNS) and [parasympathetic nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasympathetic_nervous_system) (PSNS).

Enterochromaffin (EC) cells (also known as Kulchitsky cells) are a type of [enteroendocrine cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Enteroendocrine_cell), and [neuroendocrine cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroendocrine_cell).

definition: entoglossus is an elongated [bony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) [process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Process_(anatomy)) in [lizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lizard)s and [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s that projects from the body of the [hyoid apparatus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyoid_apparatus) into the [tongue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tongue).
entotympanic is a bone found in the ear region of many [placental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placentalia) [mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal).

definition: epidermis is the outermost of the three major layers that constitute the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin), the inner layers being the [dermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermis) and [hypodermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subcutaneous_tissue).

epidermis is an [epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium) (sheet of [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))) that covers the body of a [eumetazoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eumetazoa)n ([animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) more complex than a [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge)).
epigyne or epigynum is the external genital structure of female [spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider)s.

Epipophyses are bony projections of the [cervical vertebrae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cervical_vertebrae) found in [archosauromorphs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archosauromorpha), particularly [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur)s (including some basal [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s).

Epipubic bones are a pair of bones projecting forward from the [pelvic bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvis) of modern [marsupials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsupials), [monotremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monotremes) and fossil mammals like [multituberculates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multituberculata), and even [basal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basal_(phylogenetics)) [eutheria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eutheria)ns (the ancestors of [placental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placental)s, who lack them).

Epiretinal membrane or macular pucker is a disease of the eye in response to changes in the [vitreous humor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitreous_humor) or more rarely, [diabetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diabetes).
Episternal ossicles (or suprasternal ossicles) are small bones that are sometimes present at the upper end of the chest bone.

epitrochleoanconeus muscle (anconeous epitrochlearis muscle, anconeus-epitrochlearis or anconeus sextus) is a small [accessory muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accessory_muscle) of the [arm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arm) which runs from the back of the inner condyle of the [humerus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humerus) over the [ulnar nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulnar_nerve) to the [olecranon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olecranon).

definition: Equinalysis is a [computer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer) [software](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software) program designed to capture and analyse [equine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equine) [locomotion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_locomotion) by visually tracking and quantifying biomechanical data.

definition: equine eye is one of the largest of any land mammal.

Erectile tissue is tissue in the body with numerous vascular spaces, or [cavernous tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavernous_tissue), that may become engorged with [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood).
Ergastic substances are non-[protoplasmic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protoplasmic) materials found in [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

ergot is a small [callosity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Callosity) (Calcar metacarpeum and Calcar metatarseum) on the underside of the [fetlock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetlock) of a [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) or other [equine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equine).

Euthyneury is a [plesiomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symplesiomorphy) condition present in some [gastropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropoda) which is a result of two evolutionary events.
Evelyn tables are a set of four [[Embalming#For anatomy education|anatomical preparations]] on wooden boards that are thought to be the oldest anatomical preparations in Europe.

evolution of mammalian auditory ossicles was an [evolution](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution)ary process that resulted in the formation of the [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)ian [middle ear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_ear), where the three middle ear bones or [ossicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ossicles), namely the [incus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Incus), [malleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malleus) and [stapes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stapes) (a.k.a.

definition: excretory system is a passive biological system that removes excess, unnecessary materials from the [body fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_fluid)s of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism), so as to help maintain internal chemical [homeostasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homeostasis) and prevent damage to the body.

exfoliation describes the natural process of [bark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bark_(botany)) peeling or otherwise separating from a [tree trunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree_trunk), typically in large strips or plates that remain partially attached to the trunk until such time as they are completely detached by the elements or the eventual and subsequent exfoliation of additional layers of bark.
Exophers are a type of membrane-bound [extracellular vesicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_vesicle) (EV) that are released by budding out of cells into the extracellular space.
Extensor digitorum brevis manus is an extra or [accessory muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accessory_muscle) on the backside (dorsum) of the [hand](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hand).

extensor retinaculum (dorsal carpal ligament, or posterior annular ligament) is but a thickening of the [antebrachial fascia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antebrachial_fascia) (deep fascia of forearm) that holds the [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon)s of the [extensor muscles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_extensors_of_the_human_body) in place.

definition: External gills are the [gill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill)s of an animal, most typically an amphibian, that are exposed to the environment, rather than set inside the [pharynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharynx) and covered by [gill slit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill_slit)s, as they are in most [fishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishes).
External lamina is a structure similar to [basal lamina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basal_lamina) that surrounds the [sarcolemma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcolemma) of muscle cells.
external limiting membrane (or outer limiting membrane) is one of the ten distinct layers of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye).

Extracellular space refers to the part of a [multicellular organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism) outside the [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), usually taken to be outside the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane)s, and occupied by fluid.

Extracellular vesicles (EVs) are [lipid bilayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid_bilayer)-delimited particles that are naturally released from almost all types of [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

exuviae are the remains of an [exoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoskeleton) and related structures that are left after [ecdysozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecdysozoa)ns (including [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s, [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s and [arachnid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arachnid)s) have [molted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecdysis).

eyespot (sometimes ocellus) is an [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye)-like marking.

fabella is a small [sesamoid bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sesamoid_bone) found in some mammals embedded in the [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon) of the lateral head of the [gastrocnemius muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrocnemius_muscle) behind the lateral [condyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condyle_(anatomy)) of the [femur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femur).

FaceFX is a [facial animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_animation) software developed by OC3 Entertainment.

facial disc is the concave collection of [feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feather)s on the face of some [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s—most notably [owl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Owl)s—surrounding the eyes.

definition: fascicle is a bundle of [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf) or flowers growing crowded together; alternatively the term might refer to the [vascular tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_tissue)s that supply such an organ with nutrients.

definition: fasciculus retroflexus (FR) also known as the habenulointerpeduncular tract is a bundle of fibers located at the base of the [midbrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midbrain) in [vertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrates).

fasciole in [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s refers to a band or ribbon-like structure that is often seen as a flattened, slightly depressed area on the [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc_shell), formed by the successive growth lines on the edges of a canal.
Fat body is a highly dynamic insect [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) composed primarily of [storage cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adipocyte).

fauces (also termed the isthmus of fauces or oropharyngeal isthmus) is the opening at the back of the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth) into the [throat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throat).

FDI World Dental Federation notation (also called FDI notation or ISO3950 notation) is the world's most commonly used [dental notation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dental_notation) (tooth numbering system).

Feathering or feather is the long hair on the lower legs of some [breeds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_horse_breeds) of [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) and [pony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pony).
Feature scales are enlarged scales found on various reptiles.

page: Federative International Programme on Anatomical Terminology
definition: Federative International Programme for Anatomical Terminology (FIPAT) is a group of experts who review, analyze, and discuss the terms of the [morphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) structures of the human body.
femoral canal is the medial (and smallest) compartment of the three compartments of the [femoral sheath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femoral_sheath).

femoral gland is a specialised [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland) found in some male [frog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frog)s that plays a role in [chemical communication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemical_communication) and reproductive signalling.

Femoral pores are a part of a [holocrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holocrine) [secretory gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretory_gland) found on the inside of the thighs of certain [lizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lizard)s and [amphisbaenian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphisbaenian)s which releases [pheromone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pheromone)s to attract mates or mark territory.

femoral ring is the opening at the proximal, abdominal end of the [femoral canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femoral_canal), ==See also== * [Femoral canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femoral_canal) * [Femoral hernia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femoral_hernia) * [Inguinal canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inguinal_canal) ==References== ==External links== * [[Category:Lower limb anatomy]] 0lsclch2q84rzemgwl7xcqmq7yl8is7

femoral sheath (also called the crural sheath) is a funnel-shaped downward extension of [abdominal fascia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominal_fascia) within which the [femoral artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femoral_artery) and [femoral vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femoral_vein) pass between the [abdomen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdomen) and the [thigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thigh).
femoral triangle (or Scarpa's triangle) is an anatomical region of the upper third of the [thigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thigh).

fenestra (fenestration; : fenestrae or fenestrations) is any small opening or pore, commonly used as a term in the [biological sciences](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology).
Fern sports are plants that show marked change from the normal type or parent stock as a result of mutation.

definition: Fetlock is the common name in [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse)s, large animals, and sometimes dogs for the [metacarpophalangeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metacarpophalangeal) and [metatarsophalangeal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metatarsophalangeal) [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint)s (MCPJ and MTPJ).

fibrous tunic of the bulb of the eye; the sclera is opaque, and constitutes the posterior five-sixths of the [tunic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunic); the cornea is transparent, and forms the anterior sixth.

fibular retinacula (also known as peroneal retinacula) are fibrous retaining bands that bind down the tendons of the [fibularis longus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibularis_longus) and [fibularis brevis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibularis_brevis) muscles as they run across the side of the [ankle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankle).

definition: fin is a thin appendage or component attached to a larger body or structure.
fingerprint is an impression left by the [friction ridge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Friction_ridge)s of a human [finger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finger).

Fish bone is any [bony tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bony_tissue) in a [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish), although in common usage the term refers specifically to delicate parts of the non-[vertebral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebral) skeleton of such as [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib)s, [fin spine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_fin)s and intramuscular bones.

definition: Fish measurement is the measuring of individual fish and various parts of [their anatomies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_anatomy), for data used in many areas of [ichthyology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ichthyology), including [taxonomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taxonomy_(biology)) and [fishery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fishery) biology.
fish scale is a small rigid plate that grows out of the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin) of a fish.

fixation is the preservation of [biological tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_tissue)s from decay due to [autolysis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autolysis_(biology)) or [putrefaction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Putrefaction).

flail limb (also flail arm or flail leg) is a medical term which refers to an extremity in which the primary nerve has been severed or ceased to function, resulting in complete lack of mobility and sensation.

flank gland is one of several specialized caudolateral [glands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glands) (a group of glands located along the sides and the rear) found predominately in certain species of [rodents](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodents) including voles, shrews, hamsters, and other members of the family [Cricetidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricetidae).
Fleischner Society is an international, multidisciplinary medical society for thoracic radiology, dedicated to the diagnosis and treatment of diseases of the chest.

Flesh is any [aggregation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aggregation_(ethology)) of [soft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_tissue) [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology))s of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism).
floor plate is a structure integral to the developing [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system) of vertebrate organisms.

Fluorescence in situ hybridization (FISH) is a [molecular cytogenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytogenetics) technique that uses [fluorescent probes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hybridization_probe) that bind to specific parts of a [nucleic acid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleic_acid) sequence with a high degree of sequence [complementarity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Complementarity_(molecular_biology)).

definition: fold of the left vena cava, ligament of the left vena cava, or vestigial fold of Marshall, is a triangular fold of the serous [pericardium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pericardium) that lies between the left [pulmonary artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_artery) and subjacent [pulmonary vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_vein).
follicle is a small, spherical or vase-like group of cells enclosing a cavity in which some other structure grows or other material is contained.
Follicular drug delivery is a mechanism that enables the transport of therapeutic agents through the hair follicles present on the skin.

fontanelle (or fontanel) (colloquially, soft spot) is an [anatomical feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) of the infant [human skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_skull) comprising soft [membranous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane) gaps ([sutures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suture_(joint))) between the cranial bones that make up the [calvaria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calvaria_(skull)) of a [fetus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetus) or an [infant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infant).
Foramen cecum, in [dental anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dental_anthropology), is a minor expression of the [protostylid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protostylid) of the tooth.

foramen tympanicum, or also known as the foramen of Huschke, is an [anatomical variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_anatomical_variations) of the tympanic part of the [temporal bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temporal_bone) in humans resulting from a defect in normal [ossification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ossification) during the first five years of life.

Forcipules are the modified, pincer-like [front legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxilliped) of [centipede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Centipede)s that are used to inject [venom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom) into prey.

forearm is the region of the [upper limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_limb) between the [elbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbow-joint) and the [wrist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrist).

forelimb or front limb is one of the [paired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilateral_symmetry) [articulated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s ([limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limb_(anatomy))s) attached on the [cranial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranial) ([anterior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_(anatomy))) end of a [terrestrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrestrial_animal) [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod) [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)'s [torso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torso).
Forensic pathology is a field of medicine that focuses on determining the [cause of death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cause_of_death) by examining a corpse.

Fossa navicularis magna (also known as pharyngeal fossa or phyaryngeal fovela) is a variant bony depression found at the midline of the occipital part of [clivus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clivus_(anatomy)).

Foundational Model of Anatomy Ontology (FMA) is a reference [ontology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ontology_(computer_science)) for the domain of [human anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body).
fourth trochanter is a [shared characteristic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synapomorphy) common to [archosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archosaur)s.
fovea centralis is a small, central pit composed of closely packed [cones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cone_cell) in the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).

foveal avascular zone (FAZ) is a region within the [fovea centralis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fovea_centralis) at the centre of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of the human eye that is devoid of retinal blood vessels.

foveola is located within a region called the [macula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macula), a yellowish, cone photoreceptor filled portion of the human [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina).

Frederick Gymer Parsons [FRCS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FRCS) [FZS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fellow_of_the_Zoological_Society_of_London) (1863 – 11 March 1943) was a British writer and scientist, specialising in the fields of [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) and [anthropology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthropology).

frenulum (; , the [diminutive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diminutive) of ; ), ), is a small fold of [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) that secures the motion of a mobile [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) in the [body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body).

frenulum of labia minora (fourchette or posterior commissure of the labia minora) is a [frenulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frenulum) where the [labia minora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labia_minora) meet [posteriorly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_(anatomy)).
frog is a part of a [horse hoof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse_hoof), located on the underside, which should touch the ground if the horse is standing on soft footing.
frontal shield, also known as a facial shield or frontal plate, is a feature of the anatomy of several bird species.
Frontotemporal lobar degeneration (FTLD) is a pathological process that occurs in [frontotemporal dementia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontotemporal_dementia).

frozen section procedure is a [pathological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_pathology) [laboratory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_laboratory) procedure to perform rapid [microscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscope) analysis of a specimen.

definition: frustule is the hard and porous cell wall or external layer of [diatom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diatom)s.
fundiform ligament of the penis is a structure of the external genitalia whose descriptions differ according to the source consulted.

fundus of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) is the interior surface of the eye opposite the [lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lens_(anatomy)) and includes the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina), [optic disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optic_disc), [macula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macula), [fovea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fovea_centralis), and [posterior pole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_pole).

Funeral cosmetology, also known as mortuary makeup, restorative arts, mortuary cosmetology, or desairology, is a [cosmetological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cosmetology) art practiced on deceased human bodies to prepare for [viewing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viewing_(funeral)).

Fungal DNA barcoding is the process of identifying species of the [biological kingdom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingdom_(biology)) [Fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) through the [amplification](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polymerase_chain_reaction) and [sequencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_sequencing) of specific DNA sequences and their comparison with sequences deposited in a DNA barcode database such as the ISHAM reference database, == See also == * [DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_barcoding) * [Microbial DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microbial_DNA_barcoding) * [Pollen DNA barcoding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollen_DNA_barcoding) * [DNA barcoding in diet assessment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/DNA_barcoding_in_diet_assessment) * [Consortium for the Barcode of Life](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Consortium_for_the_Barcode_of_Life) == References == == Further reading == * == External links == * [http://www.aftol.org/primers.php Aftol primer listing] (as used in James et al.

fur is a [soft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Softness), thick growth of [hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair) that covers the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin) of almost all [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.
furcula, or furca is a forked, tail-like [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage).

Furstenberg's rosette is a structure in the [teat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teat) of cattle, sheep and other [ruminant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruminant)s, located at the internal end of the teat canal (also known as the streak canal or teat duct) at the junction with the [teat cistern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teat_cistern).

Gallic horse (Equus caballus gallicus) is a prehistoric [subspecies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subspecies) of [Equus caballus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equus_caballus) (the horse) that lived in the [Upper Paleolithic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upper_Paleolithic).

gametophyte () is one of the two [alternating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alternation_of_generations) [multicellular phases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism) in the life cycles of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

Gamna–Favre bodies are large, [intracytoplasmic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) [basophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basophilic) [inclusion bodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inclusion_bodies) seen in [endothelial cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endothelium) in patients with [lymphogranuloma venereum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymphogranuloma_venereum).

ganglion cell layer (ganglionic layer) is a layer of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) that consists of [retinal ganglion cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_ganglion_cell)s and displaced [amacrine cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amacrine_cell)s.

Gap junctions are [membrane channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_channel)s between adjacent [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) that allow the direct exchange of cytoplasmic substances, such as small molecules, substrates, and metabolites.
gasteroid fungi are a group of [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) in the [Basidiomycota](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiomycota).

Gastralia (: gastralium) are [dermal bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermal_bone)s found in the [ventral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_terms_of_location) body wall of modern [crocodilia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crocodilia)ns and [tuatara](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuatara), and many prehistoric [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod)s.
gastric mucosa is the [mucous membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucous_membrane) layer that lines the entire [stomach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stomach).

Gastrointestinal pathology is the subspecialty of [surgical pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgical_pathology) which deals with the [diagnosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis) and characterization of [neoplastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasia) and non-neoplastic [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease)s of the [digestive tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digestive_tract) and accessory organs, such as the [pancreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreas) and [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver).

gemma (English plural gemmas, Latin plural gemmae) is a single [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), or a mass of cells, or a modified bud of tissue, that detaches from the parent and develops into a new individual.

Gemmules are internal [buds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budding) found in [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_sponge)s and are involved in [asexual reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asexual_reproduction).

general senses are the [sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense)s which are perceived due to receptors scattered throughout the body such as touch, temperature, and hunger, rather than tied to a specific structure, as the [special senses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Special_senses) [vision](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_perception) or [hearing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hearing) are.
geniculum is a small [[wikt:genu|genu]], or angular [knee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee)-like structure.

genital hiatus is an [anthopometric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthopometric) measure of the [vulva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulva) defined as the distance between the [urethral meatus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urethral_meatus) and the posterior margin of the [hymen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymen).
genital papilla is an anatomical feature of the external [genitalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genitalia) of some animals.
germ pore is a small pore in the outer wall of a fungal [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore) through which the germ tube exits upon germination.
germ tube is an outgrowth produced by spores of spore-releasing [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) during [germination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germination).

Giant retinal ganglion cells are [photosensitive ganglion cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosensitive_ganglion_cell)s with large dendritic trees discovered in the [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human) and [macaque](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macaque) [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) by Dacey et al.

Gibson Plumage Index (GPI), sometimes known as the Gibson Code, is a system for describing the [plumage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plumage) of [great albatross](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_albatross)es.

gill () is a specialized [respiratory organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiration_organ) that many [aquatic animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_animal)s use for [aquatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_respiration) [gas exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_exchange), i.e.

Gill hyperplasia is a [medical condition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_diseases_and_parasites) consisting of the inflammation, [hyperplasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperplasia), or [hypertrophy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypertrophy) of gill tissue, caused by disease, poor water quality, or injury of the gills.

definition: Gill slits are individual openings to [gills](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gills), i.e., multiple gill arches, which lack a single outer cover.
Giovan Battista Verle was a 17th-century Italian instrument maker.

girdle is part of the [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) of a [chiton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiton), one class of marine [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s, the class [Polyplacophora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyplacophora).

gizzard, also referred to as the ventriculus, gastric mill, and gigerium, is an [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) found in the [digestive tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digestive_tract) of some animals, including [archosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archosaurs) ([bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s and other [dinosaurs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaurs), [crocodile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crocodile)s, [alligator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alligator)s, [pterosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pterosaur)s), [earthworm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Earthworm)s, some [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod)s, some [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish), and some [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s.

glabella, in [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s, is the area of skin between the [eyebrow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyebrow)s and above the [nose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_nose).
gland is defined functionally as a plant structure which secretes one or more products.

media.file: Origanum vulgare leave with water droplet, showing epistomatic stomata.jpg

definition: Glands of Zeis are unilobar [sebaceous gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebaceous_gland)s located on the margin of the [eyelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelid).
categories: Anatomy named for one who described it

definition: Glenolabral articular disruption (GLAD) lesion is a type of [shoulder injury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder_injury).
glenopolar angle (GPA) is a radiographical measurement used to assess the rotational alignment of the [glenoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenoid) relative to the scapula body.
globoid is a spherical crystalline inclusion in a protein body found in seed tissues that contains [phytate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phytic_acid) and other nutrients for plant growth.

glochidium (plural glochidia) is a microscopic [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva)l stage of some [freshwater mussel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater_mussel)s, [aquatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_animal) [bivalve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalve) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s in the families [Unionidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unionidae) and [Margaritiferidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Margaritiferidae), the river mussels and European freshwater pearl mussels.

glomerulus (: glomeruli) is a network of small blood vessels ([capillaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillaries)) known as a tuft, located at the beginning of a [nephron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephron) in the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney).

glomus body (or glomus organ; plural glomera) is a component of the [dermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermis) layer of the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin), involved in [body temperature regulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thermoregulation).
Glomus cells are the cell type mainly located in the [carotid bodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carotid_body) and [aortic bodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aortic_body).
