definition: acetabula) or hip socket is an opening in the formed by the , , and that is visible in lateral and medial views.

gluteal sulcus (also known as the gluteal fold, tuck, fold of the buttock, horizontal gluteal crease, or gluteal furrow) is an area of the body of [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s and anthropoid apes, described by a horizontal crease formed by the inferior aspect of the [buttocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buttocks) and the posterior upper [thigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thigh).

glycogen body is an oval structure in the [spinal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_cord) of [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s that is made of specialized [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) that contain large amounts of [glycogen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glycogen).

Gnathobases () are paired modified sections on the underside of the base of some [arthropod limbs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod_limb) (specifically on the basipod/basipodite, the basalmost segment which attaches directly to the body), used for food processing.

categories: Anatomy named for one who described it

definition: Golgi matrix is a collection of proteins involved in the structure and function of the [Golgi apparatus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golgi_apparatus).

Golgi tendon organ (GTO) (also known as Golgi organ, tendon organ, neurotendinous organ or neurotendinous spindle) is a skeletal muscle [stretch receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stretch_receptor) [proprioceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proprioceptor).
categories: Anatomy named for one who described it

definition: Gongylidia (singular gongylidium) are [hyphal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphal) swellings of fungus cultivated by higher-attine genera of [fungus-growing ants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus-growing_ants).
gonophore is a reproductive organ in members of the [Hydrozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hydrozoa) which produces [gamete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gamete)s.

media.file: EB1911 Hydromedusae - Structure of the Gonophore.jpg

definition: Gonopods are specialized [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s of various [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s used in reproduction or egg-laying.
gonopore, sometimes called a gonadopore, is a [genital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genital) pore in many [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate)s.
gorget ( ) is a patch of colored [feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feather)s found on the throat or upper breast of some species of [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s.
Gracility is slenderness, the condition of being gracile, which means slender.
Granulation tissue is new [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) and microscopic blood vessels that form on the surfaces of a wound during the healing process.
greater sciatic foramen is an opening ([[:wikt:foramen|foramen]]) in the posterior [human pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_pelvis).
Green leaf volatiles (GLV) are organic compounds released by plants.

grooming claw (or toilet claw) is the specialized [claw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claw) or [nail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy)) on the foot of certain [primate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primate)s, used for [personal grooming](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personal_grooming).
Gross anatomy is the study of [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) at the visible or [macroscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macroscopic) level.

Ground substance is an amorphous gel-like substance in the extracellular space of [animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animals) that contains all components of the [extracellular matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_matrix) (ECM) except for fibrous materials such as [collagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collagen) and [elastin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastin).
ground tissue of plants includes all tissues that are neither [dermal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(botany)) nor [vascular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_tissue).

Growing teeth is a [bioengineering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioengineering) technology with the ultimate goal to create new full [molars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molars) in a person or an animal.

Grueneberg ganglion (GG), also written as Grüneberg ganglion is an [olfactory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Olfactory) subsystem located at the entrance of the nasal cavity of [rodent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodent)s.

Guard hair or overhair is the outer layer of [hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair) of most [mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal), which overlay the [fur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fur).

media.file: Down Awn and guard hairs of cat 2012 11 13 9203r.JPG

definition: Gular skin (throat skin), in [ornithology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ornithology), is an area of [feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feather)less skin on birds that joins the lower [mandible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandible) of the [beak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beak) (or bill) to the bird's [neck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neck).

gums or gingiva (: gingivae) consist of the [mucosal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucosal) tissue that lies over the [mandible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandible) and [maxilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxilla) inside the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth).
Gynecologic pathology is the medical pathology subspecialty dealing with the study and diagnosis of disease involving the female genital tract.
Habit-tic deformity is a condition of the nail caused by external trauma to the [nail matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy)).
hair follicle is an [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) found in [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)ian [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin).
Hair plates are a type of [proprioceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Proprioception) found in the folds of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) joints.
Hair-pencils and coremata are [pheromone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pheromone) signaling structures present in [lepidoptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lepidoptera)n males.
hamus or hamulus is a structure functioning as, or in the form of, hooks or hooklets.

hand is a [prehensile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prehensile), multi-[finger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finger)ed appendage located at the end of the [forearm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forearm) or [forelimb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forelimb) of [primate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primate)s such as [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s, [chimpanzee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimpanzee)s, [monkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monkey)s, and [lemur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lemur)s.

hangnail is a small piece of [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_skin) or nail next to a [fingernail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy)) or [toenail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy)).

hard palate is a thin horizontal [bony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) plate made up of two bones of the [facial skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facial_skeleton), located in the roof of the mouth.

Harderian gland is a gland found within the eye's [orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy)) that occurs in [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod)s (reptiles, amphibians, birds and mammals) that possess a [nictitating membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nictitating_membrane).

media.file: Cave vertebrates of America; a study in degenerative evolution (1909) (20577823892).jpg

definition: Hardwood is [wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wood) from [flowering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowering_plant) (angiosperm) [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree)s.

Hartig net is the network of inward-growing [hypha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypha)e, that extends into the plant host [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root), penetrating between plant cells in the root epidermis and cortex in [ectomycorrhiza](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ectomycorrhiza)l symbiosis.

Hatschek's pit, not to be confused with Hatschek's nephridium, is a deep [ciliated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliated) [fossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossa_(anatomy)) on the [dorsal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorsum_(biology)) midline of the [buccal cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buccal_cavity) (the region of the gut behind the mouth).

definition: heart valve (cardiac valve) is a biological [one-way valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Check_valve) that allows [blood to flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_flow) in one direction through the chambers of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart).

Heater cells are specialized modified muscle cells located at the base of the brain in [billfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Billfish), including [swordfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Swordfish).
helicine arteries of penis are [arteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artery) in the [penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penis).

hematoxylin body, or LE body, is a dense, homogeneous, [basophilic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basophilic) particle, easily stainable with [[H peripheral glomerular loop: hhomogenous eosinophilic intracytoplasmic inclusions] [[Category:Anatomical pathology]] [[Category:Autoimmune diseases]] [[Category:Systemic connective tissue disorders]] amoanoa20rec2smh1f7n9l96fnm0p8d

Hemolymph or haemolymph is a [body fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_fluid) that circulates inside [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod) bodies transporting [nutrient](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrient)s and [oxygen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oxygen) to [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology))s, comparable with the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) in [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.

Hemorrhoidal artery embolization (HAE, or hemorrhoid embolization) is a non-surgical treatment of internal [hemorrhoids.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hemorrhoid) == References == == External links == * [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Whje31Jlm10 Hemorrhoidal artery embolization] [[Category:Interventional radiology]] [[Category:Anatomical pathology]] [[Category:Digestive system surgery]] iojxf8b0ryg5c1ht41u3oukshzv2

Henle's layer is the third and the outermost layer of the [inner root sheath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_root_sheath) of the [hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair) follicle, consisting of a single layer of [cubical cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cubical_cells) with clear flattened nuclei.

Henry's pocket, more formally known as a cutaneous marginal pouch, is a fold of skin forming an open pouch on the lower posterior part of the [external ear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/External_ear).

page: Hepatic branches of anterior vagal trunk

definition: Hepatic caecum or hepatic cecum is a name used in describing various physiological structures in some crustaceans, insects and lancelets.

hepatic diverticulum (or liver bud) is a primordial cellular extension of the embryonic [foregut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foregut) [endoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endoderm) that gives rise to the [parenchyma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parenchyma) of the [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver) and the [bile duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bile_duct).

Hepatic stellate cells (HSC), also known as perisinusoidal cells or Ito cells (earlier lipocytes or fat-storing cells), are [pericyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pericyte)s found in the [perisinusoidal space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perisinusoidal_space) of the [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver), also known as the space of Disse (a small area between the [sinusoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver_sinusoid)s and [hepatocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepatocyte)s).
hepatocyte is a cell of the main [parenchyma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parenchyma)l tissue of the [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver).
Herbert Henry Woollard, FRS (2 August 1889 – 18 January 1939) was an Australian academic, anatomist and army medical officer.
Herring bodies or neurosecretory bodies are structures found in the [posterior pituitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_pituitary).

Heterocrine glands (or composite glands) are the [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland)s which function as both [exocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exocrine_gland) and [endocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_gland).
Heterogonesis describes the segregation of parental genomes into distinct cell lineages in the dividing [zygote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zygote).
Heteronomous annulation is a characteristic of some [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s.
hiatus is a natural fissure in a structure.

hilum (; : hila), sometimes formerly called a hilus (; : hili), is a depression or fissure where structures such as [blood vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel)s and [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve)s enter an [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)).

hindlimb or back limb is one of the [paired](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bilateral_symmetry) [articulated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s ([limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limb_(anatomy))s) attached on the [caudal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caudal_(anatomical_term)) ([posterior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_(anatomy))) end of a [terrestrial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terrestrial_animal) [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod) [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)'s [torso](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torso).

Hip scoring is a procedure used to determine the degree of [hip dysplasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_dysplasia_(canine)) in [dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog)s and other animals and reporting the findings in a standard way.

Hippomanes ([Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) ἱππομανές) are brownish or olive-greenish, elastic formations that arise physiologically in female bovines and equines during pregnancy.
histochemical tracer is a compound used to reveal the location of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s and track [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)al projections.
Histogenesis is the formation of different [tissues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_tissue) from undifferentiated [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

Histopathology (compound of three [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) words: 'tissue', 'suffering', and [-logia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/-logy) 'study of') is the [microscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_microscope) examination of [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) in order to study the manifestations of [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease).

definition: history of the pineal gland is an account of the scientific development on the understanding of the [pineal gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pineal_gland) from the [ancient Greeks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greece) that led to the discovery of its [neuroendocrine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroendocrine_cell) properties in the 20th century CE.

hock, tarsus or uncommonly gambrel, is the region formed by the [tarsal bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarsus_(skeleton)) connecting the [tibia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tibia) and [[Equine anatomy#Cannon|metatarsus]] of a [digitigrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digitigrade) or [unguligrade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ungulate) [quadrupedal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrupedal) mammal, such as a [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse), [cat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cat), or [dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog).
Holochroal eyes are [compound eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compound_eyes) with many tiny lenses (sometimes more than 15,000, each 30-100μm, rarely larger).

Holoptic refers to one of the ways in which the [arthropod eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod_eye) develops, particularly the [eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compound_eye) of various species of insects.

Hominoid Personality Questionnaire (also: HPQ) is a [personality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Personality) rating instrument used for [non-human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Non-human) [primate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primate)s.

Homogenization, in [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology) or [molecular biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molecular_biology), is a process whereby different fractions of a biological sample become equal in composition.
homotopic connectivity is the connectivity between mirror areas of the [human brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain) [hemispheres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerebral_hemisphere).

hoof (: hooves or hoofs) is the tip of a [toe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toe) of an [ungulate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ungulate) [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal), which is covered and strengthened with a thick and horny [keratin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keratin) covering.

Horizontal transfer of mitochondria is the movement of whole [mitochondria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondria) and [mitochondrial DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrial_DNA) between cells.

Hormogonia are motile filaments of cells formed by some [cyanobacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyanobacteria) in the order [Nostocales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nostocales) and [Stigonematales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stigonematales).

horn is a permanent pointed projection on the head of various animals that consists of a covering of [keratin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keratin) and other [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s surrounding a core of live [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone).

definition: horse body mass is highly variable, depending on [breed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breed), model, physiological state, condition, owner's purpose and usage of the animal.
horse hoof is the lower extremity of each leg of a [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse), the part that makes contact with the ground and carries the weight of the animal.

definition: Horse teeth refers to the [dentition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dentition) of equine species, including [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse)s and [donkey](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donkey)s.
horse tongue is an organ that is part of the equine [[Equine anatomy#Digestive system|digestive system]].

definition: Horseshoe kidney, also known as ren arcuatus (in Latin), renal fusion or super kidney, is a [congenital disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congenital_disorder) affecting about 1 in 500 people that is more common in men, often asymptomatic, and usually diagnosed incidentally.

human back, also called the dorsum (: dorsa), is the large [posterior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_(anatomy)) area of the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body), rising from the top of the [buttock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buttock)s to the back of the [neck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neck).
human body is the entire structure of a [human being](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human).

human digestive system consists of the [gastrointestinal tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrointestinal_tract) plus the accessory organs of digestion (the [tongue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tongue), [salivary gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salivary_gland)s, [pancreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreas), [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver), and [gallbladder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gallbladder)).

human leg is the [lower limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leg) of the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body), including the [thigh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thigh), [knee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee), [lower leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crus_(lower_leg)), [ankle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankle), [foot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foot), or sometimes even the [hip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip) or [buttock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buttock) region.
human nose is the first organ of the [respiratory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system).

definition: human skeleton is the internal framework of the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body).

definition: human skin is the outer covering of the body and is the largest organ of the [integumentary system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Integumentary_system).

humeroradial joint is the [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) between the [head of the](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head_of_the_radius) [radius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radius_(bone)) and the [capitulum of the](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capitulum_of_the_humerus) [humerus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humerus), is a limited [ball-and-socket joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ball-and-socket_joint), hinge type of [synovial joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_joint).

Hunter-Schreger bands, commonly abbreviated as HSB, are features of the [enamel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_enamel) of the [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) in [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s, mostly [placental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placental)s.

HuS-E/2 cells are [immortalized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immortalised_cell_line) primary human [hepatocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepatocyte)s that were isolated from the discarded old [liver tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver_tissue) obtained from a 9-year-old male patient with primary [hyperoxaluria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperoxaluria) (after the approval of ethical committee and required written consent) who had undergone [liver transplantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver_transplantation) to receive a new liver.

Huxley's layer is the middle layer of the [inner root sheath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_root_sheath) of the [hair follicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_follicle), situated between [Henle's layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Henle's_layer) (outermost) and the [IRS cuticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuticle_(hair)) (innermost).

hymenium is the fertile, [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore)-bearing tissue layer of many fungal [fruiting bodies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruiting_body).

hymenophore refers to the [hymenium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymenium)-bearing structure of a [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) [fruiting body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruiting_body).
hyoid apparatus is the collective term used in veterinary anatomy for the bones which suspend the tongue and [larynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larynx).

definition: Hyperthecosis, or ovarian hyperthecosis, is [hyperplasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyperplasia) of the [theca interna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Theca_interna) of the [ovary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovary).
Hypertrophy is an increase in the size of individual [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

hypha (; ) is a long, branching, filamentous structure of a [fungus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus), [oomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oomycete), or [actinobacterium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actinobacterium).

hypobranchial gland is a [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland)ular structure which is part of the anatomy of many [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s, including several different families of [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod)s, and also many [protobranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protobranchia) [bivalves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalvia).
hypocotyl (short for This rate is highest when plants are kept in darkness mediated by a process called skotomorphogenesis, which contrasts photomorphogenesis.

hypophyseal portal system is a system of [blood vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessels) in the [microcirculation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microcirculation) at the base of the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain), connecting the [hypothalamus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothalamus) with the [anterior pituitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_pituitary).

Hypoplasia (; adjective form hypoplastic) is underdevelopment or incomplete development of a [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) or [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(biology)).
hyposphene-hypantrum articulation is an accessory joint found in the vertebrae of several fossil reptiles of the group [Archosauromorpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archosauromorpha).

hypostome (also called the [maxilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxilla), [radula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radula), or [labium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labium_(insect))) is a [calcified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osseous_tissue) harpoon-like structure near the mouth area of certain [parasitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitism) [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s including [tick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tick)s, that allows them to anchor themselves firmly in place on a [host](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Host_(biology)) vertebrate while sucking [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood).

hypothalamic–pituitary–gonadal axis (HPG axis, also known as the hypothalamic–pituitary–testicular/ovarian axis) refers to the [hypothalamus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothalamus), [pituitary gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pituitary_gland), and [gonadal glands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonad) as if these individual [endocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_gland)s were a single entity.

hypothalamus (: hypothalami; ) is a small part of the [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) that contains a number of [nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleus_(neuroanatomy)) with a variety of functions.
hypothallus is the layer on which the fruit body sits, lying in contact with the substrate.

iClone is a [real-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_computing) [3D](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/3D_computer_graphics) [animation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_animation) and [rendering](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rendering_(computer_graphics)) software program.

definition: crest of the ilium (or iliac crest) is the superior border of the [wing of ilium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wing_of_ilium) and the superolateral margin of the [greater pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greater_pelvis).

iliopectineal bursa or the iliopsoas bursa is a large [synovial bursa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_bursa) that separates the external surface of the [hip joint capsule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capsule_of_hip_joint) from the tendon of the [iliopsoas muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iliopsoas_muscle).
iliotibial tract or iliotibial band (ITB; also known as Maissiat's band or the IT band) is a longitudinal fibrous reinforcement of the [fascia lata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascia_lata).

imaginal disc is one of the parts of a [holometabolous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holometabolism) [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva) that will become a portion of the outside of the [adult insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imago) during the [pupal transformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pupal_transformation) to the [imago](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Imago).

definition: imperforate hymen is a [congenital disorder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Congenital_disorder) where a [hymen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymen) without an opening completely obstructs the [vagina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vagina).

in silico clinical trial, also known as a virtual clinical trial, is an individualized [computer simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_simulation) used in the development or regulatory evaluation of a [medicinal product](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medicinal_product), [device](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_device), or intervention.

in-ovo sexing is method for [determining the sex of a chick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chick_sexing) while it is still [in ovo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_ovo) ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) for This allows hatcheries to use the combined solution without any upfront investment just based on a performance fee per egg.

page: Inferior extensor retinaculum of the foot
definition: inferior extensor retinaculum of the foot (cruciate crural ligament, lower part of anterior annular ligament) is a Y-shaped band placed in front of the [ankle-joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankle-joint), the stem of the Y being attached laterally to the upper surface of the [calcaneus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcaneus), in front of the depression for the [interosseous talocalcaneal ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interosseous_talocalcaneal_ligament); it is directed medialward as a double layer, one lamina passing in front of, and the other behind, the tendons of the [peroneus tertius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peroneus_tertius) and [extensor digitorum longus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extensor_digitorum_longus).

inferior frontal junction area (IFJ) is an area of the brain located at the junction of the [inferior frontal sulcus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inferior_frontal_sulcus) and the inferior [precentral sulcus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Precentral_sulcus).

inferior ligament of the epididymis is a strand of fibrous tissue which is covered by a reflection of the [tunica vaginalis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunica_vaginalis) and connects the lower aspect of the [epididymis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epididymis) with the [testis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testis).
inferior rectus muscle is a [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle) in the [orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy)) near the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).

term: Inferior transverse ligament of the tibiofibular syndesmosis
page: Inferior transverse ligament of the tibiofibular syndesmosis
definition: inferior transverse ligament of the [tibiofibular syndesmosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inferior_tibiofibular_articulation) is a [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) structure in the lower leg that lies in front of the [posterior ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_ligament_of_the_lateral_malleolus).

Infraclavicular fossa is an indentation, or fossa, immediately below the [clavicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavicle), above the third rib and between the [deltoid muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deltoid_muscle) laterally and [medioclavicular line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medioclavicular_line) medially.

inframammary fold (IMF), inframammary crease or inframammary line is the natural lower boundary of the [breast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast); the place where the breast and the [chest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chest) meet.
infraorbital vein is a vein that drains structures of the floor of the orbit.

definition: infundibulum of a tooth is the funnel-like center that is filled with cementum.
Inguinal lymph nodes are [lymph node](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymph_node)s in the [groin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Groin).

Injection of vinylite and corrosion is an [anatomical technique](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_technique) used to visualize branching and pathways of the [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system).

definition: inner nuclear layer or layer of inner granules, of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina), is made up of a number of closely packed cells, of which there are three varieties: [bipolar cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina_bipolar_cell)s, [horizontal cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horizontal_cell)s, and [amacrine cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amacrine_cell)s.

inner plexiform layer is an area of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) that is made up of a dense reticulum of [fibrils](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibrils) formed by interlaced [dendrites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dendrites) of [retinal ganglion cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_ganglion_cells) and cells of the [inner nuclear layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_nuclear_layer).

inner root sheath or internal root sheath of the hair follicle is located between the [outer root sheath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Outer_root_sheath) and the [hair shaft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_shaft).

definition: Scales are present on the bodies of various insects.

Insect wings are adult outgrowths of the [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) [exoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoskeleton) that enable [insects to fly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_flight).

integument is the tissue surrounding an organism's body or an organ within, such as [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin), a [husk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Husk), [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoskeleton), germ or [rind](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peel_(fruit)).

integumentary system is the set of organs forming the outermost layer of an animal's body, comprising the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin), [hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair), [scales](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scale_(zoology)), [feathers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feathers), [hooves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hoof), [claw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claw)s, and [nails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy)).

Interactive skeleton-driven simulation (or Interactive skeleton-driven dynamic deformations) is a scientific [computer simulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computer_simulation) technique used to approximate realistic physical [deformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deformation_(engineering))s of dynamic bodies in [real-time](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Real-time_computing).

interatrial sulcus, separating the two [atria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atrium_(heart)), is scarcely marked on the posterior surface, while anteriorly it is hidden by the [pulmonary artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_artery) and [aorta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aorta).
Intercalated discs or lines of Eberth are microscopic identifying features of [cardiac muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle).
interclavicle is a bone which, in most [tetrapods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapods), is located between the [clavicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavicles).

intercuneiform joints are the [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint)s (articulations among) the [cuneiform bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuneiform_bones).

interdental plate refers to the [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)-filled [mesial-distal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_terms_of_location) region between the [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth).
Interdigital webbing refers to the presence of skin membranes.
interlobar arteries are vessels of the [renal circulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_circulation) which supply the [renal lobes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_lobes).
interlobar veins are veins of the [renal circulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_circulation) which drain the [renal lobes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_lobes).
intermembral index is a [ratio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ratio) used to compare limb proportions, expressed as a [percentage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Percentage).
intermembrane space (IMS) is the space occurring between or involving two or more membranes.

internal limiting membrane, or inner limiting membrane, is the boundary between the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) and the [vitreous body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitreous_body), formed by [astrocytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Astrocytes) and the end feet of [Müller cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muller_glia).
Interoception is the collection of [[Sense#Other internal sensations and perceptions|senses]] providing information to the organism about the internal state of the body.

interosseous membrane of the forearm (rarely middle or intermediate radioulnar joint) is a fibrous sheet that connects the interosseous margins of the [radius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radius_(bone)) and the [ulna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulna).

Intersex is a general term for an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) that has [sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex) characteristics that are between [male](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male) and [female](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female).

interspinales are short [muscle fascicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle_fascicle)s, found in pairs between the spinous processes of the contiguous [vertebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebra)e, one on either side of the [interspinal ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interspinal_ligament).
interspinous plane (Planum interspinale) is an anatomical [transverse plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transverse_plane) that passes through the anterior superior iliac spines.

interstitium is a [[wikt:contiguity|contiguous]] fluid-filled space existing between a structural barrier, such as a [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane) or the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin), and internal structures, such as [organs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)), including [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle)s and the [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system).

intertemporal bone is a paired [cranial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) bone present in certain [sarcopterygians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcopterygii) (lobe-finned fish) and extinct [amphibian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibian)-[grade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolutionary_grade) [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod)s.

intervenous tubercle (tubercle of Lower) is a small projection on the posterior wall of the [right atrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Atrium_(heart)), above the [fossa ovalis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossa_ovalis_(heart)).

interventricular septum (IVS, or ventricular septum, or during development septum inferius) is the stout wall separating the [ventricles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventricle_(heart)), the lower chambers of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart), from one another.

intimate part, personal part, or private part, is a place on the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) which is customarily kept covered by [clothing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clothing) in public venues and conventional settings, as a matter of [fashion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fashion) and [cultural norms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cultural_norms).
Intracellular space is the interior space of the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane).
intrascleral plexus is the network of [blood vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel)s within the substance of the [sclera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclera).
introitus is an entrance into a canal or hollow [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)).

intromittent organ is any external organ of a [male](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male) organism that is specialized to deliver sperm during [copulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copulation_(zoology)).

Intubation granuloma is a benign growth of [granulation tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granuloma) in the larynx or trachea, which arises from tissue trauma due to [endotracheal intubation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tracheal_intubation).

Invadopodia are [actin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actin)-rich protrusions of the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane) that are associated with degradation of the [extracellular matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_matrix) in cancer invasiveness and metastasis.

ionocyte (formerly called a chloride cell) is a [mitochondrion-rich](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitochondrion) [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) within ionoregulatory organs of animals, such as [teleost](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teleost) [fish gill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_gill), insect Malpighian tubules, crustacean gills, antennal glands and maxillary glands, and copepod Crusalis organs.
isidium (plural: isidia) is a tiny, wart- or finger-like outgrowth on the [thallus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thallus) surface of certain [lichen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichen) species.

Isolated organ perfusion technique is employed to precipitate an organ's perfusion and circulation that are independent/isolated from the body's systemic circulation for various purposes such as organ-localized [chemotherapy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemotherapy), organ-targeted delivery of drug, gene or anything else, [organ transplantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_transplantation), and organ injury recovery.

lacrimal apparatus is the physiological system containing the [orbital](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy)) structures for [tear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tears) production and drainage.

lacrimal canaliculi (: canaliculus) are the small channels in each [eyelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelid) that drain lacrimal fluid, from the [lacrimal puncta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacrimal_punctum) to the [lacrimal sac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacrimal_sac).

lacrimal caruncle, or caruncula lacrimalis, is the small, pink, globular nodule at the inner corner (the medial [canthus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canthus)) of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).
lacrimal gland is to the upper left.

lacrimal lake is the pool of [tears](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tears) in the lower [conjunctiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunctiva)l cul-de-sac, which drains into the opening of the tear drainage system (the [puncta lacrimalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puncta_lacrimalia)).

lacrimal punctum (: puncta) or lacrimal point is a minute opening on the summits of the [lacrimal papilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacrimal_papilla)e, seen on the margins of the [eyelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelid)s at the lateral extremity of the [lacrimal lake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacrimal_lake).

Lactiferous ducts are ducts that converge and form a [[Morphogenesis#Branching morphogenesis|branched system]] connecting the [nipple](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nipple) to the [lobules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lobules) of the [mammary gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammary_gland).
lacuna magna (also called Guérin's sinus) is the largest of several recesses in the roof of the [navicular fossa of the male urethra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navicular_fossa_of_male_urethra).

lamella (: lamellae), or gill, is a papery [hymenophore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymenophore) rib under the cap of some [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom) species, most often [agaric](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agaric)s.
lamella is a thin plate-like structure, often one amongst many lamellae very close to one another, with open space between.

lamella (: lamellae) in [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology) refers to a thin layer, [membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane) or plate of [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)).
lamella (plural: lamellae) is a specific type of fold or tooth located on the inner boundary of the [aperture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aperture_(mollusc)).

lamellar bodies (otherwise known as lamellar granules, membrane-coating granules (MCGs), keratinosomes or Odland bodies) are secretory [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle)s found in [type II alveolar cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alveolar_cell) in the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s, and in [keratinocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keratinocyte)s in the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin).

Lamellodiscs are epidermal structures, which are typical of and found only in certain [monogenea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monogenea)ns of the family [Diplectanidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diplectanidae).
Lameness is an abnormal [gait](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gait) or stance of an animal that is the result of dysfunction of the [locomotor system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_locomotion).

Lamina is a general [anatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) term meaning * The [lamina affixa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamina_affixa): a layer of [epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium) growing on the surface of the [thalamus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thalamus).
lamina is the most peripheral [neuropil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuropil) of the [insect visual system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_visual_system).

lamina limitans is the innermost surface of the dentinal tubule (that exist in [dentin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dentin)) that lies in intimate contact with the long process of the [odontoblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odontoblast).

lamina lucida is a component of the [basement membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basement_membrane) which is found between the epithelium and underlying connective tissue (e.g., [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis) and [dermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermis) of the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin)).

Lamina monopolar cells are a class of neurons in the most peripheral [neuropil](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuropil) of the [arthropod visual system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod_visual_system), the [lamina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamina_(neuropil)).

lamina propria is a thin layer of [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) that forms part of the moist linings known as mucous membranes or [mucosae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucosae), which line various tubes in the body, such as the [respiratory tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_tract), the [gastrointestinal tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrointestinal_tract), and the [urogenital tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urogenital_tract).
lanceolate ending is a [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron) ending that wraps around a [hair follicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_follicle).

media.file: The representation of Langerhans cells in the Cell Ontology.jpg

definition: lap is a surface (usually horizontal) created between the [knee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee) and [hips](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_(anatomy)) of a [biped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biped) when it is in a seated or lying down position.

Large deformation diffeomorphic metric mapping (LDDMM) is a specific suite of algorithms used for diffeomorphic mapping and manipulating dense imagery based on diffeomorphic metric mapping within the academic discipline of [computational anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Computational_anatomy), to be distinguished from its precursor based on diffeomorphic mapping.

large intestine, also known as the large bowel, is the last part of the [gastrointestinal tract](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrointestinal_tract) and of the [digestive system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digestion) in [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod)s.

largest body part is either the largest given body part across all living and extinct organisms or the largest example of a [body part](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_plan) within an existing [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species).
laryngeal saccules are soft tissue masses that are extensions of the [laryngeal ventricles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Laryngeal_ventricle) in the [larynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larynx).
lateral costotransverse ligament is a short, thick, though ==References== [[Category:Thorax (human anatomy)]] [[Category:Back anatomy]] [[Category:Ligaments]] 94zesylw7e41m0w8q6nhrdoyol4if4x

lateral epicondyle of the humerus is a large, [tuberculated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tubercle_(anatomy)) eminence, curved a little forward, and giving attachment to the [radial collateral ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radial_collateral_ligament_of_elbow_joint) of the [elbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbow) joint, and to a [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon) common to the origin of the [supinator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Supinator) and some of the extensor muscles.

Lateral hearts, also known as pseudohearts or commissural vessels, are blood vessels on either side of the alimentary canal of some [annelids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annelids) that pump blood from the dorsal vessel to the ventral vessel.

lateral horn (lateral [protocerebrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protocerebrum)) is one of the two areas of the [insect brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_brain) where projection neurons of the [antennal lobe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antennal_lobe) send their [axon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axon)s.
lateral palpebral raphe is a ligamentous band near the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).

Lateral recess of fourth ventricle (also known as the lateral recess), is a paired extension of the [fourth ventricle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fourth_ventricle) of the brain that projects laterally towards the [pontomedullary junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pontomedullary_junction), reaching the lateral border of the [brainstem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brainstem).

lateral rectus muscle is a [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle) on the lateral side of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) in the [orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy)).
laterality refers to asymmetric preference, usage, skill, or specialization of symmetric body parts in an organism.

laticifer is a type of elongated secretory cell found in the [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf) and/or stems of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s that produce [latex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latex) and [rubber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rubber) as [secondary metabolites](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_metabolites).
Laurer's canal is a part of the reproductive system of [trematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trematode)s, analogous to the [vagina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vagina).

layer of rods and cones (Jacob's membrane) in the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye) are of two kinds, [rod cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rod_cell)s and [cone cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cone_cell)s, the former being much more numerous than the latter except in the [macula lutea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macula_lutea).
leaf gap is a space in the stem of a plant through which the leaf grows.

Leaf plastocron index is a measure of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) [leaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf) age based on [morphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) development (the [plastochron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastochron)).

Learned non-use of a [limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limb_(anatomy)) is a learning phenomenon whereby movement is suppressed initially due to adverse reactions and failure of any activity attempted with the affected limb, which then results in the suppression of behavior.
left atrioventricular orifice (left atrioventricular opening or mitral orifice) is placed below and to the left of the [aortic orifice](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aortic_orifice).
left border of heart (or obtuse margin) is formed from the rounded lateral wall of the [left ventricle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Left_Ventricle).
left triangular ligament is a large [peritoneal fold](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritoneum).

left–right asymmetry (LR asymmetry) is the process in early [embryonic development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryonic_development) that [[Homochirality#Symmetry breaking|breaks the normal symmetry]] in the [[Symmetry#In biology|bilateral]] [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo).

leg is a [weight-bearing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Weight-bearing) and [locomotive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_locomotion) anatomical structure, usually having a [column](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Column)ar shape.
Leg hair is [body hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_hair) that grows on the legs of humans, generally appearing after the onset of [puberty](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puberty).

Theatrum Anatomicum or Leiden anatomical theatre was an [anatomical theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_theatre) and [cabinet of curiosities](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_curiosities) of [Leiden University](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leiden_University) that opened in [Leiden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leiden) in the Netherlands in 1594.
lens, or crystalline lens, is a transparent [biconvex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biconvex_lens) structure in most land vertebrate [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye)s.
lens capsule is a component of the [globe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Globe_(human_eye)) of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye).

lesion is any damage or abnormal change in the [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism), usually caused by [injury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Injury) or [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease)s.

levatores costarum (), twelve in number on either side, are small tendinous and fleshy bundles, which arise from the ends of the transverse processes of the seventh [cervical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cervical_vertebrae) and upper eleven [thoracic vertebrae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoracic_vertebrae).

definition: Leydig's organ (named after the German histologist [Franz Leydig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Franz_Leydig) who first described it in 1857) is a unique structure found only in some, but not all, [elasmobranchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elasmobranchii) ([shark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shark)s and [rays](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batoidea)).
Lillie's trichrome is a combination of dyes used in [histology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology).

definition: limbs of the [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) are structures made of dozens of [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)s, [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint)s, [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle)s, [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon)s, and [ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligament)s that support the weight of the equine body.

limbus vertebra is a [[Tubercle#Bones|bone tubercle]] formed by bone trauma on a [vertebral body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebral_body), bearing a radiographic similarity to a vertebral [fracture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fracture).

Linburg–Comstock variation is an occasional [tendinous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon) connection between the [flexor pollicis longus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flexor_pollicis_longus) and the [flexor digitorum profundus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flexor_digitorum_profundus) of the [index](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Index_finger), the [middle finger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Middle_finger) or both.
lines of non-extension are notional lines running across the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) along which body movement causes neither stretching or contraction.

definition: Lister's tubercle or dorsal tubercle of radius is a bony prominence located at the [distal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_terms_of_location) end of the [radius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radius_(bone)).
Liu's stain (劉氏染色法) is a staining technique used to stain animal cells.
Liver cytology is the branch of cytology that studies the liver cells and its functions.

liver segment is one of eight segments of the liver as described in the widely used Couinaud classification (named after [Claude Couinaud](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claude_Couinaud)) in the [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) of the [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver).

liver sinusoid is a type of [capillary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillary) known as a sinusoidal capillary, discontinuous capillary or sinusoid, that is similar to a [[Capillary#Fenestrated|fenestrated capillary]], having discontinuous [endothelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endothelium) that serves as a location for mixing of the oxygen-rich blood from the [hepatic artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepatic_artery) and the nutrient-rich blood from the [portal vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portal_vein).

Living Human Project (LHP) is a project that begun in 2002 to develop a distributed repository of anatomo-functional data and simulation algorithms for the human [musculoskeletal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musculoskeletal) apparatus used to create the [physiome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiome) of the human musculoskeletal system.

lobe is a clear anatomical division or extension [Interlobar duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interlobar_duct)s connect lobes and [interlobular duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interlobular_duct)s connect lobules.

media.file: Lobules and ducts of the breast.jpg

definition: lobules of liver, or hepatic lobules, are small divisions of the [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver) defined at the microscopic scale.

loins, or lumbus (: lumbi), are the sides between the lower [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib)s and [pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvis), and the lower part of the [back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Back).

London Burkers were a group of [body snatchers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_snatchers) operating in [London](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London), England, who apparently modeled their activities on the notorious [Burke and Hare murders](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burke_and_Hare_murders).

loreal pit is the deep depression, or fossa, in the [loreal area](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lore_(anatomy)) on either side of the head in [pit viper](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pit_viper)s (crotaline snakes).

love dart (also known as a gypsobelum, shooting darts, or just as darts) is a sharp, [calcareous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium_carbonate) or [chitin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitin)ous [dart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dart_(missile)) which some [hermaphroditic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hermaphroditic) [land snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_snail)s and [slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug)s create.

definition: lower-back tattoo, also known as tramp stamp, is a [tattoo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tattoo) on the [lower back](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_back) that became popular in the first decade of the 21st century, and gained a reputation for their [erotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Erotic) appeal.

lucky stone is actually the unique ear bone or [otolith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otolith) of a [freshwater drum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater_drum) ([Aplodinotus grunniens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aplodinotus_grunniens)), also known as the sheephead fish.

lumbocostal ligament is a fibrous band that crosses from the [twelfth rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Twelfth_rib) to the tips of the [transverse processes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transverse_processes) of the first and second [lumbar vertebrae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumbar_vertebrae).
lumen (: lumina) is the inside space of a tubular structure, such as an artery or intestine.
lungs are the primary [organs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(biology)) of the [respiratory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system) in many animals, including humans.
lunula (: lunulae; ) is the crescent-shaped whitish area of the bed of a [fingernail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fingernail) or [toenail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toenail).

lunule (from the Latin meaning small moon or crescent moon) is an anatomical feature which is found in the exterior surface of the shells of some species of clams, [bivalve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalve) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s, as for example in the family [Veneridae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veneridae) and in the genus [Ascetoaxinus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascetoaxinus).

lymphatic system, or lymphoid system, is an [organ system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_system) in [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s that is part of the [immune system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_system) and complementary to the [circulatory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Circulatory_system).
related: List of lymph nodes of the human body

definition: lymphatic vessels (or lymph vessels or lymphatics) are thin-walled vessels (tubes), structured like [blood vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel)s, that carry [lymph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymph).

Lymphopoiesis (lĭm'fō-poi-ē'sĭs) (or lymphocytopoiesis) is the generation of [lymphocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymphocyte)s, one of the five types of [white blood cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_blood_cell) (WBCs).

lysosome () is a membrane-bound [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle) that is found in all [animal cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_cell)s (except [red blood cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_blood_cell)s), and rarely in [plant cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell)s.

Maceration is a bone preparation technique whereby a clean [skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeleton) is obtained from a [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) carcass by leaving it to [decompose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decomposition) inside a closed container at near-constant temperature.
Macropinosomes are a type of [cellular compartment](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cellular_compartment) that form as a result of [[Pinocytosis#Macropinocytosis|macropinocytosis]].

macula densa is an area of closely packed specialized [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) lining the wall of the distal tubule where it touches the [glomerulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glomerulus_(kidney)).

Mallory's trichrome stain also called Mallory's Triple Stain is a stain utilized in [histology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology) to aid in revealing different [macromolecule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macromolecule)s that make up the cell.
Malpighian tubule system is a type of [excretory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excretory) and [osmoregulatory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osmoregulation) system found in some *Gullan, P.J.
Mammaglobin is a [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) that encodes a 10-[kilodalton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kilodalton) [glycoprotein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glycoprotein).

mandibles are a pair of appendages near the insect's mouth, and the most anterior of the three pairs of oral appendages (the [[Insect mouthparts#Labrum|labrum]] is more anterior, but is a single fused structure).

mandibular central incisor is the [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) located on the [jaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_mandible), adjacent to the midline of the [face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face).

mandibular first molar or six-year molar is the [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) located distally (away from the midline of the [face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face)) from both the [mandibular second premolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_second_premolar)s of the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth) but mesial (toward the midline of the face) from both [mandibular second molar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_second_molar)s.

mandibular second molar is the [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) located distally (away from the midline of the [face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face)) from both the [mandibular first molar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_first_molar)s of the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth) but mesial (toward the midline of the face) from both [mandibular third molar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_third_molar)s.

mandibular second premolar is the [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) located distally (away from the midline of the [face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face)) from both the [mandibular first premolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_first_premolar)s of the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth) but mesial (toward the midline of the face) from both [mandibular first molar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_first_molar)s.

mane]] On horses, the mane is the [hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair) that grows from the top of the neck of a [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) or other [equine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equine), reaching from the [poll](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Poll_(horse)) to the [withers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Withers), and includes the [forelock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forelock) or foretop.

mantle (also known by the [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language) word pallium meaning mantle, robe or cloak, adjective pallial) is a significant part of the anatomy of [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s: it is the [dorsal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorsum_(biology)) body wall which covers the visceral mass and usually protrudes in the form of flaps well beyond the visceral mass itself.

marginal nucleus of spinal cord, posteromarginal nucleus, or spinal lamina 1 ([Rexed lamina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rexed_lamina) 1) is located at the most dorsal aspect of the [posterior grey column](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_grey_column) of the [spinal cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spinal_cord).

marginal zone is the region at the interface between the non-lymphoid [red pulp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_pulp) and the [lymphoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymphoid) [white-pulp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White-pulp) of the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen).
Marionette lines (melomental folds) are long vertical lines that laterally circumscribe the [chin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chin).

Martin–Gruber anastomosis (MGA) is a connection from the [median nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Median_nerve) to the [ulnar nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulnar_nerve) in the [forearm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forearm).

Mary Frances Keene [FRCS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FRCS) (, 15 August 1885 – 9 May 1977) was professor of anatomy at the [London School of Medicine for Women](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/London_School_of_Medicine_for_Women), the first woman professor of anatomy in the United Kingdom, first woman president of the [Anatomical Society of Great Britain and Ireland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_Society), and a president of the [Medical Women's Federation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_Women's_Federation).

mastocytoma in dogs (or mast cell tumor in dogs) is a neoplasm ([neoplasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasm)) originating from [mast cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mast_cell) in the [domestic dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog), which occurs mainly in the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin) and [subcutis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subcutaneous_tissue).

Matthiessen's ratio is the ratio between the distance from the centre of the [lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lens_(anatomy)) to the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina), versus the lens [radius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radius) in fish and other [aquatic animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_animals).

maxillae (singular maxilla) are paired structures present on the head as [mouthparts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod_mouthparts) in members of the clade [Mandibulata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibulata), used for tasting and manipulating food.

maxillary central incisor is a [human tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_tooth) in the front upper jaw, or [maxilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxilla), and is usually the most visible of all teeth in the mouth.

maxillary lateral incisors are a pair of upper ([maxilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxilla)ry) [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) that are located laterally (away from the midline of the [face](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Face)) from both [maxillary central incisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxillary_central_incisor)s of the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth) and medially (toward the midline of the face) from both [maxillary canine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxillary_canine)s.

maximum intercuspation refers to the [[Commonly used terms of relationship and comparison in dentistry#occlusal|occlusal]] position of the [mandible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandible) in which the [cusps](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cusp_(dentistry)) of the teeth of both arches fully interpose themselves with the cusps of the teeth of the opposing arch.
meatus ( ; each are passages through the [nasal cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasal_cavity) within the skull.

median artery is an [artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artery) that is occasionally found in humans and other animals.

median eminence is generally defined as the portion of the ventral [hypothalamus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothalamus) from which the [portal vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypophyseal_portal_system) arise.
Mediastinitis is [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation) of the tissues in the mid-chest, or [mediastinum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediastinum).
medulla is the innermost layer of the [hair shaft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_shaft).
medullary bone (MB) is a temporary anatomical structure found in most extant birds, and some extinct dinosaurs and birds.
Medullary rays, also known as vascular rays or pith rays, are cellular structures found in some species of [wood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wood).
medullary ray (Ferrein's pyramid) is the middle part of a [cortical lobule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortical_lobule) (or renal lobule).
