Myomeres are blocks of [skeletal muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeletal_muscle) tissue arranged in sequence, commonly found in [aquatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_animal) [chordate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chordate)s.

nail is a protective plate characteristically found at the tip of the [digit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digit_(anatomy))s ([finger](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Finger)s and [toe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toe)s) of almost all [primate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primate)s (except for [marmoset](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marmoset)s), corresponding to the [claw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claw)s in other [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod) animals.

Nail biting, also known as onychophagy or onychophagia, is an [oral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_mouth) [compulsive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body-focused_repetitive_behavior) [habit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Habit) of biting one's [fingernails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fingernails).
nail disease or onychosis is a disease or deformity of the [nail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy)).
Natatory fringes are rows of stiff hairs that occur along the margins of the hindfeet in some [rodent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rodent)s.
natural bobtail is an animal's tail which due to a mutated [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene) grows unusually short or is missing completely.
natural pacemaker is the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart)'s natural rhythm generator.
navicular bone is a small bone found in the feet of most mammals.
Neanderthal anatomy is characterised by a long, flat skull and a stocky body plan.

neck frill is the relatively extensive margin seen on the back of the heads of [reptile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptile)s with either a [bony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) support such as those present on the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull)s of [dinosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dinosaur)s of the suborder [Marginocephalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marginocephalia) or a [cartilaginous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cartilage) one as in the [frill-necked lizard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frill-necked_lizard).

Neer impingement test is a test designed to reproduce symptoms of [rotator cuff](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rotator_cuff) [impingement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder_impingement_syndrome) through flexing the shoulder and pressure application.
Nematode chemoreceptors are [chemoreceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemoreceptor)s of [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode)s.

Nematode infection in dogs - the [infection](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infection) (also [infestation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infestation)) of [dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog)s with [parasitic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitism) [nemamotodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinworm_infection) - are, along with tapeworm infections and infections with protozoa ([giardiasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giardiasis), [neosporosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neospora_caninum)), frequent [parasitoses](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parasitic_disease) in veterinary practice.

Nematosomes are multicellular motile bodies found in the [gastrovascular cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrovascular_cavity) of the model sea anemone Nematostella vectensis [starlet sea anemone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starlet_sea_anemone).

Neointimal hyperplasia refers to proliferation and migration of vascular [smooth muscle cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_muscle_cell)s primarily in the [tunica intima](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunica_intima), resulting in the thickening of [arterial wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arterial_wall)s and decreased arterial [lumen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lumen_(anatomy)) space.
neonatal line is a particular band of incremental growth lines seen in [histologic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology) sections of both enamel and dentin of primary teeth.

Natal teeth are [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) that are present above the gumline (have already [erupted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_eruption)) at [birth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth), and neonatal teeth are teeth that emerge through the [gingiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gingiva) during the first month of life (the [neonatal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infant) period).
neoplasm () are current medical terms for non-neoplastic swelling.

nephridiopore is a pore at the end of the [nephridium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephridium), an [excretory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Excretion) [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) found in [invertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrates), such as [flatworm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flatworm)s and [annelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annelid)s.
nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney).
nephrostome is the funnel-like component of a [metanephridium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metanephridium).

nerve net consists of interconnected [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s lacking a [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) or any form of [cephalization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalization).

neural crest is a ridge-like structure that is formed transiently between the [epidermal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermal) [ectoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ectoderm) and [neural plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_plate) during [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) development.
neural spine sail is a large, flattish protrusion from the back of an animal formed of a sequence of extended [[Vertebra#Processes|vertebral spinous processes]] and associated tissues.
neurite or neuronal process refers to any projection from the [cell body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_body) of a [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron).
neuroectodermal neoplasm is a [neoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasm) or [tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tumor) of the [neuroectoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroectoderm).

Neuroepigenetics is the study of how [epigenetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigenetic) changes to [genes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genes) affect the [nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nervous_system).

Neuropathology is the study of [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease) of nervous system tissue, usually in the form of either small surgical [biopsies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopsy) or whole-body [autopsies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autopsy).

neurovascular bundle is a structure that binds nerves and veins (and in some cases arteries and [lymphatics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymphatics)) with [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) so that they travel in tandem through the body.
Nevus cells are a variant of [melanocytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melanocytes).

Nicolaes Tulp (9 October 1593 – 12 September 1674) was a [Dutch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dutch_people) [physician](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physician) and [mayor of Amsterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_mayors_of_Amsterdam).

Nidamental glands are [internal organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy))s found in some [elasmobranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elasmobranch)s and certain [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s, including [cephalopod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalopod)s (specifically [Decapodiformes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decapodiformes) and [nautilus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautilus)es) and [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod)s.

Nikkur () is the process of making an animal kosher by removing [chelev](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelev) (forbidden fats) and the [gid hanasheh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gid_hanasheh) (sciatic nerve).

nipple is a raised region of tissue on the surface of the [breast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast) from which, in [lactating](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lactating) females, [milk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breast_milk) from the [mammary gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammary_gland) leaves the body through the [lactiferous duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lactiferous_duct)s to [nurse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Breastfeeding) an infant.

NK2 homeobox 1 (NKX2-1), also known as thyroid transcription factor 1 (TTF-1), is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) which in humans is encoded by the NKX2-1 [gene](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gene).

Nomina Anatomica (NA) was the international standard on human anatomic terminology from 1895 until it was replaced by [Terminologia Anatomica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminologia_Anatomica) in 1998.
Nomina Anatomica Veterinaria (often abbreviated as NAV) is a [standardized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Standardization) [nomenclature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nomenclature).
nostril (or naris , : nares ) is either of the two [orifices](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_orifice) of the [nose](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nose).

Notarium or os dorsale is a bone consisting of the fused [vertebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebra) of the shoulder in [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird)s and some [pterosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pterosaur)s.
notopleuron (plural notopleura) is a region on an [insect thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax_(arthropod_anatomy)).

notum (plural nota) is the [dorsal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dorsum_(biology)) portion of an [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)'s [thoracic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax) segment, or the dorsal surface of the body of [nudibranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nudibranch) gastropods.
Nuclear dimorphism is a term referred to the special characteristic of having two different kinds of [nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus) in a cell.

nuclear–cytoplasmic ratio (also variously known as the nucleus:cytoplasm ratio, nucleus–cytoplasm ratio, N:C ratio, or N/C) is a measurement used in [cell biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_biology).

nucleoid (meaning [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus)-like) is an irregularly shaped region within the [prokaryotic cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prokaryote) that contains all or most of the [genetic material](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Genome).

Nucleolus organizer regions ([American English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/American_English)) or nucleolus organiser regions ([British English](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/British_English)) (NORs) are [chromosomal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chromosome) regions crucial for the formation of the [nucleolus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleolus).
Nuptial tubercles or breeding tubercles (also called pearl organs or nuptial efflorescence) are noticeable skin roughness or horny nodules that form on male fish during breeding.
nutshell is the outer shell of a [nut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nut_(fruit)).
obturator process is an anatomical feature on the [pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvis) of [archosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archosaur)s.

page: Occupational hazards of human nail dust

definition: Odontodes, or [dermal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermis) [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teeth), are hard structures found on the external surfaces of animals or near internal openings.
odontogenic tumor is a neoplasm of the cells or tissues that initiate [odontogenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_development_(disambiguation)) processes.

Offshoots are lateral shoots that are produced on the main [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem) of a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) and are an [asexual](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asexual_reproduction) form of reproduction ==See also== * [Stolon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stolon), [offsets](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Offset_(botany)) or [https://www.evergreenseeds.com/what-are-runners-in-plants/ runners] [[Category:Plant anatomy]] [[Category:Plant morphology]] == References == sbjd1g6e05s3elppr88yab048fx6i82

oidium (: oidia) is an asexually produced [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore) that (in contrast to [conidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conidia)) is presumed not to constitute the main reproductive preoccupation of the fungus at that time.
oil body is a [lipid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid)-containing structure found in [plant cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell)s.
Oliger Jacobaeus (1650-1701), also known as Holger Jacobi, was a [Danish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danes) physician and [naturalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Naturalist).

omegasome is a cell organelle consisting of [lipid bilayer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lipid_bilayer) [membranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_membrane) enriched with [phosphatidylinositol 3-phosphate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phosphatidylinositol_3-phosphate) (abbreviated PI(3)P), and related to a process of [autophagy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autophagy).

definition: one-size-fits-all hypothesis of [spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_system_of_arachnids) and [insect male genitalia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_reproduction) was proposed by William G.

operculum (; ) is a [corneous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corneous) or [calcareous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcareous) anatomical structure like a [trapdoor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trapdoor) that exists in many (but not all) groups of [sea snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_snail)s and [freshwater snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater_snail)s, and also in a few groups of [land snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_snail)s, including the [Helicinidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helicinidae), [Cyclophoridae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclophoridae), [Aciculidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aciculidae), [Maizaniidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maizaniidae), [Pomatiidae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pomatiidae), etc.

operculum is a series of bones found in [bony fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bony_fish) and [chimaeras](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chimaera) that serves as a facial support structure and a protective covering for the [gill](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gill)s; it is also used for respiration and feeding.

operculum (: opercula) or calyptra () is a cap-like structure in some [flowering plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowering_plant)s, [moss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moss)es, and [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus).

operculum is a [calcareous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcareous) or [chitin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chitin)ous lid-like structure that protects the opening through which the [polypide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polypide) protrudes.

Ophthalmic pathology is a subspecialty of both [ophthalmolog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ophthalmolog)y and [surgical pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgical_pathology) concerned with the [diagnosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis) and characterization of diseases of the eye and its associated structures, including [neoplastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasia) and non-neoplastic conditions of the [human eyes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eyes).

Opiliones (commonly known as harvestmen) are an [order](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Order_(biology)) of [arachnid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arachnid)s and share many common characteristics with other arachnids.
optic cup is the white, cup-like area in the center of the [optic disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optic_disc).

optic disc or optic nerve head is the point of exit for [ganglion cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_ganglion_cell) [axon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axon)s leaving the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).

optic(al) lobe of [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s is a structure of the [protocerebrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protocerebrum) that sits behind the [arthropod eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod_eye) (mostly [compound eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compound_eye)s) and is responsible for the processing of the visual information.
ora serrata is the serrated junction between the [choroid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Choroid) and the [ciliary body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliary_body).
oral arm is an [anatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) structure of Scyphozoa.

Oral manifestations of systematic disease are signs and [symptoms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symptoms) of disease occurring elsewhere in the body detected in the [oral cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oral_cavity) and oral secretions.
oral mucosa is the [mucous membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucous_membrane) lining the inside of the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth).

orbit is the [cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_cavity) or socket/hole of the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) in which the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) and [its appendages](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accessory_visual_structures) are situated.

orbital septum (palpebral fascia) is a [membranous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_membrane) sheet that acts as the anterior (frontal) boundary of the [orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy)).

orbitalis muscle is a vestigial or rudimentary nonstriated muscle ([smooth muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_muscle)) that crosses from the [infraorbital groove](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infraorbital_groove) and [sphenomaxillary fissure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphenomaxillary_fissure) and is intimately united with the [periosteum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periosteum) of the orbit.
organ is a collection of [tissues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) joined in a structural unit to serve a common [function](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Function_(biology)).
Organ culture is the cultivation of either whole organs or parts of organs [in vitro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/In_vitro).
organs of Bojanus or Bojanus organs are excretory glands that serve the function of [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney)s in some of the [molluscs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusca).
Tömösváry organs, also known as temporal organs or postantennal organs The organs were first described by Hungarian biologist [Ödön Tömösváry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ödön_Tömösváry) in 1883.

organ of Valenciennes, named after the French naturalist [Achille Valenciennes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Achille_Valenciennes), is one of two secondary sexual organs of the female of the genus [Nautilus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautilus).

organ system is a [biological system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_system) consisting of a group of [organs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(biology)) that work together to perform one or more bodily functions.
organelle is a specialized subunit, within a [biological cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)), that has a specific function.

Orthopedic pathology, also known as bone pathology is a subspecialty of [surgical pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgical_pathology) which deals with the diagnosis and feature of many [bone diseases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_diseases), specifically studying the cause and effects of disorders of the [musculoskeletal system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_musculoskeletal_system).

categories: Anatomy named for one who described it

definition: osculum (: oscula) is an excretory structure in the living [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_sponge), a large opening to the outside through which the current of water exits after passing through the [spongocoel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spongocoel).

osphradium is a pigmented [chemosensory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemosensory) [epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium) patch in the [mantle cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mantle_cavity) present in six of the eight extant [class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_(biology))es of [molluscs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molluscs) (it is absent in the [Scaphopoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scaphopoda) and [Monoplacophora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monoplacophora); most [Cephalopoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalopoda) also lack it, but the [nautilus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautilus) has what appears to be a set of osphradia .

Ossicles are small [calcareous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcareous) elements embedded in the [dermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermis) of the body wall of [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinoderm)s.

Ossicones are columnar or conical skin-covered bone structures on the heads of [giraffe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giraffe)s, male [okapi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Okapi), and some of their extinct relatives.
Osteoderms are bony deposits forming scales, plates, or other structures based in the [dermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermis).

osteoid osteoma is a benign (non-cancerous) [bone tumor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone_tumor) that arises from [osteoblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteoblast)s and some components of osteoclasts.
Osteosclerosis is a disorder characterized by [abnormal hardening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclerosis_(medicine)) of bone and an elevation in bone density.
ostiole is a small hole or opening through which [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae) Ibarra-Manríquez, G.
Otic notches are invaginations in the posterior margin of the [skull roof](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull_roof), one behind each [orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy)).

otolith (, ' ear + , ', a stone), also called otoconium, statolith, or statoconium, is a [calcium carbonate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium_carbonate) structure in the [saccule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saccule) or [utricle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Utricle_(ear)) of the [inner ear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_ear), specifically in the [vestibular system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vestibular_system) of [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.

Outer membrane vesicles (OMVs) are [vesicles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vesicle_(biology_and_chemistry)) released from the [outer membranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterial_outer_membrane) of [Gram-negative bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gram-negative_bacteria).

definition: Ovarian squamous cell carcinoma (oSCC) or squamous ovarian carcinoma (SOC) is a rare tumor that accounts for 1% of [ovarian cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ovarian_cancer)s.
ovariole is a tubular component of the insect ovary, and the basic unit of egg production.
ovary is a part of the female reproductive organ of the flower or [gynoecium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gynoecium).

overjet is the extent of horizontal ([anterior-posterior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_terms_of_location)) overlap of the [maxillary central incisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxillary_central_incisor)s over the [mandibular central incisor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandibular_central_incisor)s.

ovipore is a pore-like [sexual organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexual_organ) of a female [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) that is [inseminated](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insemination) by the [spermatophore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatophore)s ejected by the [aedeagus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aedeagus) of a male insect during [copulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copulation_(zoology)).

ovipositor is a tube-like [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) used by some [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s, especially [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s, for the laying of [eggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Egg_(biology)).
ovule is the structure that gives rise to and contains the female reproductive cells.

Owen's laminated organ, named after the 19th century English biologist [Richard Owen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Richard_Owen), is one of two secondary sexual organs of the female of the genus [Nautilus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautilus).
Owl's eye appearance, also known as owl's eye sign, is a pattern used in the medical field to describe cells (or cell attributes) that resemble the shape of an actual owl's eye.
ozophore is an elevated cone present in the [harvestman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opiliones) ( Giribet, G.}} (eds.) (2007): Harvestmen - The Biology of Opiliones.

ozopore is the opening of a defensive [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland) present in some arthropods, notably in [millipede](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Millipede)s of the order [Polydesmida](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polydesmida) Giribet, G.}} (eds.) (2007): Harvestmen - The Biology of Opiliones.
Pachycauls are [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s with a disproportionately thick [trunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunk_(botany)), for their height, and relatively few branches.

Pachyosteosclerosis is a combination of thickening ([pachyostosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pachyostosis)) and densification ([osteosclerosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteosclerosis)) of bones.
palatoquadrate is the dorsal component of the mandibular arch, the ventral one being [Meckel's cartilage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meckel's_cartilage).

Paleohistology is the study of the [microstructure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microstructure) of [fossilized](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossilized) [skeletal tissues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeleton), offering insights into the [biology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biology), [growth patterns](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Growth_hormone), and [physiology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Physiology) of [extinct organisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extinct_organisms).

pallial sinus is an indentation or inward bending in the [pallial line](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pallial_line) on the interior of a [bivalve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalve) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk) shell's valves that corresponds to the position of the [siphons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siphon_(mollusc)) in those types of clams which have siphons (i.e.
palmar intercarpal ligaments are fibrous bands that extend transversely across the palmar surfaces of the [carpal bones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpal_bones), connecting adjacent carpals.

Palmer notation (sometimes called the military system) is a [dental notation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dental_notation) system (tooth numbering system) named for 19th-century American dentist Corydon Palmer from [Warren, Ohio](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warren,_Ohio) A plus (+) indicates upper position while minus (−) indicates lower.
palpal bulbs – also known as palpal organs and genital bulbs – are the [copulatory organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copulatory_organ)s of a male [spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider).
palpebral fissure is the elliptic space between the medial and lateral [canthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canthi) of the two open [eyelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelid)s.

Pan American Association of Anatomy (PAA) is a public, [nonprofit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nonprofit_organization), scientific organization that brings together professionals engaged in the study of [Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) and related sciences in the American continent.

Pancreas divisum is a congenital anomaly in the [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) of the ducts of the [pancreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreas) in which a single [pancreatic duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreatic_duct) is not formed, but rather remains as two distinct dorsal and ventral ducts.

pancreatic duct or duct of Wirsung (also, the major pancreatic duct due to the existence of an accessory pancreatic duct) is a duct joining the [pancreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreas) to the [common bile duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_bile_duct).

pancreatic islets or islets of Langerhans are the regions of the [pancreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreas) that contain its [endocrine cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_cells) ([hormone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hormone)-producing cells), discovered in 1869 by [German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germans) pathological anatomist [Paul Langerhans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_Langerhans).

Pancreatic progenitor cells are [multipotent stem cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multipotent_stem_cell)s originating from the developing fore-gut [endoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endoderm) which have the ability to differentiate into the lineage specific [progenitor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Progenitor)s responsible for the developing [pancreas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreas).

panniculus adiposus is the fatty layer of the [subcutaneous tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subcutaneous_tissue)s, superficial to a deeper vestigial layer of muscle, the [panniculus carnosus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Panniculus_carnosus).
panniculus carnosus is a part of the [subcutaneous tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Subcutaneous_tissue)s in [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.

papilla, in certain kinds of [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish), particularly [ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batoidea)s, [shark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shark)s, and [catfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catfish), are small lumps of dermal tissue found in the mouth, where they are Most typically, these are found on the floor of the mouth, or on the upper lip.

parafacial or parafacialia is the area between [ptilinal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ptilinal) [fissure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fissure_(anatomy)) and the [compound eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Compound_eye) of [diptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diptera)ns.
Parafollicular cells, also called C cells, are [neuroendocrine cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroendocrine_cell)s in the [thyroid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thyroid).
Paraphyses are erect sterile filament-like support structures occurring among the reproductive apparatuses of fungi, ferns, bryophytes and some thallophytes.
parapodium ([Gr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) para, beyond or beside + podia, feet; : parapodia) refers to lateral outgrowths or protrusions from the body.

parasternal line is a vertical line on the front of the thorax.

paraventricular nucleus (PVN) is a [nucleus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nucleus_(neuroanatomy)) in the [hypothalamus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hypothalamus), located next to the [third ventricle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_ventricle).

Paris type is a pattern of [mycorrhizal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycorrhizal) infection which is coil-like in [morphology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)).

parotoid gland (alternatively, paratoid gland) is a type of external [skin gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin_gland) on the back, neck and shoulder of some [frog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frog)s (especially [toad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toad)s) and [salamander](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Salamander)s, which can secrete a number of milky [alkaloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alkaloid) substances (depending on the species) known collectively as [bufotoxins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bufotoxins), which act as [neurotoxins](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neurotoxins) to [deter predation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anti-predator_adaptation).
pars plana (also known as orbicularis ciliaris this surgery is known as [pars plana vitrectomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pars_plana_vitrectomy).

definition: patagium (: patagia) is a membranous [body part](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_body) that assists an animal in obtaining [lift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lift_(force)) when [gliding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gliding_flight) or [flying](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flight).

paw is the soft foot-like part of a [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal), generally a [quadruped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadruped), that has [claw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claw)s.
Pectoral muscles (colloquially referred to as ) are the muscles that connect the front of the human [chest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chest) with the bones of the upper arm and shoulder.

Pediatric pathology is the sub-specialty of [surgical pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgical_pathology) which deals with the [diagnosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis) and characterization of [neoplastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasia) and non-neoplastic [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease)s of [child](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Child)ren.

pedicellaria (: pedicellariae) is a small wrench- or claw-shaped [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage) with movable jaws, called valves, commonly found on [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinoderm)s (phylum [Echinodermata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinodermata)), particularly in sea stars (class [Asteroidea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asteroidea)) and sea urchins (class [Echinoidea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinoidea)).

Pedicellate teeth are a tooth morphology today unique to modern [amphibians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibians), but also seen in a variety of extinct [labyrinthodonts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Labyrinthodonts).

Pedipalps (commonly shortened to palps or palpi) are the secondary pair of forward [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s among [chelicerates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelicerata) – a group of [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s including [spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider)s, [scorpion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scorpion)s, [horseshoe crab](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horseshoe_crab)s, and [sea spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_spider)s.

peduncle is a stalk supporting an [inflorescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflorescence) or a solitary [flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower), or, after [fertilisation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertilisation), an [infructescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Infructescence) or a solitary [fruit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruit).

Peliosis hepatis is an uncommon [vascular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel) condition characterised by multiple, randomly distributed, blood-filled cavities throughout the [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver).
pellis refers to the cellular cortical layers of a [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom).
Peltidium is a prodorsal shield found in animals of the subphylum [Chelicerata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chelicerata), in the phylum [Arthropoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropoda).

Pelvic fins or ventral fins are paired [fin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_fin)s located on the ventral (belly) surface of [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish), and are the lower of the only two sets of paired fins (the other being the laterally positioned [pectoral fin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoral_fin)s).

Pelvic spurs (also known as vestigial legs) are external protrusions found around the [cloaca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cloaca) in certain superfamilies of [snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake)s belonging to the greater infraorder [Alethinophidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alethinophidia).
Pelvic tilt is the orientation of the [pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvis) in respect to the [thighbones](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thighbones) and the rest of the body.

frenulum of the penis, often known simply as the frenulum (from ) or frenum, is a thin elastic strip of tissue on the underside of the [glans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glans_penis) and the neck of the [human penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_penis).

penile raphe (/ˈrā-fē/) is a visible line or ridge of [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) that runs on the [ventral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventral) (urethral) side of the [human penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_penis) beginning from the base of the [shaft](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_of_penis) and ending in the [prepuce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreskin) between the [penile frenulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penile_frenulum).

definition: Pennsylvania Anatomy Act of 1883 is legislation of the State of [Pennsylvania](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pennsylvania) to facilitate [medical education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_education).
perianth (perigonium, perigon or perigone in [monocots](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monocots)) is the non-reproductive part of a [flower](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flower).

Pericardial fluid is the [serous fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serous_fluid) secreted by the [serous layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serous_membrane) of the [pericardium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pericardium) into the [pericardial cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pericardial_cavity).

pericardial sinuses are impressions in the [pericardial sac](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pericardium) formed between the points where [great vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_vessels) enter it.
Pericardiophrenic veins are thin venous structures located in the thoracic cavity.

pericardium (), also called pericardial sac, is a double-walled fluid filled sac containing the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) and the roots of the [great vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_vessels).
peridium is the protective layer that encloses a [mass of spores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gleba) in [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus).

periodontium () is the specialized tissues that both surround and support the [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teeth), maintaining them in the [maxilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxilla)ry and [mandibular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_mandible) bones.
periorbita is the area around the [orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy)).

Periorbital puffiness, also known as puffy eyes, or swelling around the eyes, is the appearance of swelling in the tissues around the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye)s, called the [orbits](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy)).

periplast is one of three types of cell-covering of three classes of [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae).
periproct is the final body segment in [annelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annelid) worms.

periscleral lymph space or episcleral space of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye) is the space between the outer surface of the [sclera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclera) and the inner surface of the [capsule of Tenon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capsule_of_Tenon).

perisinusoidal space (or space of Disse) is a space between a [hepatocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hepatocyte), and a [sinusoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver_sinusoid) in the [liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Liver).

Peristome (from the [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) peri, meaning 'around' or 'about', and stoma, 'mouth') is an anatomical feature that surrounds an opening to an organ or structure.
peristomium is the first true body segment in an [annelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Annelid) worm's body in the anterior end.

peritubular capillaries are tiny [blood vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel), supplied by the [efferent arteriole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Efferent_arteriole), that travel alongside [nephrons](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephrons) allowing reabsorption and [secretion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretion) between blood and the inner lumen of the nephron.

perivitelline fluid is an [extracellular fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_fluid) found in the eggs of most [gastropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropoda) and constitutes the main source of nutrition and defense for their [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)s.
Perivitellins are egg proteins found in the [perivitelline fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perivitelline_fluid) of many [gastropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropoda).
Perls Prussian blue is a commonly used method to detect the presence of [iron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iron) in tissue or cell samples.
Permanent cells are [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s that are incapable of [regeneration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_cycle).

[[wikt:pes#Latin|pes]] ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language) for foot) is the [zoological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoology) term for the [distal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_terms_of_location) portion of the hind limb of [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod) animals.

definition: phagosome is a [vesicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vesicle_(biology)) formed around a particle engulfed by a [phagocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phagocyte) via [phagocytosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phagocytosis).

pharyngeal arches, also known as visceral arches, are transient structures seen in the [embryonic development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_embryonic_development) of [human](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human)s and other [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s, that are recognisable precursors for many structures.
pharyngeal artery is a branch of the [ascending pharyngeal artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascending_pharyngeal_artery).
Pharyngeal jaws are a is depicted with a pharyngeal jaw.
Pharyngeal slits are [filter-feeding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Filter_feeder) organs found among [deuterostome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deuterostome)s.

Pharyngeal teeth are [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teeth) in the [pharyngeal arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharyngeal_arch) of the throat of [cyprinid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyprinid)s, [sucker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catostomidae)s, and a number of other [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish) species otherwise lacking openly visible teeth.

pharynx (: pharynges) is the part of the [throat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Throat) behind the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_mouth) and [nasal cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nasal_cavity), and above the [esophagus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esophagus) and [trachea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trachea) (the tubes going down to the [stomach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stomach) and the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s respectively).
Phasmids are [sensilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensilla) in the lateral tail region of certain species of [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode)s.
Phenice method is a technique of determining the sex of a [human skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_skeleton) from the innominate [pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvis).

Phenoloxidase system is a major defense system in many [invertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate) which ultimately leads to [melanization](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Melanization) of pathogens and damaged tissues.

phialide ( ; , diminutive of phiale, a broad, flat vessel) is a flask-shaped projection from the vesicle (dilated part of the top of [conidiophore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conidiophore)) of certain [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi).

photophore is a specialized anatomical structure found in a variety of organisms that emits light through the process of [bioluminescence](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bioluminescence).

photoreceptor cell is a specialized type of [neuroepithelial cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuroepithelial_cell) found in the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) that is capable of [visual phototransduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_phototransduction).
phragmosome is a sheet of cytoplasm forming in highly vacuolated [plant cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell)s in preparation for [mitosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mitosis).

Phycobilisomes are [light-harvesting antennae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light_harvesting_complex) that transmit the energy of harvested photons to [photosystem II](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosystem_II) and [photosystem I](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosystem_I) in [cyanobacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyanobacteria) and in the [chloroplast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroplast)s of [red algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Red_algae) and [glaucophytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glaucophytes).

phyllochron is the intervening period between the sequential emergence of [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf) on the main [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem) of a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant), also rendered as leaf appearance }} [[Category:Plant anatomy]] [[Category:Plant morphology]] qdvg26s0immkf5o5zc0tf8241kfikcu

Phylloclades and cladodes are flattened, [photosynthetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthesis) shoots, which are usually considered to be modified [branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch)es.
Physogastrism or physogastry is a characteristic of certain arthropods (mostly insects and mites), where the abdomen is greatly enlarged and membranous.
Physostomes are fishes that have a pneumatic duct connecting the [gas bladder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_bladder) to the [alimentary canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alimentary_canal).
Phytomers are functional units of a plant, continually produced by root and shoot [meristem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meristem)s throughout a plant's vegetative life-cycle.
Phytotelma (plural phytotelmata) is a small water-filled cavity in a terrestrial plant.
piebald or pied animal is one that has a pattern of unpigmented spots (white) on a pigmented background of hair, feathers or scales.
pigment spot ocellus is an [ocellus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ocellus) that contains only part of its cells pigmented.

pileipellis is the uppermost layer of [hyphae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphae) in the [pileus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pileus_(mycology)) of a [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungal) [fruit body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiocarp).

pileus (: pilei) is the cap or cap-like part of a [basidiocarp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidiocarp) or ascocarp ([fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungal) [fruiting body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fruiting_body)) that supports a spore-bearing surface, the hymenium.
pin feather is a developing [feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feather) on a [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird).

media.file: A nestling of rock dove with pin feathers.jpg

definition: Pinacocytes are flat [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) found on the outside of [sponges](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge), as well as the internal canals of a sponge.

pinacoderm is the outermost layer of body cells ([pinacocytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinacocytes)) of organisms of the phylum [Porifera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Porifera) (sponges), equivalent to the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(skin)) in other animals.

pineal gland (also called the pineal body) is a small [endocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_gland) in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) of most [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.

Pith, or medulla, is a [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) in the [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem)s of [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant)s.
Pituicytes are [glial cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glial_cell)s of the [posterior pituitary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_pituitary).

placenta (: placentas or placentae) is a temporary [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo)nic and later [fetal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fetus) [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(biology)) that begins [developing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryonic_development) from the [blastocyst](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blastocyst) shortly after [implantation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Implantation_(embryology)).

plagiaulacoid is a type of blade-like, most often serrated, [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth) present in various [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal) groups, usually a [premolar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Premolar).

plait is an anatomical feature which is present on the [shells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell) of some [snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snail)s, or [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod)s.
Plant anatomy or phytotomy is the general term for the study of the internal structure of [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

Plant cells are the [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) present in [green plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viridiplantae), photosynthetic [eukaryote](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote)s of the kingdom [Plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)ae.

plant cuticle is a protecting film covering the outermost skin layer ([epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(botany))) of [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf), young shoots and other aerial plant organs (aerial here meaning all plant parts not embedded in soil or other substrate) that have no [[Bark (botany)#Periderm|periderm]].
stem is one of two main structural axes of a [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant), the other being the [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root).

media.file: Translocation from the source to the sink within the phloem.svg

definition: plasmid is a small, [extrachromosomal DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extrachromosomal_DNA) molecule within a cell that is physically separated from [chromosomal DNA](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/GDNA) and can replicate independently.

Plastination is a technique or process used in [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) to preserve bodies or body parts, first developed by [Gunther von Hagens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gunther_von_Hagens) in 1977.

Platyclades are flattened, [photosynthetic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthesis) shoots, [branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch)es or [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem)s that resemble or perform the function of [leaves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaves), as in [Homalocladium platycladum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homalocladium_platycladum) and some [cactus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cactus) genera like [Opuntia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opuntia) and [Schlumbergera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schlumbergera).

Plectenchyma (from [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ancient_Greek) πλέκω pleko 'I weave' and ἔγχυμα enchyma 'infusion', i.e., 'a woven tissue') is the general term employed to designate all types of [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) tissues.

Pleomorphism is a term used in [histology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology) and [cytopathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytopathology) to describe variability in the size, shape and [staining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staining) of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology))s and/or their [nuclei](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_nucleus).

Pleurodont is a form of tooth implantation common in [reptile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reptile)s of the order [Squamata](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squamata), as well as in at least one [temnospondyl](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temnospondyl).

media.file: Tooth shape changes within the jaw (heterodont - homodont).jpg

definition: plica semilunaris is a small fold of [bulbar conjunctiva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conjunctiva) on the medial canthus of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).

Plumage (), or feathering, is a layer of [feather](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feather)s that covers a [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird) and the pattern, colour, and arrangement of those feathers.
pneumatodes are air-containing structures in plant roots.

pneumostome or breathing pore is a respiratory opening of the external body anatomy of a [pulmonate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonate) land [slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug) or [land snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_snail).

Podocytes are [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) in [Bowman's capsule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowman's_capsule) in the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney)s that wrap around [capillaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillary) of the [glomerulus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glomerulus_(kidney)).

Podosomes are conical, [actin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actin)-rich structures found as [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s on the outer surface of the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane) of [animal cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_cell)s.

Polar capsules are structures found in the valves of [myxosporea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myxosporea)n parasites, which contain the [polar filament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_filament).

polar organelle is a structure at a specialized region of the [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria)l [polar membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polar_membrane) that is associated with the [flagellar apparatus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellum).
Pollen is a powdery substance produced by most types of flowers of [seed plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed_plant)s for the purpose of sexual reproduction.
pollen basket or corbicula (plural corbiculae) is part of the [[Arthropod leg#Hexapoda|tibia]] on the hind legs of the female of certain species of [bee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bee)s.

pollinium (: pollinia) is a coherent mass of [pollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollen) grains in a plant that are the product of only one [anther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anther), but are transferred, during pollination, as a single unit.

Polycerates (meaning ==Mythology== [Cerastes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cerastes), a legendary Greek horned [serpent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serpent_(symbolism)), is sometimes described with two horns or with four small ones.

Polydactyly in stem-tetrapods should here be understood as having more than five digits to the finger or foot, a condition that was the natural state of affairs in the earliest [stegocephalians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stegocephalia) during the [evolution of terrestriality](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate_land_invasion).

related: Accessory nail of the fifth toe

definition: polyphyodont is any animal whose [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth_(animal)) are continually replaced.

Popliteal refers to anatomical structures located in the back of the [knee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee): *[Popliteal artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_artery) *[Popliteal vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_vein) *[Popliteal fossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_fossa) *[Popliteal lymph nodes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_lymph_nodes) *[Popliteus muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteus_muscle) *Popliteal [nerves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerves) *[Popliteal pterygium syndrome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_pterygium_syndrome) [[Category:Lower limb anatomy]] rgeqaibw3d45in29sqpqhu03wnyswlu

pores of Kohn (also known as interalveolar connections or alveolar pores) are discrete holes in [walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alveolar_wall) of adjacent [alveoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_alveolus).
categories: Anatomy named for one who described it

definition: Porocytes are tubular cells which make up the pores of a [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_sponge) known as [ostia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ostium_(sponges)).

Porosomes are cup-shaped supramolecular structures in the [cell membranes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membranes) of [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryote) cells where [secretory vesicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretory_vesicle)s transiently dock in the process of [vesicle fusion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vesicle_fusion) and [secretion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretion).

[human brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_brain) has the same general structure as the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain)s of other [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s, but is larger than any other in relation to body size.
tissue is a cellular organizational level between [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) and a complete [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)).

Henry Vandyke Carter (born 22 May 1831, [Hull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kingston_upon_Hull) – 4 May 1897, [Scarborough](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scarborough,_North_Yorkshire)) was an English anatomist, surgeon, and anatomical artist most notable for his illustrations of the book, [Gray's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gray's_Anatomy).
postdentary trough is a skeletal feature seen in [Mesozoic mammals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Evolution_of_mammals).
posterior carpometacarpal ligament consists of a series of bands on the posterior surface of the [carpometacarpal joints](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carpometacarpal_joints).

posterior chamber is a narrow space behind the peripheral part of the [iris](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iris_(anatomy)), and in front of the [suspensory ligament of the lens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Suspensory_ligament_of_the_lens) and the [ciliary processes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliary_processes).

posterior compartment of the thigh is one of the [fascial compartments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascial_compartments_of_thigh) that contains the [knee](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knee) [[anatomical terms of motion#flexion|flexors]] and [hip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip) [[anatomical terms of motion#extension|extensors]] known as the [hamstring muscles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hamstring_muscles), as well as vascular and nervous elements, particularly the [sciatic nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sciatic_nerve).

posterior humeral circumflex vessels or posterior circumflex humeral vessels are the [posterior humeral circumflex artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_humeral_circumflex_artery) and the [posterior humeral circumflex vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_humeral_circumflex_vein) which run through the [quadrangular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadrangular_space) (or quadrilateral) space with the [axillary nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axillary_nerve).

posterior interventricular sulcus or posterior longitudinal sulcus is one of the two grooves separating the [ventricles](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ventricle_(heart)) of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) (the other being the [anterior interventricular sulcus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_interventricular_sulcus)).
posterolateral palatal pits are gaps at the sides of the back of the bony [palate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Palate), near the last [molars](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molar_(tooth)).

Postmortem caloricity is a phenomenon where the body temperature of a [corpse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadaver) rises or remains unusually high for up to 2 hours after [death](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Death) instead of falling.

postorbital bar (or postorbital bone) is a bony arched structure that connects the [frontal bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontal_bone) of the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) to the [zygomatic arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zygomatic_arch), which runs laterally around the [eye socket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye_socket).
potential space is a space between two adjacent structures that are normally pressed together (directly apposed).
related: Fascial spaces of the head and neck

definition: pouch is a distinguishing feature of female [marsupials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marsupials) and [monotremes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monotremes), ==See also== *For more about the nature and usage of the pouch, see ==References== ==External links== * [[Category:Marsupial anatomy]] rn19r43lh0md4dprv38cby04ze0jkxy

precapillary sphincter is a band of contractile [mural cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mural_cells) either classified as [smooth muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smooth_muscle_tissue) or [pericytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pericytes) that adjusts [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) flow into [capillaries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillary).
Precision cut lung slices or PCLS refer to thin sections of lung tissue that are prepared with high precision and are typically used for experimental purposes in the field of respiratory research.

precordium [[American and British English spelling differences#ae and oe|or]] praecordium is the portion of the [body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body) over the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) and lower [chest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chest).
predentary is an ossification situated on the front of the [lower jaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaw), which extended the dentary (the main lower jaw bone).

prefrontal bone is a [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) separating the [lacrimal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacrimal_bone) and [frontal bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontal_bone)s in many [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod) [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull)s.

Pregnancy-specific biological substances, which include the [placenta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Placenta), [umbilical cord](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Umbilical_cord), [amniotic fluid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amniotic_fluid), and [amniotic membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amniotic_membrane) are being studied for a number of health uses.
prehensile tail is the tail of an animal that has [adapted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation_(biology)) to grasp or hold objects.

Prehensility is the quality of an [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage) or [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) that has [adapted](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adaptation_(biology)) for [grasp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Grasp)ing or holding.

preorbital gland is a paired [exocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exocrine_gland) found in many species of [artiodactyls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artiodactyls), which is [homologous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(biology)) to the [lacrimal gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lacrimal_gland) found in humans.
prepatellar bursa is a [[Bursa of the knee joint#Frontal|frontal bursa of the knee joint]].
Preputial glands are [exocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exocrine_gland)s in the [prepuce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Penile_sheath) in front of the penis.

preputial mucosa of the [penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_penis) is the [epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium) of the inside of the prepuce, or [foreskin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foreskin).
Primal Pictures is a business that provides 3D graphic renderings of [human anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body).
proboscis () is an elongated appendage from the head of an animal, either a [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) or an [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate).
process () is a projection or outgrowth of [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) from a larger body.
prolapse is a condition in which [organs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) fall down or slip out of place.
Prone position () is a body position in which a person lies flat with their chest down and their back up.

prostate is an [accessory gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male_accessory_gland) of the [male reproductive system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Male_reproductive_system) and a muscle-driven mechanical switch between [urination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urination) and [ejaculation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ejaculation).

prostigma (also called stigma anteriore or anterior spiracle) is the [anterior](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior) of the two pairs of [spiracle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spiracle_(arthropods))s opening on the [pleura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleuron_(insect)).

term: Proteins produced and secreted by the liver
page: Proteins produced and secreted by the liver

definition: prothallus, or prothallium, (from [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) pro = forwards and [Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) θαλλος (thallos) = twig) is usually the [gametophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gametophyte) stage in the life of a [fern](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fern) or other [pteridophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pteridophyte).

prothoracic glands are either of a pair of [endocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endocrine_gland)s located in the [prothorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prothorax) of certain insects that regulate [molting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Molting).

prothorax is the foremost of the three segments in the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax_(insect_anatomy)) of an [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect), and bears the first pair of [legs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_leg).
proventriculus is part of the [digestive system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digestive_system) of [birds](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birds).

proximal tubule is the segment of the [nephron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephron) in [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney)s which begins from the renal (tubular) pole of the [Bowman's capsule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bowman's_capsule) to the beginning of [loop of Henle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loop_of_Henle).
proximodorsal [process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Process_(anatomy)) is a feature of the skeleton of [archosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archosaur)s.

Pseudociliate refers to a type of cells which are covered by small coordinated flagella ([cilia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilia)), but are not related to the [Harosan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SAR_supergroup) group called the [Ciliophora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliate).
pseudoculus (plural pseudoculi, ) is the name applied to various [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye)-like structures which are nevertheless not eyes.

Pseudocyphellae (singular pseudocyphella) are structures in [lichen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lichen)s that appear as tiny pores on the outer surface (the [cortex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cortex_(botany))) of the lichen.

pseudopod or pseudopodium (: pseudopods or pseudopodia) is a temporary arm-like projection of an [eukaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic) [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_membrane) that is emerged in the direction of movement.

Pseudopolyps are projecting masses of [scar tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scar) that develop from [granulation tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granulation_tissue) during the [healing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Healing) phase in repeated cycle of [ulceration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulceration) (especially in [inflammatory bowel disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammatory_bowel_disease)) .
pseudopupil appears as a dark spot which moves across the eye as the animal is rotated.

pterostigma (plural: pterostigmata) is a group of specialized cells in the outer [wing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect_wing)s of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s, which are often thickened or coloured, and thus stand out from other cells.

media.file: Raphidia ophiopsis M NL-Doorwerth-19540617 right wing - collection Naturalis.jpg

definition: ptilinum is an eversible pouch on the head, above the base of the [antenna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antenna_(biology)) in [schizophoran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Schizophora) [flies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diptera) (a [section](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Section_(biology)) of [muscomorphan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscomorpha) and [cyclorrhaphan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyclorrhapha) flies).
ptotic chin is a [chin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chin) that droops over the [jawline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawline).
pugmark is a [footprint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Footprint) left by a wild animal.

pulmonary alveolus (; ), also called an air sac or air space, is one of millions of hollow, distensible cup-shaped cavities in the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s where pulmonary gas exchange takes place.

pulmonary artery is an [artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artery) in the [pulmonary circulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_circulation) that carries deoxygenated [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) from the right side of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) to the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s.
Pulmonary artery stenosis (PAS) is a narrowing of the [pulmonary artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_artery).
Pulmonary bay is a medical term which describes a finding on the [chest radiograph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chest_radiograph).

Pulmonary pathology is the subspecialty of [surgical pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgical_pathology) which deals with the [diagnosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis) and characterization of [neoplastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasia) and non-neoplastic [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease)s of the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s and [thoracic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax) [pleura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleura).

pulmonary valve (sometimes referred to as the pulmonic valve) is a [valve of the heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_valve) that lies between the [right ventricle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_ventricle) and the [pulmonary artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_artery), and has three cusps.

pulmonary veins are the [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vein)s that transfer [[Blood#bloodtransport|oxygenated blood]] from the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s to the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart).

pulp is the [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue), [nerves](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerves), [blood vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessels), and [odontoblast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Odontoblast)s that comprise the innermost layer of a [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth).
Pulpitis is [inflammation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inflammation) of [dental pulp](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dental_pulp) tissue.
Pump-handle is a movement of the [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib)s that results in a change in the anteroposterior diameter of the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax).

Pycnidium (plural pycnidia) is a type of [conidioma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conidioma), or [asexual reproductive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asexual_reproduction) structure, found in many [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi), especially [ascomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascomycete)s.

media.file: Diseases of greenhouse crops and their control (1920) (20781722020).jpg

definition: pygidium (: pygidia) is the posterior body part or shield of [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s and some other [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s, such as [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s and the extinct [trilobite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trilobite)s.
quadrangular space, also known as the quadrilateral of Velpeau and the foramen humerotricipitale, is one of the three spaces in the [axillary space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axillary_space).

Quantasomes are particles found in the [thylakoid membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thylakoid_membrane) of [chloroplast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroplast)s in which [photosynthesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photosynthesis) takes place.

R bodies (from refractile bodies, also R-bodies) are polymeric protein [inclusions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inclusion_body) formed inside the [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).

radial plane is an [anatomical plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_plane) that is used to describe a virtual slice along a [radius](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radius) of a somewhat [cylindrical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cylindrical) shaped body part.
radial styloid process is a projection of [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) on the lateral surface of the distal [radius bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radius_(bone)).
radiate carpal ligament is a group of about seven fibrous bands which diverge in all directions on the palmar surface of the carpal bones.

radicle is the first part of a [seedling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seedling) to emerge from the [seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed), during the process of [germination](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Germination).

ramification is the divergence of the [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem) and limbs of a [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant) into smaller ones, i.e., [trunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunk_(botany)) into [branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch)es, branches into increasingly smaller branches, and so on.

categories: Jodrell Professors of Zoology and Comparative Anatomy

definition: raptorial implies much the same as [predator](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Predator)y but most often refers to modifications of an [arthropod's foreleg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod_leg) that make it function for the grasping of prey while it is consumed, where the gripping surfaces are formed from the opposing faces of two successive leg [segments](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Segmentation_(biology)) (see illustration).

definition: receptacle refers to vegetative tissues near the end of reproductive stems that are situated below or encase the reproductive organs.

rectosigmoid junction, formerly the rectosigmoid sphincter or sphincter of O'Beirne, is the junction of the [sigmoid colon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sigmoid_colon) and the [rectum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rectum).

red pulp of the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) is composed of [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) known also as the [cords of Billroth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cords_of_Billroth) and many splenic [sinusoids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinusoid_(blood_vessel)) that are engorged with blood, giving it a red color.

Reinke crystals are rod-like [cytoplasmic inclusions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasmic_inclusions) which can be found in [Leydig cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leydig_cell)s of the [testes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testes).
Reinke's space is a potential space between the vocal ligament and the overlying mucosa.
renal [calyces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calyx_(anatomy)) ( calyx) are conduits in the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) through which urine passes.

renal capsule is a tough fibrous layer surrounding the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) and covered in a layer of perirenal fat known as the [adipose capsule of kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adipose_capsule_of_kidney).

renal cortex is the outer portion of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) between the [renal capsule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_capsule) and the [renal medulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_medulla).

renal fascia is a dense, [elastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elastic_connective_tissue) [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) envelope enclosing the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) and [adrenal gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adrenal_gland), together with the layer of [perirenal fat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perirenal_fat) surrounding these two.

renal hilum is the recessed central fissure of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) where its vessels, [nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nerve)s and [ureter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ureter) (renal pedicle) pass.
renal medulla (Latin: medulla renis 'marrow of the kidney') is the innermost part of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney).

Renal pathology is a subspecialty of [anatomic pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomic_pathology) that deals with the [diagnosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis) and characterization of [medical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_medicine) [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease)s (non-tumor) of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney)s.
renal pelvis or pelvis of the kidney is the funnel-like dilated part of the [ureter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ureter) in the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney).

renal sinus is a cavity within the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney) which is occupied by the [renal pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_pelvis), [renal calyces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_calyx), blood vessels, nerves and fat.

reniculate kidney is a multilobed [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammalian_kidney) found in [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_mammal) and [aquatic mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aquatic_mammal)s such as [pinniped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinniped)s ([seal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pinniped)s, [sea lion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_lion)s and [walrus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Walrus)es) and [cetacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cetacean)s ([dolphin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dolphin)s and [whale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whale)s) but absent in terrestrial mammals except [bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bear)s.

Resin canals or resin ducts are [fusiform](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fusiform) intercellular spaces surrounded by [epithelial cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium) which secrete [resin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resin).
