definition: resonating device is a structure used by an [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal) that improves the quality of its [vocalizations](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal_communication) through amplifying the sound produced via [acoustic resonance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acoustic_resonance).

respiratory system is the system with which it introduces respiratory [gas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas)es to its interior and performs [gas exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_exchange).
respiratory system of the horse is the biological system by which a [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) circulates air for the purpose of gaseous exchange.

respiratory tract is the subdivision of the [respiratory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system) involved with the process of conducting air to the [alveoli](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonary_alveolus) for the purposes of [gas exchange](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gas_exchange) in [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.
resting spore is a resistant cell, adapted to survive adverse environmental conditions.

Resupination is derived from the [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) word resupinus, meaning ==References== [[Category:Plant morphology]] [[Category:Fungal morphology and anatomy]] guxt02mwq5l8mg6hhelhxtkyxn0257b

rete mirabile ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) for 'wonderful net'; : retia mirabilia) is a complex of [arteries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Artery) and [vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vein)s lying very close to each other, found in some [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s, mainly [warm-blooded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Warm-blooded) ones.
Reticulocytosis is a laboratory finding in which the number of [reticulocytes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reticulocyte) (immature red blood cells) in the bloodstream is elevated.
reticuloendothelial system (abbreviated RES) is a network of immune cells distributed throughout the body that defends against foreign invaders, clears cellular debris, and recycles iron.
reticulum is the second chamber in the four-chamber [alimentary canal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alimentary_canal) of a [ruminant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruminant) mammal.

Horizontal cells are the laterally interconnecting neurons having cell bodies in the [inner nuclear layer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inner_nuclear_layer) of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) eyes.
retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) or nerve fiber layer, stratum opticum, is part of the [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).
Retinal precursor cells are biological cells that differentiate into the various cell types of the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) during development.

Retinal waves are spontaneous bursts of [action potentials](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Action_potentials) that propagate in a wave-like fashion across the developing [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina).

Retromer is a complex of [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s that has been shown to be important in recycling [transmembrane receptors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transmembrane_receptors) from [endosome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endosome)s to the [trans-Golgi network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golgi_apparatus) (TGN) and directly back to the plasma membrane.

definition: retromolar fossa is a [fossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fossa_(anatomy)) of the [mandible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandible) located [posteriorly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Posterior_(anatomy)) to the [third molar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Third_molar).

Rhabdites (from Greek, rhabdos, rod) are rodlike structures in the cells of the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(skin)) or underlying parenchyma in certain [turbellarians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turbellarians), and in the epidermis of [nemertea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nemertea)ns.

Rhabdomyosarcoma (RMS) is a highly aggressive form of [cancer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cancer) that develops from [mesenchymal cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesenchymal_cell)s that have failed to fully differentiate into [myocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myocyte)s of [skeletal muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skeletal_muscle).

rhinophore is one of a pair of [chemosensory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chemoreceptor) club-shaped, rod-shaped or ear-like structures which are the most prominent part of the external head anatomy in [sea slugs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_slugs), [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_(ocean)) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [opisthobranch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opisthobranch) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s such as the [nudibranchs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nudibranchs), sea hares ([Aplysiomorpha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aplysiomorpha)), and sap-sucking sea slugs ([Sacoglossa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacoglossa)).
rhizines are [multicellular](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism) [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)-like structures arising mainly from the lower surface.

Rhizoids are [[wiktionary:protuberance|protuberances]] that extend from the lower [epidermal cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(botany)) of [bryophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryophyte)s and [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae).

rhizoplast (also known as internal flagellar root, fibrous root or cross-banded root) is an [organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organelle) present in a variety of [flagellate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flagellate)s, including [ochrophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ochrophyte) and [chlorophyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chlorophyte) algae and some [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi).

rhombus of Michaelis, also known as the Michaelis-Raute or the quadrilateral of Michaelis, is a [rhombus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rhombus)-shaped contour (also referred to as kite-shaped or diamond-shaped) that is sometimes visible on the lower human back.
categories: Anatomy named for one who described it

definition: Rhopalia (; ) are small [sensory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sense) [organs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(biology)) of certain [Scyphozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scyphozoa)n (true jellyfish) and Cubozoan ([box jellyfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Box_jellyfish)) species.

ribs () are the long curved [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)s which form the [rib cage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib_cage), part of the [axial skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axial_skeleton).

rib cage or thoracic cage is an [endoskeletal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endoskeletal) enclosure in the [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax) of most [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s that comprises the [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib)s, [vertebral column](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebral_column) and [sternum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sternum), which protect the [vital organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vital_organ)s of the [thoracic cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoracic_cavity), such as the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart), [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung)s and [great vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_vessels) and support the [shoulder girdle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder_girdle) to form the [core](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Core_(anatomy)) part of the [axial skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axial_skeleton).

definition: Robert Douglas Lockhart (1894–1987) was a 20th-century Scottish anatomist.

Rod cells are [photoreceptor cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photoreceptor_cell)s in the [retina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retina) of the eye that can function in lower [light](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Light) better than the other type of visual photoreceptor, [cone cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cone_cell)s.

Romanowsky staining is a prototypical [staining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staining_(biology)) technique that was the forerunner of several distinct but similar stains widely used in [hematology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hematology) (the study of blood) and [cytopathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytopathology) (the study of diseased cells).

definition: root canal is the naturally occurring [anatomic space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomic_space) within the root of a [tooth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tooth).
Root hairs or absorbent hairs, are outgrowths of epidermal cells, specialized cells at the tip of a plant [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root).

root of the lung is a group of structures that emerge at the [hilum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hilum_(anatomy)) of each [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_lung), just above the middle of the [mediastinal surface](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mediastinal_surface) and behind the [cardiac impression](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_impression_on_lung) of the lung.

definition: Rostrum (from [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) ', meaning [[:wikt:beak|beak]]) is a term used in [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) for several kinds of hardened, or bony, [beak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beak)-like structures or extensions projecting out from the skull or mouthparts of an animal.
rugae (: ruga) are a series of ridges produced by folding of the wall of an [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)).
rumen, also known as a paunch, is the largest stomach compartment in [ruminant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruminant)s.

Rumpless chickens are characterised by [caudal dysplasia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caudal_dysplasia), the absence of the [pygostyle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pygostyle) or caudal appendage – the }} [[Category:Mutation]] [[Category:Animal anatomy]] [[Category:Chicken breeds]] 1wx8soq4o2r5n0pwn0cy9hiy5rj9m01

S-layer (surface layer) is a part of the [cell envelope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_envelope) found in almost all [archaea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archaea), as well as in many types of [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).

sacrococcygeal membrane is a tough fibrous [membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_membrane) about 10mm long which extends from the inferior tip of the [sacrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sacrum) to the body of the [coccyx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coccyx) in humans.
Saefftigen's pouch is an anatomical feature found in male [Acanthocephala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acanthocephala)ns.

definition: Sala Lancisiana is a [renaissance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renaissance) building located in [Rome](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rome), part of the hospital of [San Giacomo degli Incurabili](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Giacomo_degli_Incurabili), and site of an [anatomical theatre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_theatre).
salpinx is used to refer to a type of tube.

sapheno-femoral junction (SFJ) is located at the [saphenous opening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saphenous_opening) within the groin and formed by the meeting of the [great saphenous vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_saphenous_vein) (GSV), [common femoral vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_femoral_vein) and the superficial inguinal veins (confluens venosus subinguinalis).
sarcoma is a rare type of cancer that arises from [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) of [mesenchymal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesenchyme) origin.
Sarcoplasm is the [cytoplasm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoplasm) of a [muscle cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle_cell).

definition: [Sauropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda) neck posture is a subject occasionally debated among scientists, with some favoring postures closer to horizontal whilst others a more upright posture.

scale (; ) is a small rigid [plate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plate_(animal_anatomy)) made out of [keratin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keratin) that grows out of [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) [animals](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animals)' [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin) to provide protection.

definition: scapular line, also known as the midscapular line or linea scapularis, is a vertical line passing through the [inferior angle of the scapula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inferior_angle_of_the_scapula).

scapulocoracoid is the unit of the [pectoral girdle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoral_girdle) that contains the [coracoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coracoid) and [scapula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapula).
scapulohumeral muscles are a group of seven muscles that connect the [humerus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humerus) to the [scapula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapula).
Scent gland are [exocrine gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exocrine_gland)s found in most [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.

Schaumann bodies are calcium and protein [inclusions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inclusion_body) inside of [Langhans giant cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Langhans_giant_cell)s as part of a [granuloma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Granuloma).

definition: Schlemm's canal, also known as the canal of Schlemm, and as the scleral venous sinus, is a circular [lymphatic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymph)-like vessel in the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye).

definition: Schmorl's nodes are protrusions of the [[intervertebral disc#Structure|nucleus pulposus]] of the [intervertebral disc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Intervertebral_disc) through the [vertebral body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebral_body) [[vertebra#Structure|endplate]] and into the adjacent [vertebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebra).

sclera,{{notetag|1=The word sclera ( or ; both are common), plural sclerae ( or ) or scleras, is from the Greek (sklērós), meaning hard.

scleral ring (also sclerotic ring) is a hardened ring of plates, often derived from [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone), found in the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye) of [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s in several groups of [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.

scleral spur in the [visual system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Visual_system) is a protrusion of the [sclera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclera) (the white of the eye) into the [anterior chamber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_chamber).

Sclereids are a reduced form of [sclerenchyma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclerenchyma) cells with highly thickened, lignified [cellular walls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_wall) that form small bundles of durable layers of tissue in most [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s.

sclerite ([Greek](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greek_language) , ', meaning [[File:Chrysomallon squamiferum 2.png|thumb|The [scaly-foot gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scaly-foot_gastropod) is the only gastropod with sclerites.]] ==References== [[Category:Arthropod anatomy]] [[Category:Sponge anatomy]] [[Category:Mollusc anatomy]] 7bfvg6cuuzv7160rlchmfvjpkkv4fqr

Sclerochronology is the study of periodic physical and chemical features in the hard tissues of animals that grow by accretion, including [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate)s and coralline red algae, and the temporal context in which they formed.
sclerotium (; : sclerotia () is a compact mass of hardened fungal [mycelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycelium) containing food reserves.
scolopidium (historically, scolopophore) is the fundamental unit of a [mechanoreceptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanoreceptor) organ in [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s.
scur is an incompletely developed [horn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horn_(anatomy)) growth.

scutellum is the posterior portion of either the [mesonotum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesonotum) or the [metanotum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metanotum) of an [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax_(insect_anatomy)); however, it is used almost exclusively in the former context, as the metanotum is rather reduced in most insect groups.

definition: Secarecytosis is a process involved in the development of a bird's lung cells, before the bird hatches from its egg.

secondary cell wall is a structure found in many [plant cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell)s, located between the [primary cell wall](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_cell_wall) and the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane).

secondary growth is the growth that results from [cell division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_division) in the [cambia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cambium_(botany)) or lateral [meristems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meristems) and that causes the [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem)s and [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)s to thicken.

Secotioid fungi produce an intermediate fruiting body form that is between the mushroom-like [hymenomycete](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymenomycete)s and the closed bag-shaped [gasteromycetes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gasteroid_fungi), where an evolutionary process of gasteromycetation has started but not run to completion.

Segmental analysis is a method of [anatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical) analysis for describing the connective [morphology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) of the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body).

Sellar region is a small area in the [central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_nervous_system) (CNS) that includes the [sella turcica](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sella_turcica), [cavernous sinus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cavernous_sinus), suprasellar cistern, and [pituitary gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pituitary_gland).

Semi-slugs, also spelled semislugs, are land [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod)s whose [shells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell) are too small for them to retract into, but not quite [vestigial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vestigiality).

Semper's organ is an [anatomical structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy), a [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland) located in the [head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head) of some [land snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Land_snail)s, [pulmonate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulmonata) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s.

definition: Septate junctions are intercellular junctions found in [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate) epithelial cells, appearing as ladder-like structures under [electron microscopy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Electron_microscope).

septum ([Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin_language) for something that encloses; septa) is a wall, dividing a [cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_cavity) or structure into smaller ones.
septum (plural septa) is one of the radiating vertical plates lying within the [corallite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corallite) wall.

septum glandis, also septum of the glans, refers to the [fibrous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fiber) partition of the ventral aspect of the [glans penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glans_penis) that separates the two glans wings in the ventral midline.

Serial homology is a special type of [homology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homology_(biology)), defined by Owen as demonstrating that shared developmental pathways structure the covariation of serially homologous limbs.
setae (; seta ; ) are any of a number of different bristle- or [hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair)-like structures on living [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s.

Sexual characteristics are physical traits of an [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism) (typically of a [sexually dimorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sexually_dimorphic) organism) which are indicative of or resultant from biological [sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex)ual factors.

Sexual dimorphism is the condition where different [sex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sex)es of the same [species](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Species) exhibit different [morphological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphology_(biology)) characteristics, including characteristics not directly involved in [reproduction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproduction).
sickle tail is the single [phenotypic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phenotypic) characteristic that seems to separate dogs from wolves.

Sieve elements or sieve tube elements are specialized cells that are important for the function of [phloem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phloem), which is a highly organized tissue that transports organic compounds made during photosynthesis.
simian shelf is a bony thickening on the front of the ape [mandible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mandible).

Simon focus is a [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis) (TB) nodule that can form in the [apex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apex_of_the_lung) of the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung) when a primary TB infection elsewhere in the body spreads to the lung apex via the bloodstream.
Simon Henry Parson (born 23 May 1966) is a British [anatomist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomist).

sinoatrial node (also known as the sinuatrial node, SA node, sinus node or Keith–Flack node) is an [oval shaped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ellipse) region of special [cardiac muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle) in the upper back wall of the [right atrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_atrium) made up of [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) known as [pacemaker cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacemaker_cell)s.

Sinodonty and Sundadonty are two patterns of features widely found in the [dentition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dentition)s of the populations of [East Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/East_Asian_people) and [Southeast Asia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Southeast_Asia) respectively.
sinus is a sac or cavity in any [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) or [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_tissue), or an abnormal cavity or passage.

siphon is an anatomical structure which is part of the body of aquatic [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s in three [class](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_(biology))es: [Gastropoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropoda), [Bivalvia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalvia) and [Cephalopoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cephalopoda) (members of these classes include saltwater and [freshwater snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater_snail)s, [clams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clams), [octopus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Octopus), [squid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squid) and relatives).

siphon is a tubular organ of the [respiratory system of some insects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system_of_insects) that spend a significant amount of their time underwater, that serves as a breathing tube.

siphonal canal is an anatomical feature of the [shells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell) of certain groups of [sea snails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_snails) within the clade [Neogastropoda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neogastropoda).

siphonal notch is a feature of the [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell) anatomy in some [sea snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_snail)s, [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_(ocean)) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s.

siphonoglyph is a [cilia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cilia)ted groove at one or both ends of the mouth of [sea anemone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_anemone)s and some [coral](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coral)s.

Sister Mary Joseph nodule (sometimes Sister Mary Joseph node or Sister Mary Joseph sign) refers to a palpable nodule bulging into the [umbilicus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navel) as a result of [metastasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metastasis) of a malignant cancer in the pelvis or abdomen through the [round ligament of liver](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Round_ligament_of_liver).
categories: Anatomy named for one who described it

definition: Situs solitus () is the medical term referring to the normal position of [thoracic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax) and [abdominal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdomen) organs.

definition: Skeletal pneumaticity is the presence of air spaces within bones.
skeleton is the [structural frame](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Structural_frame) that supports the body of most [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s.

categories: Anatomy named for one who described it
related: List of related male and female reproductive organs

definition: Skin is the layer of usually soft, flexible outer [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) covering the body of a [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) animal, with three main functions: protection, regulation, and sensation.
Skin folds or skinfolds are areas of [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin) that are naturally folded.

skull, or cranium, is typically a [bony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) enclosure around the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain) of a [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate).

skull roof or the roofing bones of the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) are a set of [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)s covering the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain), [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye)s and [nostril](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nostril)s in [bony fishes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bony_fishes), including [land-living vertebrates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapods).
slime coat (also fish slime, mucus layer or slime layer) is the coating of [mucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucus) covering the body of all [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish).

media.file: Eldon's galaxias (Galaxias eldoni) - closeup of skin.jpg

definition: slit sensilla, also known as the slit sense organ, is a small [mechanoreceptory](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mechanoreceptory) organ or group of organs in the [exoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoskeleton) of [arachnid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arachnid)s which detects [physical deformation or strain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deformation_(mechanics)) due to forces experienced by the animal.

Snail slime is a kind of [mucus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mucus) (an external bodily [secretion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretion)) produced by [snails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snails), which are [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusk)s.

Snakeskin may refer to the skin of a live [snake](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snake), the shed skin of a snake after [molting](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Moulting), or to a type of leather that is made from the [hide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hide_(skin)) of a dead snake.

definition: snout is the protruding portion of an animal's face, consisting of its nose, mouth, and jaw.
Store-operated channels (SOCs) are [ion channel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ion_channel)s located in the [plasma membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plasma_membrane) of cells.

term: Sociopolitical issues of anatomy in America in the 19th century

definition: Soft tissue pathology is the subspecialty of [surgical pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgical_pathology) which deals with the [diagnosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diagnosis) and characterization of [neoplastic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neoplasia) and non-neoplastic [disease](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Disease)s of the [soft tissues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Soft_tissues), such as [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle), [adipose tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adipose_tissue), [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon)s, [fascia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fascia), and [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue)s.

somatomammotroph or somatomammotrophic cell, also known as a somatolactotroph or somatolactotrophic cell, is a type of [cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) of the [anterior pituitary gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_pituitary_gland) that produces both [somatotropin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somatotropin) (growth hormone) and [prolactin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prolactin).

southern resident orcas, also known as the southern resident killer whales (SRKW), are the smallest of four communities of the exclusively fish-eating [ecotype](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ecotype) of [orca](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orca) in the northeast Pacific Ocean.

Specific leaf area (SLA) is the quotient of [leaf](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leaf) area to leaf [dry mass](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dry_mass); it has [SI units](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SI_units) of square centimeters per kilogram (cm²/kg).

spermatophylax is a [gelatinous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gelatine) [bolus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bolus_(digestion)) which some male [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s eject during [copulation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Copulation_(zoology)) with females through their [aedeagi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aedeagus) together with [spermatophore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spermatophore)s, and which functions as a [nutritive](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nutrition) supplement for the female.

sphaeroblast is a woody extrusion from the [trunk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Trunk_(botany)) or [branch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Branch) of a [tree](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tree), usually taking the form of a rounded spherical shape, as if the tree had a boil or mole.

sphincter of Boyden (also known as the choledochal sphincter) is a [sphincter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphincter) located in the [common bile duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Common_bile_duct) before it joins with the [pancreatic duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pancreatic_duct) to form the [ampulla of vater](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ampulla_of_vater).
spicules, also known as copulatory spicules, are needle-like mating structures found only in males.

Spiculectomy is a minor soft-tissue [surgical procedure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgical_procedure) to remove a spicule or splinter, often a fragment of [toenail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nail_(anatomy)), penetrating the nail bed.

definition: Spider silk is a [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein) [fibre](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fibre) or [silk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Silk) spun by [spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider)s.

definition: Spidroins are the main [protein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protein)s in [spider silk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider_silk).

spinal column, also known as the vertebral column, spine or backbone, is the core part of the [axial skeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Axial_skeleton) in [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.

spindle apparatus is the [cytoskeletal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cytoskeletal) structure of [eukaryotic cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eukaryotic_cell)s that forms during [cell division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_division) to separate [sister chromatid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sister_chromatid)s between daughter [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)).

spinneret is a [silk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider_silk)-spinning [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) of a [spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider) or the [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva) of an [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect).

media.file: Australian garden orb weaver spider spinneret.jpg

definition: spiracle or stigma is the opening in the [exoskeleton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoskeleton)s of [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s, [myriapods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Myriapoda), [velvet worms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Onychophora) and many arachnids that admits air into the [respiratory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system_of_insects).

spiral valve or scroll valve is the corkscrew-shaped lower portion of the [intestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastrointestinal_tract) of some [shark](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shark)s, [Acipenseriformes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acipenseriformes) ([sturgeon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sturgeon) and [paddlefish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paddlefish)), [ray](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Batoidea)s, [skate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skate_(fish))s, [bichir](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bichir)s, [Lepisosteiformes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lepisosteiformes) (gars), and [lungfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lungfish)es.
spire is a part of the coiled [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoskeleton) of [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s.

Spitzenkörper ([German](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/German_language) for 'pointed body', SPK) is a structure found in fungal [hyphae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyphae) that is the organizing center for hyphal growth and [morphogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morphogenesis).
Splanchnic is usually used to describe organs in the [abdominal cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdomen).
splanchnocranium (or visceral skeleton) is the portion of the [cranium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranium) that is derived from [pharyngeal arch](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pharyngeal_arch)es.
Spleen () is one of the [zàng](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zang-fu) organs stipulated by [traditional Chinese medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Traditional_Chinese_medicine) (TCM).

Spleen pain is a pain felt from the left upper [quadrant of the abdomen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominal_pain) or [epigastrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epigastrium) where the human [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) is located or neighboring.
Spleen transplantation is the transfer of [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) or its fragments from one individual to another.
splenectomy is the [surgical procedure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Surgery) that partially or completely removes the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen).
splenic injury, which includes a ruptured spleen, is any injury to the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen).

splenorenal recess (perisplenic space, pouch of Koller, or Koller's pouch) is the [intraperitoneal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritoneal_cavity) compartment that separates the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) and the left [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney).
Splenosis is the result of [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen) tissue breaking off the main organ and implanting at another site inside the body.
spongocoel (), also called paragaster (or paragastric cavity), is the large, central cavity of [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge)s.

sporeling is a young plant or fungus produced by a germinated [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore), similar to a [seedling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seedling) derived from a germinated [seed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Seed).

Sporidia are result of [homokaryotic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Homokaryotic) [smut fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smut_fungi) (which are not [pathogenic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pathogenic)), asexual reproduction through the process of [budding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Budding).

sporocarp (also known as fruiting body, fruit body or fruitbody) of [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) is a [multicellular structure](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Multicellular_organism) on which [spore-producing structures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporangium), such as [basidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidium) or [asci](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ascus), are borne.
spur is an outgrowth of [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) covered in a sheath of [horn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Keratin) found in various anatomical locations in some animals.

definition: squamae are small tubercles resembling scales on the sole of the hindfeet.

definition: stamen (: stamina or stamens) is a part consisting of the male [reproductive organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_organ)s of a flower.
staminode is an often rudimentary, sterile or abortive [stamen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stamen), which means that it does not produce [pollen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pollen).

standard anatomical position, or standard anatomical model, is the scientifically agreed upon reference position for [anatomical location terms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_terms_of_location).

Statoblasts are a means to reproduce [asexually](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Asexuality) by a method that is unique among [bryozoa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bryozoa)ns and enables a [colony's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Colony_(biology)) lineage to survive the variable and uncertain conditions of [fresh water](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fresh_water) environments.

statocyst is a [balance sensory receptor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Equilibrioception) present in some aquatic [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate)s, including [bivalve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalve)s, ==See also== *[Accelerometer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accelerometer) *[Inertial guidance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inertial_guidance) *[Müllerian vesicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Müllerian_vesicle), similar structure in [loxodid ciliates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Loxodidae) *[Otolith](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Otolith), an equivalent structure in vertebrates.
stay apparatus is an arrangement of muscles, tendons, and ligaments that work together so that an animal can remain standing with virtually no muscular effort.

Steatopygia is the state of having substantial levels of tissue on the [buttocks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buttocks) and thighs leading to a protruding 90-degree angled appearance and accompanied by [lordosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lordosis).

stele (also called vascular stele or vascular cylinder) is the central part of the [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root) or [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem) containing the tissues derived from the procambium.

Stenotic nares means the [nares](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nares) (nostrils) are pinched or narrow, making it more difficult for an animal to breathe, and resulting in a lot of open-mouth breathing and panting.
Stereocilia (or stereovilli or villi) are non-motile apical cell modifications.

Stereom is a [calcium carbonate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcium_carbonate) material that makes up the internal skeletons found in all [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinoderm)s, both living and fossilized forms.
Sternal foramen (or perforated sternum) is an oval foramen present at lower one-third of the sternum.

rectus sternalis muscle is an [anatomical variation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_variation) that lies in front of the sternal end of the [pectoralis major](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectoralis_major_muscle) parallel to the margin of the [sternum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sternum).

sternoclavicular joint or sternoclavicular articulation is a [synovial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_joint) [saddle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saddle_joint) [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) between the [[sternum#Manubrium|manubrium of the sternum]], and the [clavicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavicle_bone), and the first [costal cartilage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costal_cartilage).

sternocostal joints, also known as sternochondral joints or costosternal articulations, are [synovial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_joint) [plane joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plane_joint)s of the [costal cartilage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costal_cartilage)s of the [true ribs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib) with the [sternum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sternum).

A Mesosternum, B Metasternum, 1 first abdominal sternite, 2-6 rest of sternites]] The sternum (: sterna) is the [[Anatomical_terms_of_location#Dorsal_and_ventral|ventral]] portion of a segment of an [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod) [thorax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thorax_(arthropod_anatomy)) or [[Abdomen#Arthropoda|abdomen]].

Stichocytes are glandular unicellular cells arranged in a row along the posterior portion of the [oesophagus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oesophagus), each of which communicates by a single pore with the lumen of the oesophagus.

stichosome (from Greek stichos (στίχος) = row; soma (σῶμα) = body) is a multicellular organ that is very prominent in some species of [nematode](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nematode)s and consists of a longitudinal series of glandular unicellular cells ([stichocyte](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stichocyte)s) arranged in a row along the [oesophagus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oesophagus) that forms the posterior esophageal glands.

stifle joint (often simply stifle) is a complex [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) in the [hind limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hind_limb)s of [quadruped](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Quadruped) [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s such as the [sheep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheep), [horse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Horse) or [dog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dog).

stinger (or sting) is a sharp [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) found in various [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s (typically [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s and other [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s) capable of injecting [venom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venom), usually by piercing the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis) of another animal.
stipe () is the stem or stalk-like feature supporting the [cap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pileus_(mycology)) of a [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom).

stomatogastric ganglion (STG) is a much-studied [ganglion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganglion) (collection of [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s) found in [arthropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropods) and studied extensively in [decapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Decapoda) [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s.

Stomatogastric Nervous System (STNS) is a commonly studied [neural network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neural_network) composed of several [ganglia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ganglion) in [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod)s that controls the motion of the gut and foregut.

stratum basale (basal layer, sometimes referred to as stratum germinativum) is the deepest layer of the five layers of the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis), the external covering of [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin) in [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s.

stratum granulosum (or granular layer) is a thin layer of cells in the [epidermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epidermis_(skin)) lying above the [stratum spinosum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum_spinosum) and below the [stratum corneum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum_corneum) ([stratum lucidum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stratum_lucidum) on the soles and palms).

Streptoneury or chiastoneury is a [plesiomorphic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Symplesiomorphy) condition present in all [gastropods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropoda) which is a result of an evolutionary event called [torsion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Torsion_(gastropod)) in which the intestines, heart, [nephridia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nephridium), gills, and nerve cords ==References== [[Category:Gastropod anatomy]] t03323cjkz0ld4lotlgtuhy4jxrtm15

definition: stromule is a [microscopic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microscopy) tubular process extending from [plastid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plastid)s in [plant cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell)s.
stylet is a hard, sharp, anatomical structure found in some [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate)s.

stylophthalmine trait is an adaptation present in the [larvae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish_larva) of several different species of [actinopterygian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Actinopterygian) fish.
Subareolar lymphatic plexus, also known as Sappey's plexus is the lymphatic drainage of the areola of the breast.
subcoracoid bursa or subcoracoid bursa of Collas is a [synovial bursa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synovial_bursa) located in the [shoulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder).
Suberin is a lipophilic, complex polyester [biopolymer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biopolymer) found in plants.

definition: suboesophageal ganglion (acronym: SOG; synonym: subesophageal ganglion) of arthropods and in particular insects is part of the [arthropod central nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod_central_nervous_system) (CNS).

subpulmonic effusion is excess fluid that collects at the base of the [lung](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung), in the space between the [pleura](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pleura) and diaphragm.
subradular organ is a sensory organ below the grinding mouthparts ([radula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radula)) of some molluscs, specifically the [chiton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chiton)s.
subsporangial vesicle is a vesicle which is below the [sporangium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporangium) on a [fungus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus).
substomatal cavity is the cavity located immediately [[Anatomical terms of location#Proximal and distal|proximal]] to the [stoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stoma).
sucker in [zoology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zoology) is a specialised attachment organ of an animal.

definition: Sugiura procedure is a surgical technique that involves the removal and transection of the blood vessels that supply the upper portion of the [stomach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stomach) and the [esophagus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Esophagus).
sulcus () is a furrow or fissure (; ).
Sulcus subtarsalis is a groove in the inner surface of [eyelid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eyelid) near the eyelid margin and which is also parallel to it.
supercilium is a [plumage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plumage) feature found on the heads of some [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird) species.

superficial cervical fascia is a thin layer of subcutaneous [connective tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Connective_tissue) that lies between the [dermis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dermis) of the skin and the [deep cervical fascia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deep_cervical_fascia).

superior costotransverse ligament is a ligament of the [costotransverse joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costotransverse_joint) that attaches onto the crest of the neck of a rib, and onto the [transverse process](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transverse_process) of the [vertebra](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebra) superior to the rib.

superior extensor retinaculum of the foot (transverse crural ligament) is the upper part of the [extensor retinaculum of foot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inferior_extensor_retinaculum_of_foot) which extends from the [ankle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankle) to the [heelbone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heelbone).

superior ligament of the epididymis is a strand of fibrous tissue which is covered by a reflection of the [tunica vaginalis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tunica_vaginalis) and connects the upper aspect of the [epididymis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epididymis) with the [testis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Testis).
superior thoracic aperture, also known as the thoracic outlet, or thoracic inlet refers to the opening at the top of the [thoracic cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoracic_cavity).
supine position () means lying horizontally, with the face and torso facing up, as opposed to the [prone position](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prone_position), which is face down.

suprachoroid The spaces between the lamellae are lined by [endothelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Endothelium), and open freely into the [perichoroidal lymph space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perichoroidal_lymph_space), which, in its turn, communicates with the [periscleral space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Periscleral_lymph_space) by the perforations in the [sclera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclera) through which the vessels and nerves are transmitted.

supracondylar process of the humerus (also known as an avian spur) is a variant bony projection on the anteromedial aspect of the upper arm bone ([humerus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Humerus)), about 5–6 and/or [ischemia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ischemia).

Supracristal plane (Planum supracristale) (or supracrestal plane) is an anatomical [transverse plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transverse_plane) lying at the upper most part of the [pelvis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvis), the [iliac crest](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iliac_crest).
suprapedal gland or mucous pedal gland is an anatomical feature found in some [snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Snail)s and [slug](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Slug)s.

supratemporal bone is a paired [cranial](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) bone present in many [tetrapods](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod) and [tetrapodomorph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapodomorpha) [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish).
Surface anatomy (also called superficial anatomy and visual anatomy) is the study of the external features of the body of an animal.

definition: Surgical and Radiologic Anatomy is a [peer-reviewed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peer_review) [medical journal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_journal) that publishes original research and review articles on the bases of medical, surgical and radiologic anatomy.
Susan Standring is a British neuroscientist who is serving as the editor-in-chief of [Gray's Anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gray's_Anatomy), a reference book for human anatomy.

suspensor is a temporary [anatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy) structure in [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) and [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant)s that supports early development.

suture is a fairly rigid [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint) between two or more hard elements of an organism, with or without significant overlap of the elements.

definition: Symmetry in biology refers to the symmetry observed in [organism](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organism)s, including plants, animals, [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi), and [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria).
synovial sheath is one of the two membranes of a [tendon sheath](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon_sheath) which covers a tendon.

Systematized Nomenclature of Medicine (SNOMED) is a systematic, computer-processable collection of [medical terms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Medical_terms), in human and [veterinary medicine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Veterinary_medicine), to provide codes, terms, synonyms and definitions which cover [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy), [diseases](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diseases), findings, procedures, [microorganisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microorganisms), substances, etc.
t-shaped uterus is a type of [uterine malformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterine_malformation) wherein the uterus is shaped resembling the letter T.

T-tubules (transverse tubules) are extensions of the [cell membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcolemma) that penetrate into the center of [[Skeletal muscle#Skeletal muscle cells|skeletal]] and [cardiac muscle cell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cardiac_muscle_cell)s.

definition: tabular bones are a pair of triangular flat bones along the rear edge of the skull which form pointed structures known as tabular horns in primitive [Teleostomi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teleostomi).

Taenidia (singular: taenidium) are circumferential thickenings of the cuticle inside a [trachea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate_trachea) or tracheole in an [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)'s respiratory system.
tail of the horse and other equines consists of two parts, the [dock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rump_(animal)) and the skirt.

tail club is a [bony](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) mass at the end of the [tail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tail) of some extinct animal species, most notably the [ankylosaurids](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankylosauridae), some [sauropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauropoda)s, [glyptodont](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glyptodont)s, and some [meiolaniid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meiolaniidae) [turtle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turtle)s.

tapetum is a specialised layer of nutritive cells found within the [anther](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anther) of [flowering plants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flowering_plants), located between the [sporogenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sporogenesis) tissue and the anther wall.

tarsal tunnel is a passage found along the inner [leg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Leg) underneath the [medial malleolus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malleolus) of the [ankle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ankle).

teat is the projection from the [mammary gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammary_gland)s of [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s from which [milk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Milk) flows or is ejected for the purpose of feeding young.

definition: tegula is a small [sclerite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sclerite) situated above the base of the [costal vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Costal_vein) in the wings of various [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect)s such as [Orthoptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orthoptera), [Lepidoptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lepidoptera), [Hymenoptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hymenoptera), [Diptera](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Diptera), and [Auchenorrhyncha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auchenorrhyncha), and attached to the anterolateral portion of the [mesonotum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesonotum).

Tegument is a term in [helminthology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Helminthology) for the outer body covering of members of the [phylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phylum) [Platyhelminthes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Platyhelminthes).

Telecanthus, or dystopia canthorum, refers to increased distance between the inner corners of the eyelids (medial [canthi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Canthi)), while the [inter-pupillary distance](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Inter-pupillary_distance) is normal.

Teliospore (sometimes called teleutospore) is the thick-walled [resting spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Resting_spore) of some [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi) ([rusts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(fungus)) and [smuts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Smut_(fungus))), from which the [basidium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Basidium) arises.
Telium, plural telia, are structures produced by [rust fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(fungus)) as part of the [reproductive cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_cycle).
telson () is the hindmost division of the body of an [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod).

definition: temple, also known as the pterion, is a latch where four skull bones intersect: the [frontal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frontal_bone), [parietal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Parietal_bone), [temporal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temporal_bone), and [sphenoid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sphenoid_bone).

Temporal fenestrae are openings in the [temporal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Temple_(anatomy)) region of the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull) of some [amniotes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amniote), behind the [orbit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Orbit_(anatomy)) (eye socket).

temporomandibular joints (TMJ) are the two [joint](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joint)s connecting the [jawbone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jawbone) to the [skull](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skull).

Tenon's capsule (), also known as the Tenon capsule, fascial sheath of the eyeball () or the fascia bulbi, is a thin membrane which envelops the eyeball from the [optic nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optic_nerve) to the [corneal limbus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corneal_limbus), separating it from the orbital fat and forming a socket in which it moves.

tentacle is a flexible, mobile, and elongated [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) present in some species of [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s, most of them [invertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate)s.
tentorium (plural tentoria) is a term used to refer to the framework of internal supports within an [arthropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arthropod) head.

Terminal bar is a [histological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histology) term given to the [unresolved](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_resolution) group of [junctional complexes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Junctional_complexes) that attach adjacent [epithelial cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelial_cells) on their lateral surfaces: the [zonula occludens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zonula_occludens), [zonula adherens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zonula_adherens), [macula adherens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Desmosome) and [macula communicans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gap_junction).

Terminal cisternae (singular: terminal cisterna) are enlarged areas of the [sarcoplasmic reticulum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sarcoplasmic_reticulum) surrounding the [transverse tubules](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transverse_tubules).

Terminal end buds (TEBs) are highly [proliferative](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_proliferation) structures at the ends of elongating [lactiferous duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lactiferous_duct)s which are involved in development of the [mammary gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammary_gland)s.

terminal hair is a variant of hair that is thick and long such as that growing on the scalp, as compared with [vellus hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vellus_hair), colloquially known as peach fuzz, growing elsewhere.

terminal sulcus is a groove on the outer surface of the [right atrium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Right_atrium) of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) marking the transition between the [sinus venarum cavarum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sinus_venarum) (which has a distinct embryological origin) and the rest of the right atrium (which features [pectinate muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pectinate_muscle)s on its inner surface).
Terminologia Anatomica (commonly abbreviated TA) is the international standard for [human anatomical](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_anatomy) terminology.

Thylakoids are membrane-bound compartments inside [chloroplast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chloroplast)s and [cyanobacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cyanobacteria).
thymus (: thymuses or thymi) is a specialized [primary lymphoid organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Primary_lymphoid_organ) of the [immune system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Immune_system).
thyroid ima artery (thyroidea ima artery, arteria thyroidea ima, thyroid artery of Neubauer or the lowest thyroid artery) is an artery of the [[Head and neck anatomy#Blood supply|head and neck]].

Théophile Bonet (March 6, 1620 – March 29, 1689) was a Swiss physician and anatomist who is considered one of the founders of [anatomical pathology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_pathology).

Tibiofibular trunk (or tibioperoneal trunk) is an arterial trunk representing the direct continuation of the [popliteal artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popliteal_artery) distal to where the [anterior tibial artery](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_tibial_artery) (the first branch of the popliteal artery) branches off from it.

tibiotarsus is the large [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) between the [femur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femur) and the [tarsometatarsus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarsometatarsus) in the leg of a [bird](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bird).
Tiger eye or goat eye is a gene causing diluted eye color in horses.
