Tight junctions, also known as occluding junctions or zonulae occludentes (singular, zonula occludens), are multiprotein [junctional complex](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_junction)es between [epithelial cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelial_cells), == See also == * [Cadherin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cadherin) * [Gap junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gap_junction) * [Tight junction protein (disambiguation)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tight_junction_protein_(disambiguation)) * [Zonulin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zonulin) * [Adherens junction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Adherens_junction) == References == == External links == * [ht

Tissue culture is the growth of [tissues](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) or [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) in an artificial medium separate from the parent organism.

tomium is the sharp cutting edge of the [beak](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beak) ==See also== * [Culmen (bird)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Culmen_(bird)) * [Gonys](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonys) ==References== [[Category:Vertebrate anatomy]] g77o06qzd9rdqw3r8nyjmz8pklnwszr
Carcinoma of the tonsil is a type of [squamous cell carcinoma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Squamous_cell_carcinoma).

tooth (: teeth) is a hard, [calcified](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Calcification) structure found in the [jaw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaw)s (or [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth)s) of many [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s and used to [break down](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mastication) [food](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Food).

toothcomb (also called a tooth comb or dental comb) is a [dental](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dentition) structure found in some mammals, comprising a group of front teeth arranged in a manner that facilitates grooming, similar to a [hair comb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair_comb).
Toothlessness or edentulism is the condition of having no [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teeth).

media.file: Head of a toothless man with bare, sinewy neck in profile to left MET DP823720.jpg

definition: topographical code (or topography code) is a code that indicates a specific location in the body.

Torsion is a [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [synapomorphy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Synapomorphy) which occurs in all gastropods during [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva)l development.

torus semicircularis is a region of the [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) [midbrain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Midbrain) that contributes to [auditory perception](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Auditory_perception), studied most often in [fish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fish) and [amphibians](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Amphibian).

Total body surface area (TBSA) is an assessment of injury to or disease of the [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_skin), such as [burn](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burn_(injury))s or [psoriasis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Psoriasis).
trab is a structural element within a [sponge](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sponge) formed by the fusion of [dendroclone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dendroclone)s.

term: Trabeculae of corpora cavernosa of penis
page: Trabeculae of corpora cavernosa of penis
related: Trabeculae of corpus spongiosum of penis

term: Trabeculae of corpus spongiosum of penis
page: Trabeculae of corpus spongiosum of penis
related: Trabeculae of corpora cavernosa of penis

definition: Trabecular cartilages (trabeculae cranii, sometimes simply trabeculae, prechordal cartilages) are paired, rod-shaped cartilages, which develop in the [head](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Head) of the [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate) [embryo](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryo).

trabecular meshwork is an area of tissue in the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye) located around the base of the [cornea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cornea), near the [ciliary body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ciliary_body), and is responsible for draining the [aqueous humor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Aqueous_humor) from the eye via the [anterior chamber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anterior_chamber) (the chamber on the front of the eye covered by the cornea).

media.file: SD OCT - Anterior Chamber Angle Cross-Section (with viewfinder).png

definition: trabecular veins are the largest veins inside the [spleen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spleen).

media.file: Podocarpoxylon mcgeei radial section with tracheids Torrey 1923 Plate10 fig18.png

definition: Tracheole (trā'kē-ōl') is a fine respiratory tube of the [trachea](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Invertebrate_trachea) of an [insect](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insect) or a [spider](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spider), part of the [respiratory system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Respiratory_system_of_insects).

media.file: Naturalis Biodiversity Center - RMNH.ART.1394 - Stigmaeus humilis (C. L. Koch) - Mites - Collection Anthonie Cornelis Oudemans.jpeg

definition: trama is used in two ways.

Transcendental anatomy, also known as philosophical anatomy, was a form of [comparative anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Comparative_anatomy) that sought to find ideal patterns and structures common to all organisms in nature.

transpyloric plane, also known as Addison's plane, is an imaginary [horizontal plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transverse_plane), located halfway between the suprasternal notch of the manubrium and the upper border of the symphysis pubis at the level of the first lumbar vertebrae, L1.

transumbilical plane or umbilical plane, one of the [transverse plane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transverse_plane)s in human anatomy, is a horizontal line that passes through the abdomen at the level of the [navel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navel) (or umbilicus).
transverse plane is a plane that is rotated 90° from two other planes.
Traube's (semilunar) space is an [anatomic space](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spatium) of some clinical importance.

media.file: Tree fork wood grain anatomy, Slater and Ennos 2015.png

definition: Triangle of Doom is an anatomical triangle defined by the [vas deferens](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vas_deferens) medially, [gonadal vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gonadal_vessel) laterally and peritoneum inferiorly.

triangular fibrocartilage complex (TFCC) is formed by the triangular fibrocartilage discus (TFC), the [radioulnar ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Radioulnar_ligament_(disambiguation))s (RULs) and the [ulnocarpal ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulnocarpal_ligament_(disambiguation))s (UCLs).
Trichocyte in [algae](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Algae) are cells which grow on the outside of the [thallus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thallus), from which hairs grow.

Trichosclereids are hard needlelike branched [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) found in some species of plants that serve the purpose of protecting the plant from [herbivores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Herbivores).

Trichrome staining is a [histological](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Histological) [staining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staining) method that uses two or more [acid dye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Acid_dye)s in conjunction with a [polyacid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyacid).
Tripedalism (from the [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) tri = three + ped = foot) is locomotion by the use of three limbs.
triradiate pelvic girdle is a [shared feature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Apomorphy) common to [archosaur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Archosaur)s.

trochanter is a [tubercle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tubercle_(bone)) of the [femur](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Femur) near its joint with the [hip bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hip_bone).

media.file: Replica of Athenian trireme (trieres). Athens War Museum.jpg

definition: Trochlea (Latin for [pulley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pulley)) is a term in [anatomy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomy).
trophosome is a highly vascularised organ found in some animals that houses symbiotic [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria) that provide food for their host.

Tube feet (technically podia) are small active tubular projections on the oral face of an [echinoderm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Echinoderm), such as the arms of a [starfish](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Starfish), or the undersides of [sea urchin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_urchin)s, [sand dollar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sand_dollar)s and [sea cucumber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Holothuroidea)s; they are more discreet though present on [brittle star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brittle_star)s, and have only a feeding function in [feather star](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Feather_star)s.

media.file: Sea urchin Tube feet extended past the Spines.jpg

definition: tubercle (literally 'small tuber', Latin for 'lump') is any round [nodule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nodule_(medicine)), small [[wikt:eminence|eminence]], or [wart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wart)y outgrowth found on external or internal [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy))s of a plant or an animal.

Peripheral tuberculous lymphadenitis (or tuberculous adenitis) is a form of [tuberculosis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tuberculosis) infection occurring outside of the [lungs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lung).
tubule is a general term referring to small tube or similar type of structure.

Tubulin beta-3 chain, Class III β-tubulin, βIII-tubulin (β3-tubulin) or β-tubulin III, is a [microtubule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Microtubule) element of the [tubulin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tubulin) family found almost exclusively in [neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neuron)s, Dynamic microtubules are needed for the cell migration that underlies processes such as tumor metastasis and angiogenesis.

tunica albuginea is the fibrous envelope that extends the length of the [corpus cavernosum penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_cavernosum_penis) and [corpus spongiosum penis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Corpus_spongiosum_penis).

tunica vasculosa lentis is an extensive [capillary](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Capillary) network, spreading over the posterior and lateral surfaces of the lens of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_eye).

Tusks are elongated, continuously growing front [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teeth) that protrude well beyond the [mouth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mouth) of certain [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal) species.
tylosis (plural: tyloses) is a bladder-like distension of a [[Ground tissue#Parenchyma|parenchyma cell]] into the lumen of adjacent vessels.
tymbal (or timbal) is the corrugated [exoskeletal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exoskeleton) structure used to produce sounds in insects.

tympanal organ (or tympanic organ) is a hearing organ in [insects](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Insects), consisting of a tympanal membrane ([tympanum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tympanum_(anatomy))) stretched across a frame backed by an air sac and associated [sensory neuron](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sensory_neuron)s.

media.file: CSIRO ScienceImage 2673 The Hearing Organs of Two Moths.jpg

definition: type IX secretion system is a specialized protein [bacterial secretion system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacterial_secretion_system) found in the Fibrobacteres-Chlorobi-Bacteroidetes [superphylum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superphylum).
typhlosole is an internal fold of the [intestine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gut_(anatomy)) or intestine inner wall.

udder is an [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Organ_(anatomy)) formed of two or four [mammary glands](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammary_glands) on the females of dairy animals and [ruminant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ruminant)s such as [cattle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cattle), [goat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Goat)s, and [sheep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sheep).

styloid process of the ulna is a bony prominence found at [distal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anatomical_terms_of_location) end of the [ulna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ulna) in the [forearm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forearm).
ultimopharyngeal body, or ultimobranchial body or ultimobranchial gland is a small organ found in the neck region of many [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal)s.

Ultrastructure (or ultra-structure) is the architecture of cells and biomaterials that is visible at higher magnifications than found on a standard [optical light microscope](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Optical_light_microscope).
umbo is a raised area in the center of a [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom) cap.

uncinate processes of the ribs are extensions of [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) that project [caudally](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caudal_(anatomical_term)) from the vertical segment of each [rib](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rib).
ungual tufts are tufts of [hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair)s at the base of [claw](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Claw)s of the forefeet and hindfeet.

unicornuate uterus represents a [uterine malformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterine_malformation) where the uterus is formed from only one of the paired [Müllerian duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Müllerian_duct)s while the other Müllerian duct does not develop or only in a rudimentary fashion.

upper [limb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Limb_(anatomy))s or upper extremities are the [forelimb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Forelimb)s of an [upright-postured](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Upright_posture) [tetrapod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetrapod) [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate), extending from the [scapula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scapula)e and [clavicle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clavicle)s down to and including the [digit](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Digit_(anatomy))s, including all the [musculature](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Musculature)s and [ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligament)s involved with the [shoulder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shoulder), [elbow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elbow), [wrist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wrist) and [knuckle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knuckle) joints.

Urediniospores (or uredospores) are thin-walled [spore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Spore)s produced by the [uredium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uredium), a stage in the life-cycle of [rusts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rust_(fungus)).

urogenital hiatus is a large midline opening ==See also== * [Coccyx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Coccyx) (tailbone) * [Pubococcygeus muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pubococcygeus_muscle) * [Pelvic floor dysfunction](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvic_floor_dysfunction) * [Perineology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perineology) * [Perineal hernia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Perineal_hernia) * [Female genital prolapse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female_genital_prolapse) ==References== [[Category:Sexual anatomy]] [[Category:Muscles of the torso]] [[Category:Women's health]] 1cof1depxr0qi3556k1anhn5pgmwtgu
Uropods are posterior [appendage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Appendage)s found on a wide variety of [crustacean](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crustacean)s.

uropygial gland, informally known as the preen gland or the oil gland, is a bilobed [sebaceous gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sebaceous_gland) possessed by the majority of birds used to distribute the gland's oil through the plumage by means of [preening](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Preening_(bird)).

media.file: Blue Jay anting, showing uropygial gland.jpg

definition: Urticating hairs or urticating bristles are one of the primary [defense mechanisms](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Antipredator_adaptation) used by numerous plants, almost all [New World](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_World) [tarantula](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tarantula)s, and various lepidopteran [caterpillar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caterpillar)s.

Uterine artery embolization (UAE, uterine fibroid embolization, or UFE) is a procedure in which an [interventional radiologist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Interventional_radiologist) uses a [catheter](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catheter) to deliver small particles that block the [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) supply to the uterine body.

uterine septum is a congenital [uterine malformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterine_malformation) where the [uterine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterus) cavity is partitioned by a longitudinal [septum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Septum); the outside of the uterus has a normal typical shape.

uterus (from [Latin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latin) uterus, : uteri or uteruses) or womb () is the [organ](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollow_organ) in the [reproductive system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reproductive_system) of most [female](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Female) [mammal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mammal)s, including humans, that accommodates the [embryonic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Embryonic_development) and [fetal development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prenatal_development) of one or more [fertilized eggs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fertilized_egg) until [birth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birth).

Uterus didelphys (; sometimes also uterus ) represents a [uterine malformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterine_malformation) where the [uterus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterus) is present as a paired organ when the embryogenetic fusion of the [Müllerian duct](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Müllerian_duct)s fails to occur.

vacuole () is a [membrane-bound organelle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane-bound_organelle) which is present in [plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_cell) and [fungal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungus) [cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cell_(biology)) and some [protist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Protist), [animal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Animal), and [bacteria](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bacteria)l cells.
vaginal epithelium is the inner lining of the [vagina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vagina) consisting of multiple layers of ([squamous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epithelium)) cells.
Vaginal rugae are structures of the vagina that are transverse ridges formed out of the supporting tissues and [vaginal epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vaginal_epithelium) in females.

media.file: The science and art of midwifery (1891) (14579471209).jpg

definition: vaginal support structures are those [muscle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Muscle)s, [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone)s, [ligament](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ligament)s, [tendon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tendon)s, membranes and fascia, of the [pelvic floor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pelvic_floor) that maintain the position of the [vagina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vagina) within the pelvic cavity and allow the normal functioning of the vagina and other reproductive structures in the female.

vagus nerve, also known as the tenth [cranial nerve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cranial_nerves) (CN X), plays a crucial role in the [autonomic nervous system](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autonomic_nervous_system), which is responsible for regulating involuntary functions within the human body.

Valve interstitial cells (VIC), cardiac valve interstitial cells, or also known as valvular interstitial cells (VICs), are the most prevalent cells in the [heart valve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart_valve) leaflets, which are a type of [mesenchymal stem cells](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mesenchymal_stem_cell) (MSCs) and are responsible for maintaining the [extracellular matrix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Extracellular_matrix) that provides the mechanical properties of the heart valve.
Van der Hoeven's organ is the infrabuccal lamellar organ in the adult male of genus [Nautilus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nautilus).

Van der Vecht's gland or Van der Vecht's organ is a [gland](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gland) which is located in an area of modified [cuticle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cuticle_(insect_anatomy)) on the rearmost gastral [sternite](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sternite) of female wasps.

Van Gieson's stain is a histological [staining](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Staining) technique used to differentiate between [collagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collagen) and other tissue elements in microscopic sections.

media.file: Histopathology of steatohepatitis with established cirrhosis, with thick bands of fibrosis (van Gieson).jpg

definition: variegation is the property of having discrete markings of different colors.

varix (: varices) is an anatomical feature of the [shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod_shell) of certain [sea snail](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_snail)s, [marine](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Marine_(ocean)) [gastropod](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gastropod) [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s.

vasa recta of the kidney, (vasa recta renis) are capillaries of the [kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kidney), – a series of [blood vessel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel)s in the [blood supply of the kidney](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_circulation) that enter the [medulla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Renal_medulla) as the straight arterioles, and leave the medulla to ascend to the cortex as the straight venules.

vascular cambium is the main growth [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)) in the [stem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plant_stem)s and [root](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Root)s of many plants exhibiting [secondary growth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secondary_growth), specifically in [dicot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dicot)s such as [buttercups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Buttercups) and [oak trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oak_trees), [gymnosperm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gymnosperm)s such as [pine trees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pine_trees), as well as in certain other [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant)s.

Vascular tissue is a complex transporting [tissue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tissue_(biology)), formed of more than one cell type, found in [vascular plant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_plant)s.

vascular tumor is a [vascular anomaly](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vascular_anomaly) where a tumor forms from cells that make [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood_vessel) or [lymph vessels](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lymph_vessels); a soft tissue growth that can be either [benign](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Benign_tumor) or [malignant](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Malignant).

Vascularity, in [bodybuilding](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bodybuilding), is the condition of having many highly visible, prominent, and often extensively-ramified [superficial vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Superficial_vein)s.

veil or velum, in mycology, is one of several structures in [fungi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fungi), especially the thin [membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Membrane_(selective_barrier)) that covers the cap and stalk of an immature [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom).
vein of bulb of penis is a tributary of the [internal pudendal vein](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Internal_pudendal_vein).

Vein of Galen aneurysmal malformations (VGAMs) and Vein of Galen aneurysmal dilations (VGADs) are the most frequent [arteriovenous malformation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Arteriovenous_malformation)s in infants and fetuses.

veliger is the [plankton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Plankton)ic [larva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larva) of many kinds of [sea snails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sea_snails) and [freshwater snails](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Freshwater_snails), as well as most [bivalve](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bivalve) [mollusc](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollusc)s (clams) and [tusk shell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tusk_shell)s.

media.file: 9d old veliger larva of the nudibranch Tritonia diomedea.jpg

definition: Vellus hair ( ) is short, thin, light-colored, and barely noticeable [hair](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hair) that develops on most of a human's body during [childhood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Childhood).
venous heart is a type of [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) in which only blood with [carbon dioxide](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Carbon_dioxide) circulates.

ventral body cavity is a [body cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Body_cavity) in the anterior aspect of the [human body](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_body), comprising the [thoracic cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Thoracic_cavity) and [abdominopelvic cavity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Abdominopelvic_cavity).

ventricle is one of two large chambers located toward the bottom of the [heart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Heart) that collect and expel [blood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blood) towards the peripheral beds within the body and lungs.

Ventricose is an adjective describing the condition of a mushroom, gastropod or plant that it is ==Mycology== In [mycology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mycology), ventricose is a condition in which the [cystidia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cystidia), [lamella](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lamella_(mycology)) or [stipe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stipe_(mycology)) of a [mushroom](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mushroom) is swollen in the middle.
ventricular system is a set of four interconnected cavities known as cerebral ventricles in the [brain](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brain).

vermilion border (sometimes spelled vermillion border), also called margin or zone, is the normally sharp demarcation between the [lip](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lip) and the adjacent normal [skin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Skin).

vertebra (: vertebrae) is an [irregular bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Irregular_bone) with a complex structure composed of [bone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bone) and some [hyaline cartilage](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyaline_cartilage), that make up the [vertebral column](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebral_column) or spine, of [vertebrate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vertebrate)s.
vertex refers to the topmost point or summit of the shell.

Vertical dimension of occlusion, or VDO, also known as occlusal vertical dimension (OVD), is a term used in dentistry to indicate the superior-inferior relationship of the [maxilla](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maxilla) and the [mandible](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Human_mandible) when the [teeth](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Teeth) are [occluded](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Occlusion_(dentistry)) in [maximum intercuspation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Maximum_intercuspation).

vesicouterine pouch, also uterovesicle pouch, is a fold of [peritoneum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Peritoneum) over the [uterus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uterus) and the [bladder](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Urinary_bladder).

definition: vitreous base is an area in the [fundus](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fundus_(eye)) of the eye in which the [vitreous membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitreous_membrane), neural retina, and [pigment epithelium](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pigment_epithelium) all are firmly adherent, one to the other.

vitreous membrane (or [hyaloid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hyaloid) membrane or vitreous cortex) is a layer of [collagen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Collagen) separating the [vitreous humour](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vitreous_humour) from the rest of the [eye](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eye).

vocal sac is the flexible [membrane](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Biological_membrane) of skin possessed by most male [frog](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Frog)s and [toad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Toad)s.

vocal tract or speech apparatus is the cavity in mammals and in birds where the sound produced at the sound source ([larynx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Larynx) in mammals; [syrinx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrinx_(biology)) in birds) is filtered.
